headline: Strange beaked 'hell chicken' is the first fruit-eating dinosaur
description: vInfernogallus, meaning hell chicken, is named after its bird-like look and Hell Creek fossil site
author: Reuters
article_text:
While dinosaurs ate a lot of different things, including each other, fruit long seemed to have been absent from their menu. But scientists now have found fossils of ​a turkey-sized and toothless dinosaur possessing a parrot-like head that exhibited multiple adaptations for a specialized fruit diet.

This first-known frugivorous dinosaur, named Infernogallus jamesi, lived about ‌66 million years ago during the Cretaceous Period at the twilight of the age of dinosaurs and displayed traits on its beak and jaws for mashing soft food like fruit. It is known from fossils unearthed in Montana and North Dakota.

The name Infernogallus means "hell chicken," a nod to its bird-like appearance and the fact that its fossils were found in the Hell Creek rock formation, which spans the US states of Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota and ​Wyoming and has yielded the remains of some of the most famous dinosaurs.

It would have eaten fruit and other soft plants in the subtropical coastal floodplain ecosystem it ​shared with the likes of apex predator Tyrannosaurus, three-horned herbivore Triceratops and tank-like armored plant-eater Ankylosaurus.

Infernogallus was about 5 feet (1.5 meters) long and weighed around ⁠25 pounds (11.3 kg). While the fossils — one nearly complete skeleton and isolated bones from a jaw and palate — did not reveal feathers, the researchers believe Infernogallus was covered in them, based on ​fossils of close relatives.

It belonged to a group called theropods that includes T. rex and all the meat-eating dinosaurs, as well as some that took to eating plants and the entire bird ​lineage.

"This definitely expands the range of lifestyles we thought dinosaurs had, and it shows how adaptable theropods were," said paleontologist Greg Funston of Stony Brook University in New York, lead author of the research published in the journal Nature Communications.

Fruits are the reproductive structures of angiosperms, also called flowering plants. Angiosperms first appeared earlier in the Cretaceous, around 130 to 140 million years ago, and subsequently took over landscapes previously dominated by plants called gymnosperms ​like conifers and ginkgoes.

Infernogallus shows that some dinosaurs may have had a close ecological relationship with flowering plants.

"It has been proposed before that some groups of dinosaurs ate fruits, but there was ​never evidence to back it up," said study co-author Thomas Dudgeon, a postdoctoral researcher at the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto.

"The discovery of Infernogallus shows that dinosaur diets were likely far more diverse than we ‌previously thought. Prior ⁠to this discovery, there was a bit of a mystery in dinosaur evolution. The evolution of flowering plants introduced a brand-new food source that undoubtedly had consequences for the animals living alongside them," Dudgeon said.

The fruit available for Infernogallus may have included various berries as well as drupes, a broad category that today includes types with a central pit like peaches and cherries as well as others like mangoes and olives.

Three key features

Infernogallus showed a range of features indicating a frugivorous diet. The three most important, Funston said, were the organization of jaw muscles that powered back-and-forth chewing ​motions, a mobile joint that enabled the jaw ​to slide forward, and a series of ⁠ridges and grooves on the beak to help mash and shear soft plants like fruits.

"We see these features separately in birds and turtles today that eat soft foods, like the fig-eating vulturine parrot or green sea turtles that chew soft sea grass. But no living animal has all ​three adaptations, showing just how specialized Infernogallus was," Funston said.

Infernogallus also shows how adaptable beaks are compared to teeth.

"Once you've lost your teeth ​and developed a beak ⁠instead, the range of foods available dramatically increases, including plants, as long as you have some way to digest them," Funston said.

Most herbivorous theropods used stomach stones called gastroliths to grind food. But Infernogallus and other members of a lineage called caenagnathids chewed their food instead.

Fruit-eating animals play an important role for angiosperms by dispersing seeds.

"Mammals and birds would probably also have eaten fruit, but they didn't show the ⁠same kinds ​of specializations for a frugivorous diet that Infernogallus does, so it might have been a less important resource for ​them. Mammals and birds also were quite small in the Cretaceous, so it's unlikely that they were spreading very large seeds, or that they were spreading them big distances," Funston said.

"We know that these big-seeded fruits were proliferating and spreading, ​and it seems like caenagnathids could have fit this role — although we feel more evidence is needed before drawing that link confidently," Funston said.

headline: Chelsea deepen Manchester United's crisis
description: Carrick faces mounting pressure due to below-par showing of his charges
author: AFP
article_text:
Michael Carrick's stay of execution as Manchester United boss may not last long after his team imploded in a 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea on Saturday.

The visitors wasted a string of chances to take the lead at Stamford Bridge before Morgan Rogers waltzed through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring on 50 minutes.

Lisandro Martinez then ruined any chance of a revival from Carrick's men with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.

Winless in nine games, defeat leaves the 20-time English champions still just one point above the relegation zone and in danger of ending the weekend in the bottom three.

Many expected Carrick to be axed following last weekend's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The former United midfielder was instead given the chance to turn his side's fortunes around and will lament a lack of ruthlessness during the first half.

Carrick recalled captain Bruno Fernandes after he was left out last weekend in the wake of criticising his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.

Fernandes should have marked his return with the opener when he blazed over from Bryan Mbeumo's inviting cross.

The roles were reversed when Mbeumo could not stretch to meet Fernandes's delivery at the back post before twice Amad Diallo was denied by Chelsea's stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders.

United did finally get the ball in the net when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire's header from a corner, but the Brazilian had strayed just offside.

Carrick could not hide his frustration in a half-time interview to broadcasters and his mood soured further with a disastrous start to the second period.

Martinez sent off

Rogers credits Carrick for revitalising his career during a spell together at Middlesbrough but dealt a potentially decisive blow to his former boss.

The England international collected the ball inside the centre circle but was allowed to drive directly towards the United goal before dinking the ball over Senne Lammens.

Martinez also spoke out publicly in recent weeks to criticise United's lack of spending in the transfer market to bolster Carrick's squad.

But on this season's evidence, Martinez is one of those most in need of replacing.

The Argentine international could not cope with Rogers's strength moments later as he was penalised for hauling back the Chelsea forward.

From the resulting free-kick, Martinez then needlessly crashed into Wesley Fofana with a raised forearm.

After a VAR review, referee Peter Banks awarded a penalty and showed Martinez a second yellow card.

Lammens got hands to Palmer's spot-kick but still allowed the ball to trickle into the bottom corner.

On a rare start since Xabi Alonso took charge of the Blues, Estevao had a third goal disallowed for offside when he crashed Palmer's pass into the top corner.

Cries of "sacked in the morning" rained down from the Chelsea fans as their side toyed with United for the final quarter without adding to their lead.

Another big decision awaits the United hierarchy before a massive Champions League clash at home to Roma on Tuesday.

article_html:
LONDON:

Michael Carrick's stay of execution as Manchester United boss may not last long after his team imploded in a 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea on Saturday.

The visitors wasted a string of chances to take the lead at Stamford Bridge before Morgan Rogers waltzed through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring on 50 minutes.

Lisandro Martinez then ruined any chance of a revival from Carrick's men with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.

Winless in nine games, defeat leaves the 20-time English champions still just one point above the relegation zone and in danger of ending the weekend in the bottom three.

Many expected Carrick to be axed following last weekend's 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The former United midfielder was instead given the chance to turn his side's fortunes around and will lament a lack of ruthlessness during the first half.

Carrick recalled captain Bruno Fernandes after he was left out last weekend in the wake of criticising his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.

Fernandes should have marked his return with the opener when he blazed over from Bryan Mbeumo's inviting cross.

The roles were reversed when Mbeumo could not stretch to meet Fernandes's delivery at the back post before twice Amad Diallo was denied by Chelsea's stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders.

United did finally get the ball in the net when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire's header from a corner, but the Brazilian had strayed just offside.

Carrick could not hide his frustration in a half-time interview to broadcasters and his mood soured further with a disastrous start to the second period.

Martinez sent off

Rogers credits Carrick for revitalising his career during a spell together at Middlesbrough but dealt a potentially decisive blow to his former boss.

The England international collected the ball inside the centre circle but was allowed to drive directly towards the United goal before dinking the ball over Senne Lammens.

Martinez also spoke out publicly in recent weeks to criticise United's lack of spending in the transfer market to bolster Carrick's squad.

But on this season's evidence, Martinez is one of those most in need of replacing.

The Argentine international could not cope with Rogers's strength moments later as he was penalised for hauling back the Chelsea forward.

From the resulting free-kick, Martinez then needlessly crashed into Wesley Fofana with a raised forearm.

After a VAR review, referee Peter Banks awarded a penalty and showed Martinez a second yellow card.

Lammens got hands to Palmer's spot-kick but still allowed the ball to trickle into the bottom corner.

On a rare start since Xabi Alonso took charge of the Blues, Estevao had a third goal disallowed for offside when he crashed Palmer's pass into the top corner.

Cries of "sacked in the morning" rained down from the Chelsea fans as their side toyed with United for the final quarter without adding to their lead.

Another big decision awaits the United hierarchy before a massive Champions League clash at home to Roma on Tuesday.

Beaten in two of their three European games so far, United face both the embarrassment and financial shock of an early exit should they fall to another defeat against the Italians at Old Trafford.

headline: Harry Styles dresses as Elvis Presley for Harryween night 1 in New York
description: Styles took to the stage on October 30 in the King of Rock and Roll’s signature white jumpsuit
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Harry Styles kicked off the first night of his Halloween-themed Harryween concerts at Madison Square Garden in New York by dressing as Elvis Presley, as the singer approaches the end of his 30-show residency at the iconic venue.

The 32-year-old singer took to the stage on October 30 in the King of Rock and Roll’s signature white jumpsuit, complete with a satin-lined cape and gold sunglasses.

Styles was joined by his fiancée, Zoë Kravitz, who attended the concert dressed as a devil in a red outfit and horns. Elvis’ granddaughter, actress Riley Keough, was also spotted in the audience, filming the performance alongside Kravitz.

The Halloween show featured another surprise when Styles recreated the outfit he wore during his 2010 X Factor audition, when he was just 16 years old.

The singer donned a grey cardigan over a white T-shirt, brown trousers and a yellow scarf, completing the look with his original audition number.

He also performed Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely”, the song he sang during his audition, and repeated the famous line “I work in a bakery”, recalling the conversation he had with the judges about his part-time job as a teenager.

Styles’ audition ultimately led to his formation in One Direction alongside Niall Horan, Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson and Liam Payne. The group went on to become one of the world’s biggest boybands before going on hiatus in 2016.

The singer’s band and dancers also embraced the Halloween spirit, dressing as different versions of Styles from throughout his career.

Harryween is a Halloween-themed concert tradition in which Styles and his band dress up for performances, while fans are encouraged to attend in fancy dress.

The singer previously held two Harryween shows at Madison Square Garden in 2021, dressing as Dorothy from The Wizard of Oz on the first night and a Pierrot clown on the second.

In 2022, he brought the tradition to Los Angeles, dressing as Danny Zuko from Grease.

The Halloween concerts mark the final two nights of Styles’ 30-show Madison Square Garden residency, which forms part of his Together, Together world tour.

headline: Atletico beat Levante to top LaLiga
description: Grimaldo and Simeone are on target for Diego Simeone’s side
author: AFP
article_text:
Atletico Madrid earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante on Saturday to move provisionally top of La Liga before Barcelona host Alaves later on.

Diego Simeone's side climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants, who suffered their first league defeat against rivals Real Madrid last weekend.

Goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone in Valencia helped Atletico record a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.

"I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar.

"We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game."

There was a minute's silence at the start of the match in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week.

Levante's Dani Requena forced Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak into an impressive early save.

Morten Hjulmand thought he had put Atletico ahead after Alex Baena slipped him in, but a VAR review showed the Dane was offside.

Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, was involved in the opener.

The Spaniard's pass was poorly defended by Levante and the ball bobbled through to Grimaldo, who lashed high into the net at the near post.

Lee Kang-in hit the crossbar early in the second half as Atletico looked to put the game to bed.

The coach's son Giuliano prodded home for Atletico's second goal after being played in by World Cup winner Baena.

Oblak saved superbly from Karl Etta Eyong to stop the hosts fighting their way back into the game.

It was Simeone's 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones.

"I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011.

Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga.

On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures.

article_html:
MADRID:

Atletico Madrid earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante on Saturday to move provisionally top of La Liga before Barcelona host Alaves later on.

Diego Simeone's side climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants, who suffered their first league defeat against rivals Real Madrid last weekend.

Goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone in Valencia helped Atletico record a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.

"I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar.

"We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game."

There was a minute's silence at the start of the match in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week.

Levante's Dani Requena forced Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak into an impressive early save.

Morten Hjulmand thought he had put Atletico ahead after Alex Baena slipped him in, but a VAR review showed the Dane was offside.

Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, was involved in the opener.

The Spaniard's pass was poorly defended by Levante and the ball bobbled through to Grimaldo, who lashed high into the net at the near post.

Lee Kang-in hit the crossbar early in the second half as Atletico looked to put the game to bed.

The coach's son Giuliano prodded home for Atletico's second goal after being played in by World Cup winner Baena.

Oblak saved superbly from Karl Etta Eyong to stop the hosts fighting their way back into the game.

It was Simeone's 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones.

"I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011.

Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga.

On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures.

headline: Michael Douglas admits he initially didn’t think Glenn Close was right for ‘Fatal Attraction’
description: “I fought against it and was very cross as I didn’t see her as a psychopath, he said
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Michael Douglas has revealed that he and the filmmakers behind Fatal Attraction initially did not believe Glenn Close was the right actress to play Alex Forrest in the 1987 psychological thriller.

The actors reunited on The Graham Norton Show on October 30, where they looked back on the making of the iconic film and recalled how Close eventually won the role despite the initial doubts surrounding her casting.

Douglas, 82, explained that the production team had initially moved on from considering Close for the part, despite the actress already having received three Academy Award nominations.

“Everybody thought that Glenn was not right for the part, and so we moved on,” Douglas recalled.

However, Close's agent insisted that the actress wanted to audition for the role. Douglas said the team initially felt they could not ask someone with her established career to audition, but Close was determined to prove herself.

“She came in, and I ask anyone to see this tape, and she blew us away. We have never been so wrong in our lives,” he said.

Douglas added that the filmmakers were left feeling like “total idiots” after watching her audition, describing Close as being “in total command”.

Close ultimately played Alex Forrest opposite Douglas's Dan Gallagher, a married man whose affair with Alex spirals into a dangerous obsession. Her performance earned her an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

The pair also discussed the film's controversial ending, which was changed following test screenings.

Close revealed that the original version ended with Alex slitting her throat, leaving Dan to be arrested for her death. However, American test audiences disliked the ending and wanted Alex to die.

“It really was very film noir,” Close said, explaining that audiences were angry and wanted her character dead.

The actress said she was asked to reshoot the ending six months later, but initially opposed the decision because she did not see Alex as a psychopath.

“I fought against it and was very cross as I didn’t see her as a psychopath. But they wore me down and Alex became the most hated woman in America,” she recalled.

The theatrical version ultimately featured Anne Archer's character, Beth, shooting Alex after she attacks her family.

The reunion comes as Douglas promotes his memoir, One Helluva Ride, while Close prepares for the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, in which she plays Drusilla. The actress is also set to receive an honorary Academy Award at the Governors Awards on November 15.

headline: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal could be near ahead of December’s G20 summit
description: Trump says Russia-Ukraine peace deal is close, expressing hope for a breakthrough in negotiations
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
US President Donald Trump has expressed optimism about reaching a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, saying a deal could be close ahead of the December G20 summit at his Trump National Doral resort in Florida.

Speaking in an interview with conservative commentator Benny Johnson released on Saturday, Trump said there was a “real good chance” of resolving the conflict, pointing to the possibility of an agreement between the two leaders.

“I think we’re getting very close to making a deal there,” Trump said, acknowledging the deep hostility between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Asked about reports of a possible Russia-Ukraine agreement at the G20, Trump did not rule out the prospect, expressing confidence that negotiations could produce a breakthrough.

“I think there’s a real good chance we’re going to have that one worked out. Also, we’re working out a lot of deals,” he said.

He also addressed Iran, saying the US was determined to prevent the country from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump claimed Iranian military capabilities had been severely weakened, adding that Washington would “finish that off”.

Turning to Cuba, Trump predicted that the country’s communist leadership would not remain in power much longer, suggesting Washington could turn its attention to the island after Venezuela.

“It’s a failed country. We’re going to get people back there very soon,” he said, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was monitoring the situation closely.

Iranian strikes on more than two dozen United States military bases and other sites in the Middle East have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage, with attacks initially targeting early-warning systems before expanding to aircraft, warehouses and troop accommodation, an Associated Press report revealed.

The AP independently verified damage to American targets through satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed on the attacks or had firsthand knowledge of the damage. The analysis found that, through August, more than 115 drone and missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iran-backed groups had damaged or destroyed structures at 26 military bases and other sites housing US equipment.

According to the report, Iran initially focused on aircraft hangars and systems designed to detect incoming strikes, before broadening its targets to warehouses, troop accommodation and other facilities. The attacks, the analysis said, were aimed at weakening the systems that helped protect US bases and enabled them to function.

The attacks have significantly altered the American military presence in the region, with the US moving many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf, two regional officials told the AP. These included aircraft, air defence and communications systems, as well as other equipment crucial to base operations, the report said.

The report said the damage raised questions about the effectiveness of American defences in the region as President Donald Trump considered fresh strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections and Tehran vowed major retaliation. It warned that a resumption of hostilities could cause further costly damage to military bases, deepening uncertainty over whether Washington would rebuild its installations and replace equipment in the region after the war.

The analysis found that Iranian strikes had damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at US bases between April 1 and June 30. The report said its findings offered a broader picture of the destruction than previously released independent assessments, including those by the Pentagon's inspector general.

The Trump administration and US military have disclosed few details about the conflict's toll on personnel and equipment. Delays in releasing satellite imagery have also hampered independent assessments, the report further said.

US Central Command declined to comment on the damage, citing operational security. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell, however, said US forces and bases were well protected and the military was stronger than ever.

“Our service members in CENTCOM have everything they need to continue their historic success ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon,” he said in a statement.

Kuwait bears brunt of attacks

Most Iranian attacks have targeted Kuwait, although US installations in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have also been hit, the AP analysis of satellite imagery showed.

The deadliest known strike on US troops during the war took place in Kuwait, where six soldiers were killed in a drone attack at Port Shuaiba on March 1.

Ali Al Salem Air Base was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying 15 aircraft hangars, several warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.

Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, suffered extensive damage. Most of its hangars were rendered inoperable, while its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops was hit in late July. A separate strike severely damaged the garage and dining room, two regional officials told the AP.

The officials and two other regional military officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive details about the damage.

Although the strikes inflicted far greater damage on Iran, American equipment losses were inevitable, said Raphael Cohen, director of the National Security Programme at the RAND School of Public Policy.

Modern warfare had made militaries “susceptible to large-scale, cheap drone attacks”, he said.

“This should be a wake-up call for the United States,” Cohen added.

Early-warning systems among first targets

Iran began its retaliation by striking systems designed to detect incoming attacks before expanding its targets to buildings and equipment that kept US bases operational, the report said.

Within the first two days of the war in late February, Iran destroyed protective enclosures housing US radar systems at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and Naval Support Activity Bahrain. It also struck portable radars at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.

Iran prioritised key early-warning radars that form the backbone of the US air defence system and are difficult and expensive to replace, said N.R. Jenzen-Jones, director of Armament Research Services.

A radar in Jordan was reportedly destroyed. It was one of only 13 such systems possessed by the US Army worldwide, with each costing about half a billion dollars, according to the AP report.

Another radar in Qatar was significantly damaged, although it remains unclear whether it was destroyed. The system was purchased under a 2013 deal worth $1.1 billion and appeared to be the only one of its kind in the region.

The attacks were likely “intended to disrupt and degrade the U.S. and allies’ ability to respond to further strikes”, Jenzen-Jones said.

After hitting the radar, Iran carried out more than 50 successful strikes on 18 locations housing US military equipment during the first month of the war, prioritising sites with aircraft.

The attacks damaged refuelling aircraft, communications systems, fuel bunkers and troop accommodation, two regional officials said. A strike on Prince Sultan Air Base damaged the rear half of a Boeing E-3 Sentry surveillance aircraft, while another hit a CIA unit at the US Embassy in Riyadh.

A regional military official who recently visited the Saudi air base described damaged equipment, debris and bombed-out barracks and dining halls. He said the attack on the surveillance plane also damaged several other aircraft, including two aerial refuelling tankers.

A Congressional Research Service report updated in October said 15 US aircraft had been damaged at bases across the region.

Al Dhafra Air Base, south of Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates, was also frequently targeted early in the war. A regional military official said aircraft hangars, other installations, an early-warning radar system and surveillance drones had been damaged.

Satellite imagery delays hamper assessment

Major satellite imagery providers with US contracts blocked or delayed the public release of images at the request of American officials, sometimes citing national security concerns, the report revealed. This limited independent verification until imagery became available from OneAtlas, a satellite provider owned by Airbus.

At Camp Buehring, high-quality imagery from reliable providers was unavailable until late August. More than 30 structures were damaged or destroyed between the suspension of imagery in early March and its return in August. The report said it confirmed repeated strikes on the base in March, April, May and July.

With neither side outlining a clear end to the conflict, further damage remains possible if hostilities resume, the report said.

The conflict could signal a new operating environment for US forces, Cohen said, warning that military installations and equipment were increasingly vulnerable to relatively inexpensive drone attacks.

“This is the operating environment that we’re going to face in the future,” he said.

“The idea that we can rely on fixed infrastructure in the way that we have during the global war on terrorism is over.”

According to the report, Iran initially focused on aircraft hangars and systems designed to detect incoming strikes, before broadening its targets to warehouses, troop accommodation and other facilities. The attacks, the analysis said, were aimed at weakening the systems that helped protect US bases and enabled them to function.

The attacks have significantly altered the American military presence in the region, with the US moving many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf, two regional officials told the AP. These included aircraft, air defence and communications systems, as well as other equipment crucial to base operations, the report said.

The report said the damage raised questions about the effectiveness of American defences in the region as President Donald Trump considered fresh strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections and Tehran vowed major retaliation. It warned that a resumption of hostilities could cause further costly damage to military bases, deepening uncertainty over whether Washington would rebuild its installations and replace equipment in the region after the war.

The analysis found that Iranian strikes had damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at US bases between April 1 and June 30. The report said its findings offered a broader picture of the destruction than previously released independent assessments, including those by the Pentagon's inspector general.

The Trump administration and US military have disclosed few details about the conflict's toll on personnel and equipment. Delays in releasing satellite imagery have also hampered independent assessments, the report further said.

US Central Command declined to comment on the damage, citing operational security. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell, however, said US forces and bases were well protected and the military was stronger than ever.

The officials and two other regional military officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive details about the damage.

Modern warfare had made militaries “susceptible to large-scale, cheap drone attacks”, he said.

headline: Zendaya recreates Halle Berry’s iconic 2000s look for Halloween 2026
description: The Halloween tribute follows Zendaya’s recent transformation, which saw her debut a short pixie haircut at the Emmy's
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Zendaya has paid tribute to Halle Berry’s iconic fashion moment from 2000, recreating the actress’s vintage Lanvin outfit for Halloween with the help of her longtime stylist Law Roach.

Roach shared photographs of the Dune star’s Halloween look on Instagram on October 31, showing Zendaya wearing the same yellow, brown and white printed string bikini top and matching low-rise trousers Berry wore to the New York premiere of X-Men in July 2000.

The archival Lanvin ensemble featured a geometric print, a triangle bikini top with delicate straps and wide-leg trousers. Zendaya completed the look with pointed-toe heels and tinted sunglasses, closely matching Berry’s original styling.

View this post on Instagram

Berry had accessorised the outfit with a belly chain and yellow-tinted sunglasses, while Zendaya added her own touches to the vintage recreation.

The Halloween tribute follows Zendaya’s recent transformation, which saw her debut a short pixie haircut at the 2026 Emmy Awards in September. The hairstyle drew comparisons to Berry’s signature cropped looks, with Roach confirming that the actress had been inspired by the X-Men star.

Berry also acknowledged the tribute, sharing Roach’s interview on her Instagram Story and praising Zendaya’s appearance.

The two actresses have previously been connected through fashion, with Zendaya paying tribute to other iconic stars over the years. In 2024, she wore a vintage Bob Mackie design inspired by Cher at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony.

Zendaya’s Halloween look also comes as she begins the promotional tour for Dune: Part Three, which is scheduled to arrive in cinemas in December 2026.

headline: Mckenna Grace says filming 'Sunrise on the Reaping’ took a toll so she reached out to Josh Hutcherson
description: “I was like, ‘This is crazy.’ And he was like, ‘Yeah yeah, no, they’re all like that. It’s definitely hard,’” she said
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Mckenna Grace has revealed that filming The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping was so physically and emotionally demanding that she reached out to former co-star Josh Hutcherson to ask about his own experience making the franchise.

The actress, 20, stars as twins Maysilee and Merrilee Donner in the upcoming prequel, with Maysilee selected as a tribute in the 50th Hunger Games alongside a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada.

Speaking to PEOPLE, Grace explained that her body struggled to distinguish between the fictional trauma her character endured in the arena and the reality of filming the scenes.

“Eventually after I booked the film and I was shooting, I reached out to him and we spoke and I was like, ‘Were your games, did it feel as physically taxing and emotionally?’” she said.

Grace, who previously worked with Hutcherson in Five Nights at Freddy’s 2, recalled being surprised by how difficult the filming process had been.

“I was like, ‘This is crazy.’ And he was like, ‘Yeah. Yeah, no, they’re all like that. It’s definitely hard,’” she said.

Hutcherson, 34, played Peeta Mellark opposite Jennifer Lawrence’s Katniss Everdeen in the original four Hunger Games films, released between 2012 and 2015.

Grace explained that she was not necessarily looking for advice from Hutcherson, but wanted to hear stories about his time on the films as a longtime fan of the franchise.

“I wanted to know what their games were like and also what Jen and Josh were like at our age, and the fun that they had on those movies and what it was like working in the water on Catching Fire,” she said.

Hutcherson shared memories of the intense filming conditions, including early call times and freezing water during the second film, in which Katniss and Peeta return to the arena for the 75th Hunger Games.

“He was like, ‘That stuff was intense and brutal, and you’d get up so early and be in this freezing water,’” Grace recalled.

The actress added that hearing those stories was a highlight of her experience, although she admitted that focusing on anecdotes rather than advice might not have been the most helpful approach.

Grace’s role in Sunrise on the Reaping marks her entry into the Hunger Games universe, with the film also featuring Ralph Fiennes, Kieran Culkin, Glenn Close and Elle Fanning.

Lawrence and Hutcherson are also set to reprise their roles as Katniss and Peeta in brief appearances in the prequel.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on November 20, 2026.

headline: Absence of department heads complicates PAC meetings
description: Punjab Assembly PAC members express concern over senior officials' absence from committee meetings
author: Muhammad Ilyas
article_text:
A summons from the Public Accounts Committee is meant to bring those responsible for public spending to the table. But when senior bureaucrats are called to explain billions of rupees in audit objections, it is often their subordinates who turn up instead. The practice has raised an uncomfortable question for Punjab’s parliamentary watchdog: can accountability be enforced when those expected to answer are missing from the room?

Senior government officials are increasingly failing to attend meetings of the Punjab Assembly's Public Accounts Committee (PAC), sending junior officers in their place despite being summoned to respond to audit objections. The practice has prompted concern among committee members over the level of senior officials' participation in the parliamentary oversight process.

Instead of department secretaries and other responsible senior officials, Additional Secretaries, Deputy Secretaries and Section Officers are frequently attending meetings to represent their respective departments. The issue has raised questions about whether subordinate officers have the authority and relevant information to provide satisfactory answers to audit objections involving public funds.

Public Accounts Committee Chairman Iftikhar Chachar has also taken notice of the matter, maintaining that an officer specifically summoned for the examination of audit objections is required to attend the meeting. Officials who fail to appear may face reprimands from the committee.

Chachar said the situation had started improving since he began questioning officials about their absence and taking notice of the practice. Departments are now expected to inform the committee before a meeting if a summoned officer is outside the country or city.

Such officials are also required to provide evidence explaining their absence and inform the committee which officer will attend in their place to respond to members' questions.

The committee has expressed concern over the repeated appearance of subordinate officers in place of department heads and senior officials. While Additional Secretaries, Deputy Secretaries and Section Officers may represent their departments, their presence can create difficulties when matters require authoritative explanations, final decisions or access to complete departmental records.

The Public Accounts Committee is an important parliamentary forum responsible for examining government expenditure, audit objections and financial irregularities. The participation of senior departmental officials is considered essential for providing accurate responses, explaining financial discrepancies and ensuring timely decisions on audit matters.

The Punjab Assembly is currently examining audit objections relating to the financial year 2023-24, involving amounts reportedly running into billions of rupees. Officials from various government departments are being summoned to explain the objections and clarify discrepancies identified during the audit process.

The absence of senior officials can delay the examination and settlement of audit objections, particularly when junior officers lack the authority to make decisions or provide final explanations on behalf of their departments.

The committee chairman's emphasis on the personal attendance of summoned officers and the requirement to justify their absence reflects the importance being attached to departmental accountability.

Ensuring the participation of department secretaries and other responsible senior officials in PAC meetings remains important for strengthening parliamentary oversight, improving the resolution of audit objections and ensuring accountability for public expenditure.

headline: ‘IT: Welcome to Derry’ drops surprise Halloween special on HBO Max
description: 'IT: Welcome to Derry – A Story of Derry', the 30-minute instalment arrived on the streaming platform on October 31
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
HBO Max has surprised IT: Welcome to Derry fans with a new special episode, released on Halloween as viewers await the horror series’ second season.

Titled IT: Welcome to Derry – A Story of Derry, the 30-minute instalment arrived on the streaming platform on October 31, taking audiences hundreds of years before the events of the first season.

The special follows three Indigenous youngsters who venture into the Western Wood, where they encounter a terrifying ancient spirit. Its story explores the origins of the supernatural evil that would eventually become associated with Pennywise, the shape-shifting entity played by Bill Skarsgård.

The episode features Kiawentiio, Brandon Oakes, Isabel Deroy-Olson, Michael Podemski-Bedard, Morningstar Angeline, Jennifer Podemski, Brenda Odjick, Jennifer Guerrero, Zahn McClarnon and Eric Trask.

Cherie Dimaline and Jasmyne Flournoy wrote the special, while Tazbah Chavez directed it.

The surprise release comes after IT: Welcome to Derry was renewed for a second season in August. The upcoming season will move the story back to 1935, during the Great Depression, and centre on the massacre of the Bradley Gang, a group of bank robbers who stop in Derry to buy ammunition before encountering unimaginable horror.

The series serves as a prequel to the IT films, which were released in 2017 and 2019 and adapted from Stephen King’s 1986 novel.

The first season, set in 1962, followed residents of Derry as they faced the town’s recurring horrors and the return of Pennywise.

The new special offers fans another glimpse into the town’s dark history while they wait for the second season, which has yet to receive a release date.

IT: Welcome to Derry – A Story of Derry is now streaming on HBO Max.

headline: Gen Z protests reach Germany as thousands join Halloween rallies
description: German protests draw up to 18,000, half the 36,000 estimated by organisers
author: Reuters
article_text:
Tens of thousands of people across Germany joined demonstrations on Saturday, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe ‌took to the streets to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country's long-time leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests organised by the campaign group "Gen Z regelt" — "Gen Z takes charge" in German — ​are planned in 34 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in ​education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.

Official numbers on Saturday afternoon suggested participant turnout was below the ⁠182,000 organisers initially expected. Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, half the roughly 36,000 on the organisers' website.

German authorities said Saturday's ​demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, had been largely peaceful so far, but warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

In Hamburg, some barricades ​were set on fire.

"We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion," Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday.

"What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of ​the burden."

Parts of Germany's far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to mobilise support, according to the federal ​interior ministry.

Luxury shops board up windows

"We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers," said Roman ‌Poseck, interior ⁠minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany's financial hub, Frankfurt.

"France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

Some businesses across German cities boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations due to concerns over possible unrest, including along Berlin's luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.

For organisers, the focus is on what they see as the growing pressure on younger generations in Europe's largest economy.

"The government has offered no response to our ​concerns other than to continue making cuts ​and piling further burdens upon ⁠us," said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

"We will continue to exercise our fundamental right to assemble until you stop ignoring us."

The protests come as Germany struggles to revive economic ​growth and faces growing pressure on pensions and public services as baby boomers retire and the working-age population ​shrinks.

But questions have been ⁠raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany's national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

Sean Baker, a student at the Technical ⁠University of ​Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention to the poor ​state of buildings on campus.

"When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building," he told Reuters. "Yet this is where we're expected to study on a regular basis."

article_html:
Tens of thousands of people across Germany joined demonstrations on Saturday, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe ‌took to the streets to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country's long-time leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests organised by the campaign group "Gen Z regelt" — "Gen Z takes charge" in German — ​are planned in 34 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in ​education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.

Official numbers on Saturday afternoon suggested participant turnout was below the ⁠182,000 organisers initially expected. Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, half the roughly 36,000 on the organisers' website.

German authorities said Saturday's ​demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, had been largely peaceful so far, but warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

In Hamburg, some barricades ​were set on fire.

"We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion," Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday.

"What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of ​the burden."

Parts of Germany's far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to mobilise support, according to the federal ​interior ministry.

Luxury shops board up windows

"We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers," said Roman ‌Poseck, interior ⁠minister for the state of Hesse, whose capital is Germany's financial hub, Frankfurt.

Read More: France braces for fresh unrest, government vows tough response

"France must not be held up as a model in this regard."

Some businesses across German cities boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations due to concerns over possible unrest, including along Berlin's luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.

For organisers, the focus is on what they see as the growing pressure on younger generations in Europe's largest economy.

"The government has offered no response to our ​concerns other than to continue making cuts ​and piling further burdens upon ⁠us," said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

"We will continue to exercise our fundamental right to assemble until you stop ignoring us."

The protests come as Germany struggles to revive economic ​growth and faces growing pressure on pensions and public services as baby boomers retire and the working-age population ​shrinks.

But questions have been ⁠raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany's national school student umbrella organisation, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on November 20.

Sean Baker, a student at the Technical ⁠University of ​Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention to the poor ​state of buildings on campus.

"When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building," he told Reuters. "Yet this is where we're expected to study on a regular basis."

headline: ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Clayface’ battle for Box Office no 1 on Halloween weekend
description: The documentary is estimated to earn $10.6m, narrowly ahead of 'Clayface', which is projected to earn $10.2m
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
A24’s You Can See Everything and DC Studios’ Clayface are in a close race for the top spot at the North American box office as the Halloween weekend continues.

The Elizabeth Holmes documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is estimated to earn $10.6 million in its third weekend, narrowly ahead of Clayface, which is projected to bring in $10.2 million.

The figures put You Can See Everything in the No. 1 position for the first time since its release, after it spent its first two weekends in second place.

The documentary is expected to reach approximately $63 million domestically, following a $19.5 million second weekend after expanding to more than 2,600 cinemas.

Its continued success has made it one of the highest-grossing documentaries ever, with audiences drawn to its unusual approach to the story of Holmes, the disgraced Theranos founder who was convicted of defrauding investors.

The film’s performance has also fuelled speculation about its awards-season prospects, with the possibility of becoming the first documentary to receive an Academy Award nomination for Best Picture.

Meanwhile, Clayface, the R-rated DC body horror film starring Tom Rhys Harries, is expected to earn $10.2 million in its second weekend, representing a 57% decline from its opening.

The film has reached an estimated domestic total of $44 million over 10 days, with its reported production budget of $40 million putting it on course for a modest theatrical success.

Directed by James Watkins, Clayface follows an aspiring actor whose life takes a horrifying turn after a medical procedure goes wrong. The film opened to $24 million domestically last weekend and a further $19 million internationally.

Elsewhere at the box office, Laika’s animated fantasy Wildwood is projected to take third place with $6.8 million in its second weekend, bringing its 10-day domestic total to approximately $25 million.

Black Bear’s Wicker, starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård, is expected to earn $4.1 million in its second weekend, taking its domestic total to $13.2 million.

Paramount’s Street Fighter rounds out the top five with an estimated $3.5 million, bringing its domestic total to $53 million.

The close contest between You Can See Everything and Clayface comes as studios and exhibitors navigate a busy Halloween weekend, with the box office continuing to be shaped by the success of both mainstream releases and unexpected breakout films.

headline: Pakistan rebukes Afghan Taliban's 'deeply misguided approach' to resolving bilateral tensions
description: Warns it will take all necessary measures under international law to eliminate threats to national security.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan on Saturday rejected the Afghan Taliban spokesperson's latest remarks about resolving bilateral issues, describing them as reflective of a “deeply misguided approach” towards the deteriorating relations between the two countries, and said terrorism emanating from Afghan soil remained a major obstacle to normal ties.

The response came after Afghan Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid accused Islamabad of lacking the readiness to resolve tensions with Kabul through dialogue, saying efforts to ease the dispute had so far failed.

In a statement posted on its official X account, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said Mujahid’s latest remarks exposed the Taliban leadership’s unwillingness to confront the main issue straining bilateral ties — its failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil.

“The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” the statement said.

It added that Pakistan’s position was unequivocal, stressing that “terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable”.

The statement said Pakistan would not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that threatened its security or allow its people to remain targets of attacks originating from Afghanistan, adding that Islamabad reserved the right to take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to eliminate threats to its national security, wherever they originated.

“Kabul must recognise that the responsibility for addressing these threats rests squarely with the Afghan Taliban regime,” it said, warning that Pakistan’s resolve to protect its people must never be mistaken for weakness.

The ministry said the Taliban regime’s continued refusal to address terrorism remained the principal obstacle to normal relations, adding that shifting blame, making assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies would neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities.

“Pakistan’s security will not be held hostage to Afghan Taliban’s inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities,” the statement said.

The statement came after Mujahid told Radio Azadi that Afghanistan had made its final efforts through talks to ease tensions with Pakistan, but these had so far produced no results.

He confirmed that messages had been exchanged between Kabul and Islamabad, adding that efforts by mediating countries and Afghan Taliban officials had also failed to reduce tensions.

A day earlier, Pakistan had urged the Afghan Taliban authorities to take “decisive action” against terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory, questioned their “complicity and support” for groups including the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and reaffirmed its right to self-defence.

Addressing an interactive dialogue with the UN special rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan in the General Assembly’s Third Committee, Counsellor Muhammad Jawad Ajmal of Pakistan’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations expressed concern over the presence and activities of several militant groups in Afghanistan.

These included the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army, the Majeed Brigade, the Islamic State in Khorasan Province and the East Turkestan Islamic Movement, along with their affiliates operating from Afghan territory.

Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been strained due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the TTP, from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.

Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.

Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.

In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.

Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.

UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.

Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.

Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.

The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.

Pakistan on Saturday rejected the Afghan Taliban spokesperson's latest remarks about resolving bilateral issues, describing them as reflective of a “deeply misguided approach” towards the deteriorating relations between the two countries, and said terrorism emanating from Afghan soil remained a major obstacle to normal ties.

The response came after Afghan Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid accused Islamabad of lacking the readiness to resolve tensions with Kabul through dialogue, saying efforts to ease the dispute had so far failed.

31 October 2026

The Afghan Taliban spokesperson’s latest tweet exposes the regime’s deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan. The Taliban leadership continues to blame… pic.twitter.com/gNnBnoAJfI

— Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (@MoIB_Official) October 31, 2026

In a statement posted on its official X account, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said Mujahid’s latest remarks exposed the Taliban leadership’s unwillingness to confront the main issue straining bilateral ties — its failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil.

“The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” the statement said.

It added that Pakistan’s position was unequivocal, stressing that “terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable”.

The statement said Pakistan would not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that threatened its security or allow its people to remain targets of attacks originating from Afghanistan, adding that Islamabad reserved the right to take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to eliminate threats to its national security, wherever they originated.

“Kabul must recognise that the responsibility for addressing these threats rests squarely with the Afghan Taliban regime,” it said, warning that Pakistan’s resolve to protect its people must never be mistaken for weakness.

Read: Pakistan urges Afghan Taliban to take 'decisive action' against terrorist groups

The ministry said the Taliban regime’s continued refusal to address terrorism remained the principal obstacle to normal relations, adding that shifting blame, making assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies would neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities.

“Pakistan’s security will not be held hostage to Afghan Taliban’s inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities,” the statement said.

The statement came after Mujahid told Radio Azadi that Afghanistan had made its final efforts through talks to ease tensions with Pakistan, but these had so far produced no results.

He confirmed that messages had been exchanged between Kabul and Islamabad, adding that efforts by mediating countries and Afghan Taliban officials had also failed to reduce tensions.

A day earlier, Pakistan had urged the Afghan Taliban authorities to take “decisive action” against terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory, questioned their “complicity and support” for groups including the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and reaffirmed its right to self-defence.

Addressing an interactive dialogue with the UN special rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan in the General Assembly’s Third Committee, Counsellor Muhammad Jawad Ajmal of Pakistan’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations expressed concern over the presence and activities of several militant groups in Afghanistan.

These included the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army, the Majeed Brigade, the Islamic State in Khorasan Province and the East Turkestan Islamic Movement, along with their affiliates operating from Afghan territory.

Read More: Info ministry calls out Afghan Taliban for deflecting attention from terrorist sanctuaries

Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been strained due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the TTP, from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.

Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.

Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.

In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.

Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.

UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.

Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.

headline: PHC seeks replies from governor, speaker against governor’s rule
description: PTI challenges emergency, governor’s rule in K-P; court orders release of 23 more PTI workers arrested under MPO
author: Yasir Ali
article_text:
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General’s Office has issued notices to the governor and other relevant authorities, including the provincial assembly speaker, seeking detailed replies and comments on separate writ petitions challenging the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in parts of the province.

The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor’s rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.

The petitioners argued that the situation in K-P was not beyond the control of the provincial government to warrant such extraordinary measures. They maintained that the federal government had exceeded its constitutional authority by imposing emergency and governor’s rule, effectively depriving an elected provincial government and its representatives of their powers.

The petitions further stated that governor’s rule could only be imposed in exceptional circumstances when the situation in a province deteriorated beyond control, with the provincial government itself expected to recommend such action.

They also challenged the invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces, arguing that the deployment of troops in aid of civil administration fell within the provincial government’s domain. The petitioners alleged that several constitutional requirements had been disregarded while taking these decisions.

Meanwhile, the Advocate General’s Office has directed the governor, chief secretary, provincial assembly speaker and secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department to submit their respective reports and comments before the court through officers of Grade 17 or above by November 7.

However, questions have been raised over how the provincial assembly speaker would submit his response, as the provincial government maintains that he is currently in protective custody. The Advocate General’s Office has also been informed of the situation.

The high court will take up the petitions for further hearing on November 10.

PHC orders release of 23 more PTI workers

In another case, the high court has granted interim relief to 23 more PTI workers arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, ordering their release on bail.

A bench comprising Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah heard writ petitions challenging the detention of 23 individuals, including Akbar Sher, Shehzad, Razaullah, Saqib, Ehsanullah and Momin Khan.

The petitioners were represented by lawyers Yasir Khattak and Azhar Rahim Khan, while K-P Advocate General Sanaullah and the relevant officials also appeared before the court.

According to the court order, the deputy commissioner of Mardan had been issued a notice at the previous hearing, directing him to explain the reasons and circumstances under which the petitioners were detained and sent to jail.

However, the concerned authorities have yet to submit their report despite the court’s directions.

The bench observed that, in the absence of the required report, it had no option but to examine the available record and provide relief to the petitioners. It noted that similar relief had previously been granted in cases involving comparable circumstances.

Consequently, the court ordered the release of each petitioner against two surety bonds worth Rs100,000.

The bench clarified that the petitions would continue to be heard on merit and that the interim relief did not amount to a final decision on the legality of the detentions.

The deputy commissioner of Mardan was once again directed to submit the relevant report and record before the court.

The hearing was adjourned until November 12.

article_html:
PESHAWER:

The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General’s Office has issued notices to the governor and other relevant authorities, including the provincial assembly speaker, seeking detailed replies and comments on separate writ petitions challenging the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in parts of the province.

The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor’s rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.

The petitioners argued that the situation in K-P was not beyond the control of the provincial government to warrant such extraordinary measures. They maintained that the federal government had exceeded its constitutional authority by imposing emergency and governor’s rule, effectively depriving an elected provincial government and its representatives of their powers.

Read: K-P governor's rule to end in six months, emergency to continue until peace restored: Tariq Fazal

The petitions further stated that governor’s rule could only be imposed in exceptional circumstances when the situation in a province deteriorated beyond control, with the provincial government itself expected to recommend such action.

They also challenged the invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces, arguing that the deployment of troops in aid of civil administration fell within the provincial government’s domain. The petitioners alleged that several constitutional requirements had been disregarded while taking these decisions.

Meanwhile, the Advocate General’s Office has directed the governor, chief secretary, provincial assembly speaker and secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department to submit their respective reports and comments before the court through officers of Grade 17 or above by November 7.

However, questions have been raised over how the provincial assembly speaker would submit his response, as the provincial government maintains that he is currently in protective custody. The Advocate General’s Office has also been informed of the situation.

The high court will take up the petitions for further hearing on November 10.

PHC orders release of 23 more PTI workers

In another case, the high court has granted interim relief to 23 more PTI workers arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, ordering their release on bail.

A bench comprising Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah heard writ petitions challenging the detention of 23 individuals, including Akbar Sher, Shehzad, Razaullah, Saqib, Ehsanullah and Momin Khan.

The petitioners were represented by lawyers Yasir Khattak and Azhar Rahim Khan, while K-P Advocate General Sanaullah and the relevant officials also appeared before the court.

According to the court order, the deputy commissioner of Mardan had been issued a notice at the previous hearing, directing him to explain the reasons and circumstances under which the petitioners were detained and sent to jail.

Also Read: PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritise public welfare projects

However, the concerned authorities have yet to submit their report despite the court’s directions.

The bench observed that, in the absence of the required report, it had no option but to examine the available record and provide relief to the petitioners. It noted that similar relief had previously been granted in cases involving comparable circumstances.

Consequently, the court ordered the release of each petitioner against two surety bonds worth Rs100,000.

The bench clarified that the petitions would continue to be heard on merit and that the interim relief did not amount to a final decision on the legality of the detentions.

The deputy commissioner of Mardan was once again directed to submit the relevant report and record before the court.

The hearing was adjourned until November 12.
