headline: Pakistan slams Taliban's 'misguided approach'
description: Pakistan slams Taliban's 'misguided approach'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The information ministry on Saturday rebuked the Afghan Taliban's stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its "persistent refusal to address terrorism" emanating from Afghanistan's soil.

The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who blamed Islamabad's "wrong policies" for preventing a resolution to the conflict and insisted Kabul was not the cause of counterterrorism issues.

"Pakistan does not want to resolve the conflict with Afghanistan through talks," Mujahid told Hurriyat Radio, claiming that Islamabad "lacks the necessary readiness for a peaceful resolution of differences".

In its statement, the information ministry said the Afghan spokesman's remarks expose the "regime's deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan".

"The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad's policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil," it added.

"The Afghan Taliban regime must understand that Pakistan will not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that impact its security nor allow its people to remain targets of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan," it stated.

"Shifting blame, making hollow assurances and questioning Pakistan's policies will neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities. The Afghan Taliban leadership must understand that Pakistan's security will not be held hostage to Afghan Taliban's inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities."

headline: Faryal Talpur set to step up role in PPP's Punjab affairs
description: Faryal Talpur set to step up role in PPP's Punjab affairs
author: Rameez Khan
article_text:
With local government elections on the horizon, MPA Faryal Talpur, sister of President Asif Ali Zardari, has recently been entrusted with overseeing the province's organisation, previously under the direct control of party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, party sources said on Friday.

Talpur is expected to spend two days in Lahore in the second week of November, a visit that some party sources say could become a monthly feature.

Multiple party sources confirmed that, over the past few weeks, Talpur, a member of the Sindh Assembly who also heads the party's women's wing and is regarded within the party as its third most powerful figure after the chairman and co-chairman, has been actively holding meetings in Islamabad with representatives of the party's Punjab chapters.

These included the People's Youth Organisation, the women's wing and office-bearers from Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Sialkot and Faisalabad, as well as discussions on complaints raised by party office-bearers.

Sources said speculation first emerged within the party in early October that Talpur had been assigned the task of overseeing Punjab affairs and would visit Lahore in the first or second week of that month.

However, the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during the second week of October caused speculation about her expected visit to subside. The subsequent round of meetings in Islamabad, however, lent credence to reports that she had been given the driving seat in Punjab.

Recently, party sources said, Punjab leaders had been informed that Talpur, popularly known as Addi, was expected to visit Lahore on November 10 and 11.

The visit is ostensibly to attend the wedding of Nawab Shehzad's child, but party sources believe it will mark her formal entry into Punjab politics. They said Addi would subsequently visit the province once a month, staying for two to three days.

One source said the PPP Central Punjab secretariat was being extensively renovated to accommodate Talpur and her staff. The office of the party's general secretary on the first floor had been allocated to Faryal Bibi, while access to the entire floor during her stay would be restricted to those with prior clearance.

The source said the Central Punjab secretariat had been divided among several mid-tier party leaders, who were bearing the costs of the renovation work. The arrangements, the source added, were being made with Talpur's expected monthly visits in mind.

However, a second source said he was not entirely certain whether she would visit Punjab every month.

Another party leader said a schedule of meetings had also been prepared for Addi, under which she would meet district-level organisations, mainly from nearby districts, with the exception of Sahiwal.

Party ticket-holders would also be invited, including candidates for National Assembly seats who had secured around 30,000 votes and provincial assembly candidates who had obtained approximately 20,000 votes.

The leader said PPP Punjab General Secretary Hasan Murtaza would brief Talpur on the party's organisational structure in the province and the overall political situation.

Another party leader, requesting anonymity, said Talpur's presence was a good omen for the PPP in Punjab, particularly as local government elections approach.

He said her leadership would allow decisions to be made more swiftly, arguing that decisions routed through the party chairman often took considerable time, causing party workers and leaders to lose momentum.

He said Addi was well versed in street politics and that her leadership during the local government elections would be a major asset for the party.

PPP Information Secretary Nadeem Afzal Chan said Talpur would visit Lahore on November 10 and 11 and was expected to look after the party's affairs in Punjab.

However, he said it would not be entirely accurate to suggest that she would be calling all the shots in the province, as party decisions were made after consultation.

Chan said the party had President Asif Ali Zardari, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Bibi Faryal Talpur, and that matters overseen by Talpur were subsequently discussed with the party chairman before a final decision was reached.

Asked whether she would visit Lahore every month, he said they would know once she arrived.

Meanwhile, amid complaints submitted to Talpur and the party chairman, a disciplinary committee has been established in Punjab to address internal grievances and strengthen organisational discipline.

article_html:
LAHORE:

With local government elections on the horizon, MPA Faryal Talpur, sister of President Asif Ali Zardari, has recently been entrusted with overseeing the province's organisation, previously under the direct control of party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, party sources said on Friday.

Talpur is expected to spend two days in Lahore in the second week of November, a visit that some party sources say could become a monthly feature.

Multiple party sources confirmed that, over the past few weeks, Talpur, a member of the Sindh Assembly who also heads the party's women's wing and is regarded within the party as its third most powerful figure after the chairman and co-chairman, has been actively holding meetings in Islamabad with representatives of the party's Punjab chapters.

These included the People's Youth Organisation, the women's wing and office-bearers from Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Sialkot and Faisalabad, as well as discussions on complaints raised by party office-bearers.

Sources said speculation first emerged within the party in early October that Talpur had been assigned the task of overseeing Punjab affairs and would visit Lahore in the first or second week of that month.

However, the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during the second week of October caused speculation about her expected visit to subside. The subsequent round of meetings in Islamabad, however, lent credence to reports that she had been given the driving seat in Punjab.

Recently, party sources said, Punjab leaders had been informed that Talpur, popularly known as Addi, was expected to visit Lahore on November 10 and 11.

The visit is ostensibly to attend the wedding of Nawab Shehzad's child, but party sources believe it will mark her formal entry into Punjab politics. They said Addi would subsequently visit the province once a month, staying for two to three days.

One source said the PPP Central Punjab secretariat was being extensively renovated to accommodate Talpur and her staff. The office of the party's general secretary on the first floor had been allocated to Faryal Bibi, while access to the entire floor during her stay would be restricted to those with prior clearance.

The source said the Central Punjab secretariat had been divided among several mid-tier party leaders, who were bearing the costs of the renovation work. The arrangements, the source added, were being made with Talpur's expected monthly visits in mind.

However, a second source said he was not entirely certain whether she would visit Punjab every month.

Another party leader said a schedule of meetings had also been prepared for Addi, under which she would meet district-level organisations, mainly from nearby districts, with the exception of Sahiwal.

Party ticket-holders would also be invited, including candidates for National Assembly seats who had secured around 30,000 votes and provincial assembly candidates who had obtained approximately 20,000 votes.

The leader said PPP Punjab General Secretary Hasan Murtaza would brief Talpur on the party's organisational structure in the province and the overall political situation.

Another party leader, requesting anonymity, said Talpur's presence was a good omen for the PPP in Punjab, particularly as local government elections approach.

He said her leadership would allow decisions to be made more swiftly, arguing that decisions routed through the party chairman often took considerable time, causing party workers and leaders to lose momentum.

He said Addi was well versed in street politics and that her leadership during the local government elections would be a major asset for the party.

PPP Information Secretary Nadeem Afzal Chan said Talpur would visit Lahore on November 10 and 11 and was expected to look after the party's affairs in Punjab.

However, he said it would not be entirely accurate to suggest that she would be calling all the shots in the province, as party decisions were made after consultation.

Chan said the party had President Asif Ali Zardari, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and Bibi Faryal Talpur, and that matters overseen by Talpur were subsequently discussed with the party chairman before a final decision was reached.

Asked whether she would visit Lahore every month, he said they would know once she arrived.

Meanwhile, amid complaints submitted to Talpur and the party chairman, a disciplinary committee has been established in Punjab to address internal grievances and strengthen organisational discipline.

headline: Bank cash reporting limit raised to Rs3m
description: Bank cash reporting limit raised to Rs3m
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The federal government has increased the threshold for reporting cash transactions at banks from Rs2 million to Rs3 million, requiring financial institutions to report daily cash transactions exceeding the revised limit to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU).

Previously, banks were required to report cash transactions exceeding Rs2 million. The revised threshold forms part of a series of measures being taken to strengthen the country's anti-money laundering framework.

The government has also agreed to empower provincial anti-corruption establishments to help prevent money laundering.

headline: Three DISCOs to go under the hammer in 2027 Q1
description: Three DISCOs to go under the hammer in 2027 Q1
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

Prime Minister's Adviser on Privatisation and Chairman of the Privatisation Commission Muhammad Ali has said that he government is planning to privatise three power distribution companies (DISCOs) during the first quarter of 2027.

The Companies included Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (FESCO), Gujranwala Electric Power Company (GEPCO) and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO), he said in an interview, on Saturday.

Ali said that due diligence for the three companies was already underway, while potential investors had requested additional time to assess the complex transactions.

headline: ECP schedules Quetta, Kharian delimitations
description: ECP schedules Quetta, Kharian delimitations
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has notified delimitation schedules for the Quetta and Kharian cantonment boards following their reclassification by the federal government.

The federal government has reclassified the Quetta Cantonment Board from Class-II to Class-I and that in Punjab's Kharian from Class-III to Class-II. The ECP has fixed the number of wards in Quetta at 10 and five in Kharian.

According to three notifications issued on Oct 29, the delimitation exercise for Quetta and Kharian will be carried out from November this year until January 2027.

Administrative arrangements, including the procurement of maps and training of committees and authorities, will be completed from Nov 2 to 4, and delimitation committees will prepare preliminary lists of wards from Nov 5 to 19, which will be published on Nov 20 to invite objections.

Objections can be filed before delimitation authorities from Nov 21 to Dec 20. The authorities will dispose of objections by Jan 5, 2027 and communicate decisions to committees by Jan 8. Final lists of wards will be published on Jan 13.

The ECP has appointed the Gujrat district election commissioner as the convener of the delimitation committee for Kharian, with the Kharian cantonment executive officer and Gujrat assistant election commissioner as members.

For Quetta, the Quetta East district election commissioner will act as convener, while the Quetta additional cantonment executive officer and Quetta East assistant election commissioner will serve as members.

The regional election commissioners for Gujranwala and Quetta have been appointed as delimitation authorities for the Kharian and Quetta cantonment boards, respectively, to decide objections.

The commission directed that officers appointed for delimitation shall not be transferred without its prior approval.

Women voters

The ECP will launch a pilot project in Kasur district of Punjab and Qambar Shahdadkot district of Sindh from December 2026 to February 2027 to facilitate the registration of 174,845 women as voters and help reduce the gender gap in electoral rolls through improved access to identity cards and voter registration services.

According to ECP, the initiative aims to identify eligible women who do not possess Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs) or are not registered as voters, persuade them to complete the process and facilitate their registration through door-to-door outreach and mobile registration facilities.

Under the initiative, the Commission will facilitate the registration of 115,689 women in Kasur and 59,156 in Qambar Shahdadkot.

The project will initially prioritize statistical blocks with a higher gender gap in voter registration, based on available data.

The required data will be collected in November 2026, followed by registration activities from December 2026 to February 2027.

Local social workers and enumerators will conduct door-to-door visits to prepare statistical block wise lists of eligible women and raise awareness about the importance of obtaining CNICs and registering as voters.

To improve access, the ECP will coordinate with the NADRA to deploy Mobile Registration Vans (MRVs) to women's doorsteps. Registration facilities will also be provided at centres established in government buildings.

headline: Country faces over 200,000 tons of fertiliser shortfall
description: Country faces over 200,000 tons of fertiliser shortfall
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Middle East conflict and gas shortages have exacerbated the urea shortage, adding to farmers' woes as they grapple with rising crop cultivation costs.

The government has acknowledged a fertilizer shortfall of more than 200,000 tonnes against the country's demand.

This was disclosed during Question Hour in the National Assembly. The government said due to the Middle East situation, gas supply was affected, causing two urea plants in the country to remain temporarily closed, resulting in a shortfall of over 200,000 tons of fertilizer availability and creating shortage issues in the market.

During Question Hour, Parliamentary Secretary Shaista Khan told the House that agricultural production depends on fertilizer availability, therefore any increase or decrease in fertilizer prices and supply is a matter of concern for the government. The government is also relying on imports to meet fertilizer requirements, with about 50% of the country's needs being met from abroad. Due to the Middle East crisis, fertilizer prices have also increased.

She said the Ministry of National Food Security and Research gives priority to farmers' needs and various projects are being launched to solve their problems, including provision of easy loans to farmers so they can meet their agricultural needs.

In reply to a supplementary question, the secretary said that on the issue of adulteration of wheat with sand and soil in K-P, the concerned minister is planning has been done to take action against those involved in supply of substandard wheat.

She further said that work is underway at NARC for development and research of new seed varieties. To cope with climate change challenges, research is being conducted on seeds compatible with wheat and water scarcity conditions to enable Pakistan's agriculture sector to combat effects of climate change.

headline: FCC lists challenge to PHC's PTI order
description: FCC lists challenge to PHC's PTI order
author: Hasnaat Malik
article_text:
The FCC has listed for hearing K-P government petitions against a Peshawar High Court's interim order directing police not to arrest PTI workers in K-P.

An FCC division bench comprising Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan and Justice Ali Baqar Najfi will take up petitions against the PHC interim order on November 5.

Earlier, PTI workers approached the PHC challenging their detention by the executive under Section 3 of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960. The matter is still pending in the high court. However, the K-P government has challenged the interim order in 48 PTI workers' case.

It has been witnessed that though the PHC has granted some relief to PTI workers, no substantive relief has been granted to the party supporters by the Lahore High Court. PTI's legal team claims that thousands of workers are detained under MPO all over the country especially Punjab.

Since the passage of the 27th Constitutional Amendment, the PTI has struggled to get substantive relief in matters related to civil liberties.

Likewise, the PTI has not received any relief from the FCC, created last year under the 27th Amendment. Recently the court rejected PTI founder Imran Khan's wife Bushra Bibi's petition seeking suspension of her sentence in the Al-Qadir Trust case.

The FCC while hearing a three-prisoner case, summoned the record of Imran Khan's hospital shifting case from the Supreme Court. Although the PTI is reluctant to approach the FCC in any matter, the court has taken up several cases against the party. It has even passed interim orders.

The FCC judges face a battle of perception since the federal government appointed them. The federal government is also the primary litigant before the court.

Cameras

The FCC has reserved its verdict on an appeal filed by the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government against a high court order directing an end to CCTV surveillance inside prisoners' cells.

During the hearing, the court raised questions about inmates' privacy, human dignity and security, with Justice Rozi Khan observing that a prison cell was like a bedroom and questioning how cameras could be installed there.

The judge also questioned the practice in the context of Article 14 of the Constitution, which guarantees the inviolability of human dignity.

Justice Aamer Farooq asked whether cameras had been installed only inside prisoners' cells or throughout the prison. He also sought to know whether inmates' every movement was monitored inside their cells.

Representing the provincial government, lawyer Shamail Aziz argued that the prisoners were involved in serious crimes and that the cameras were primarily intended to ensure security.

headline: Govt defends shifting of PPL HQ to Islamabad
description: Govt defends shifting of PPL HQ to Islamabad
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry has said the proposed relocation of Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL) headquarters from Karachi to Islamabad was an operational and administrative matter aimed at improving efficiency and reducing unnecessary expenses.

Responding to a Calling Attention Notice moved by Senators Syed Waqar Mehdi and Zamir Hussain Ghumro in the Senate, he rejected concerns that the proposal was driven by regional or provincial considerations.

He said the decision was being considered on technical and operational grounds, adding that the company's board had repeatedly highlighted the need to vacate the existing building due to its condition.

The minister said around 77 per cent of PPL employees were based at field locations and other offices and would not be affected by the proposed relocation. Only around 15 per cent of the workforce was based at the headquarters, he added.

Talal Chaudhry said maintaining offices and administrative arrangements at two locations would increase costs, ultimately placing an unnecessary financial burden on the public.

He stressed that the company's board and management should be allowed to make decisions based on operational requirements rather than viewing the matter through a provincial or regional lens.

The meeting covered the overall political environment, democratic affairs and other key political issues. The US delegation listened to the PTI leadership's position and exchanged views on various matters.

headline: Express drama explores burden of parental expectations
description: Express drama explores burden of parental expectations
author: Qaisar Kamran
article_text:
In many Pakistani households, a child's future is often decided long before they are old enough to understand what they actually want to become.

Some are expected to become doctors, others engineers or chartered accountants. But what happens when a child's ambitions lie somewhere entirely different?

This conflict is explored in the Express Entertainment drama Hum Bhi Jee Lian, where actor Sharoze Sabzwari character Arsal finds himself caught between his family's expectations and his own creative ambitions.

Speaking with The Express Tribune about the project, the actor Sharoze Sabwari said the story immediately appealed to him because of the contradiction at the heart of his character: a young man with a writer's imagination who is being pushed towards accountancy.

Arsal has lost both his parents, leaving his elder sister, played by Faiza Hassan, responsible for raising him and deciding his future. She wants him to become a chartered accountant, a path he has been encouraged to follow since childhood.

But beneath those expectations is someone who wants to write stories.

"The writer inside him is what attracted me to the character," the actor said. "There is a writer hidden inside him, but above that is accountancy. For someone who wants to write, it is a very dry subject, yet he is being made to study it."

He believes the situation reflects the experiences of many young people whose families prioritise conventional careers over their children's individual interests.

"People are studying medicine or law because their parents want them to, even though they want to become something else," he said.

The actor said the drama also explores how parental and family pressure can continue even when children grow older. Sometimes, he added, elders fail to understand a child's personality and ambitions, dismissing their choices rather than trusting them.

He believes parents need to recognise that their children belong to a different generation and should be allowed to make decisions about their own futures.

Parents, he argued, should understand their children's age, interests and way of thinking, and encourage them in the direction where their abilities naturally lie.

"If you push them towards what they are inclined to do, they will shine even more," he said.

While the drama explores the freedom to choose one's own path, the actor also spoke about the challenges of pursuing creative ambitions in Pakistan's entertainment industry.

He said he was grateful to have achieved many of the dreams he had when he first entered acting, including the opportunity to work on several well-known projects.

However, he hopes to move beyond the younger characters he has frequently portrayed.

Having played college students and characters involved in romantic and unrequited love stories, he said he now wants roles that carry greater responsibility and contribute more substantially to the narrative.

"I have a lot more to do. I want to play mature characters, roles with more responsibilities and characters that take the story forward," he said.

He acknowledged, however, that an actor's ambitions do not always match the commercial realities of television production.

According to him, writers and producers have different considerations from performers. While an actor may want to play a particular character, producers must also consider whether audiences will watch the project.

"Art is also a business. Production houses are there to make money, at the end of the day," he said, adding that actors should understand the commercial considerations behind casting and storytelling.

The actor also reflected on why many performers appear reluctant to speak openly about social and economic issues.

He said the growth of social media had changed the nature of public criticism. In the past, criticism might have appeared in a newspaper or magazine, but today it can reach an actor's family and personal circle almost immediately.

With smartphones and internet access becoming widespread, even relatives living in remote areas can encounter online criticism and comments about an actor's work.

"It is no longer just criticism directed at me. It can reach my family members as well," he said. He suggested that this has made some performers more cautious about expressing their opinions publicly.

The actor also acknowledged that an earlier remark he made about being grateful for one's circumstances could have sounded dismissive of people's economic difficulties.

He clarified that gratitude and faith should not prevent people from acknowledging the hardships others face, particularly amid rising inflation.

While the drama explores the freedom to choose one's own path, the actor also spoke about the challenges of pursuing creative ambitions in Pakistan's entertainment industry.
He said he was grateful to have achieved many of the dreams he had when he first entered acting, including the opportunity to work on several well-known projects.
However, he hopes to move beyond the younger characters he has frequently portrayed.

Having played college students and characters involved in romantic and unrequited love stories, he said he now wants roles that carry greater responsibility and contribute more substantially to the narrative.
"I have a lot more to do. I want to play mature characters, roles with more responsibilities and characters that take the story forward," he said.
He acknowledged, however, that an actor's ambitions do not always match the commercial realities of television production.

According to him, writers and producers have different considerations from performers. While an actor may want to play a particular character, producers must also consider whether audiences will watch the project.

"Art is also a business. Production houses are there to make money, at the end of the day," he said, adding that actors should understand the commercial considerations behind casting and storytelling.
The actor also reflected on why many performers appear reluctant to speak openly about social and economic issues.

He said the growth of social media had changed the nature of public criticism. In the past, criticism might have appeared in a newspaper or magazine, but today it can reach an actor's family and personal circle almost immediately.
With smartphones and internet access becoming widespread, even relatives living in remote areas can encounter online criticism and comments about an actor's work.

"It is no longer just criticism directed at me. It can reach my family members as well," he said. He suggested that this has made some performers more cautious about expressing their opinions publicly.
The actor also acknowledged that an earlier remark he made about being grateful for one's circumstances could have sounded dismissive of people's economic difficulties.
He clarified that gratitude and faith should not prevent people from acknowledging the hardships others face, particularly amid rising inflation.

headline: Selma Blair issues public apology after plane incident
description: Selma Blair issues public apology after plane incident
author: News Desk
article_text:
Selma Blair has publicly apologised following an incident aboard a flight from Los Angeles to New York that led to her arrest and criminal charges.

The Cruel Intentions and Legally Blonde actress, 54, shared a video statement on Instagram on October 30, addressing the October 11 incident at John F Kennedy International Airport. She allegedly injured a flight attendant and kicked a nurse after being removed from the aircraft.

Blair is facing two second-degree assault charges related to alleged attacks on the nurse and a Port Authority officer. In her video, the actress said her legal team had advised her against discussing the case in detail.

"What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life," Blair said.

She then addressed those affected by the incident, adding: "To the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed: I am so sorry."

Blair's representatives previously attributed the episode to a medical emergency. Her attorney, Shawn Barnes, told the court that she had boarded the flight after missing several doses of medication used to control neurological symptoms.

According to her lawyer, the missed medication, combined with the effects of altitude, resulted in severe confusion and disorientation. Barnes also said Blair had fallen and hit her head during the flight.

The actress was released from custody on $20,000 bail the day after the incident.

Blair is scheduled to return to court in Queens on January 19, where proceedings related to the charges are expected to continue.

Blair won her first professional role in a 1995 episode of the children's sitcom The Adventures of Pete & Pete. In 1996, she landed her first feature film role in the comedy The Broccoli Theory. In 1997, she made her first appearance in a mainstream feature film, the comedy In & Out. She auditioned six times for the role and remained on-set for several weeks, but most of her scenes were cut from the film's final version.

Her first lead role was in the film Strong Island Boys. She then won the lead in the 1997 fantasy film Amazon High. The film did not air, but portions of it were used in the 2000 Xena: Warrior Princess episode "Lifeblood". She subsequently appeared in several independent and short productions, including the award-winning Debutante.

The case remains ongoing, and the allegations have not been established in court. Her apology marks her first public statement addressing the incident directly, as she continues to face legal proceedings in New York.

headline: Pakistani songs make their mark in global music
description: Pakistani songs make their mark in global music
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A Pakistani song reaching international music charts is no longer an isolated achievement. Behind some of these successes is a growing network of artists, producers and creative collaborators working to take local music beyond traditional markets.

The recent success of Alfaaz, performed by Hamza Malik and Zain Zohaib, offers an example of this changing landscape. Released under Giraffe Music, the song has topped Spotify's daily charts in Pakistan and India, reached No. 2 on the UK Official Asian Music Chart and climbed to No. 35 on Spotify's Global Daily Top 200.

It has also secured the second position on Billboard's India Songs chart for the week ending 31 October 2026, moving up from third place the previous week.

While the singers and their performance remain at the heart of the track's success, its international reach also draws attention to the wider creative network supporting Pakistani music.

For Giraffe, Alfaaz is not the first project to find an audience beyond Pakistan.

In 2025, Majboor, performed by Sheheryar Rehan and Zoha Waseem, gained popularity online before Belgian DJ and producer Lost Frequencies reimagined the track, giving it an international dimension.

Although originally released in 2025, the song gained further momentum in 2026, reaching No. 1 on Spotify's Pakistan and Global Viral charts, as well as the Pakistan Viral chart. It also reached No. 2 in India.

The two songs have followed different paths, but both demonstrate how digital platforms and international collaborations can help Pakistani music reach listeners in new markets.

Its work reflects a broader shift in how music is developed and promoted, where bringing artists, creative ideas and collaborators together can be as important as producing the song itself.

headline: Shatner, 'Star Trek' co-stars pay tribute to Patrick Stewart
description: Shatner, 'Star Trek' co-stars pay tribute to Patrick Stewart
author: News Desk
article_text:
William Shatner and members of the Star Trek cast have paid tribute to Patrick Stewart following the actor's death at the age of 86, remembering the man behind Captain Jean-Luc Picard as a friend, colleague and extraordinary performer.

Shatner, who famously portrayed Captain James T Kirk in the original Star Trek series, shared a heartfelt message following Stewart's death on October 28.

"What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner wrote.

"From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

Shatner concluded his tribute by expressing his condolences to Stewart's wife, Sunny Ozell, and his family, adding that the actor would be deeply missed.

Stewart became internationally recognised for playing Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, taking over the captain's chair after Shatner's iconic portrayal of Kirk in the original series.

The two actors eventually shared the screen in Star Trek: Generations in 1994, bringing together the original and next-generation crews in a story that marked a passing of the torch between the franchise's leading captains.

Other members of the Star Trek family also paid tribute to Stewart.

George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu in the original series, described Stewart as a "true and irreplaceable legend" whose portrayal of Picard inspired a new generation of fans.

"As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before," Takei wrote. "He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity."

Stewart's The Next Generation co-stars also shared messages of remembrance. Wil Wheaton, who played Wesley Crusher, posted a photograph with Stewart alongside the words "Godspeed, Captain".

Jonathan Frakes, who portrayed William Riker, shared a photograph of Stewart and wrote, "Rest in peace, my friend."

Akiva Goldsman, co-creator and co-showrunner of Star Trek: Picard, described Stewart as a remarkable performer whose portrayal of Picard had permanently expanded the Star Trek universe.

"Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman said.

He added that Stewart was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise.

Stewart died following what his family described as a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia". His family said he had been surrounded by loved ones, music, prayer, tears and laughter during his final days.

Beyond Star Trek, Stewart was also widely known for playing Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, with a career spanning more than six decades across television, film and theatre. He also acted in Hedda (1975), Excalibur (1981), Dune (1984), Robin Hood: Men in Tights (1993), Jeffrey (1995), Match (2014), Green Room (2015), and The Kid Who Would Be King (2019).

His death has prompted tributes from across the entertainment industry, with fellow actors and collaborators remembering both his extraordinary talent and the humanity he brought to his most celebrated roles.

article_html:
William Shatner and members of the Star Trek cast have paid tribute to Patrick Stewart following the actor's death at the age of 86, remembering the man behind Captain Jean-Luc Picard as a friend, colleague and extraordinary performer.

Shatner, who famously portrayed Captain James T Kirk in the original Star Trek series, shared a heartfelt message following Stewart's death on October 28.

"What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner wrote.

"From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

Shatner concluded his tribute by expressing his condolences to Stewart's wife, Sunny Ozell, and his family, adding that the actor would be deeply missed.

Stewart became internationally recognised for playing Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, taking over the captain's chair after Shatner's iconic portrayal of Kirk in the original series.

The two actors eventually shared the screen in Star Trek: Generations in 1994, bringing together the original and next-generation crews in a story that marked a passing of the torch between the franchise's leading captains.

Other members of the Star Trek family also paid tribute to Stewart.

George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu in the original series, described Stewart as a "true and irreplaceable legend" whose portrayal of Picard inspired a new generation of fans.

"As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before," Takei wrote. "He inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity."

Stewart's The Next Generation co-stars also shared messages of remembrance. Wil Wheaton, who played Wesley Crusher, posted a photograph with Stewart alongside the words "Godspeed, Captain".

Jonathan Frakes, who portrayed William Riker, shared a photograph of Stewart and wrote, "Rest in peace, my friend."

Akiva Goldsman, co-creator and co-showrunner of Star Trek: Picard, described Stewart as a remarkable performer whose portrayal of Picard had permanently expanded the Star Trek universe.

"Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman said.

He added that Stewart was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise.

Stewart died following what his family described as a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia". His family said he had been surrounded by loved ones, music, prayer, tears and laughter during his final days.

Beyond Star Trek, Stewart was also widely known for playing Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, with a career spanning more than six decades across television, film and theatre. He also acted in Hedda (1975), Excalibur (1981), Dune (1984), Robin Hood: Men in Tights (1993), Jeffrey (1995), Match (2014), Green Room (2015), and The Kid Who Would Be King (2019).

His death has prompted tributes from across the entertainment industry, with fellow actors and collaborators remembering both his extraordinary talent and the humanity he brought to his most celebrated roles.

headline: Gaza charities 'incredibly grateful' for Macklemore's support
description: Gaza charities 'incredibly grateful' for Macklemore's support
author: News Desk
article_text:
Gaza charities have expressed their gratitude to Macklemore for using his platform to support Palestinians, as the rapper prepares to conclude his sold-out Free Palestine Tour in London.

The Seattle-born artist launched the three-show European tour after being dropped as a supporting act on Ed Sheeran's US stadium tour in September, following comments he made about Gaza.

Macklemore, 43, has spoken out in support of Palestinians during performances, calling for a "Free Palestine" and describing the situation in Gaza as a "genocide".

All proceeds from the three sold-out concerts will go to 12 organisations and charities supporting Palestinians, including those providing humanitarian aid, medical care, education and community support.

Shabby Amini, director of fundraising and marketing at Medical Aid for Palestinians, said the organisation was "incredibly grateful" for Macklemore's support.

"We are incredibly grateful to Macklemore for his generous support and for using his platform to keep the experiences of Palestinians in the spotlight, especially at a time when many are choosing to stay silent," Amini said.

"Macklemore's support is a powerful reminder that Palestinians must not be forgotten when the headlines move on."

A spokesperson for Anera, an aid organisation supporting displaced Palestinians, also praised the rapper's efforts to bring people together through music.

"Music has always had the power to bring people together, inspire action and unite us in the pursuit of something greater," the spokesperson said.

"Seeing thousands of people come together through song and love in solidarity with the people of Gaza moves us deeply."

Macklemore's Free Palestine Tour began in Dublin on October 26, followed by a show in Paris on October 29. The final concert is scheduled to take place at London's OVO Arena Wembley on Friday evening.

The organisations set to benefit from the tour include Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, Heal Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children's Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children's Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.

The rapper announced the tour 10 days after being removed from Sheeran's The Loop tour.

Macklemore has said that Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, contacted Sheeran and said the rapper would not be allowed to perform at the venue if he remained on the bill.

Sheeran later said the decision to remove Macklemore was made by his promoter, after venues indicated they would not host the shows with the rapper as a supporting act.

Several other artists subsequently withdrew from Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

Macklemore & Ryan Lewis's 2012 single "Thrift Shop" (featuring Wanz) became the first self-released song to top the Billboard Hot 100 in 11 years. Their second single, "Can't Hold Us" (featuring Ray Dalton), also peaked on chart, making Macklemore and Lewis the first duo in the chart's history to have their first two singles both reach the peak position. Their debut studio album The Heist (2012) peaked at number 2 on the U.S. Billboard 200. The duo entered into a slightly unusual three-month, one-album contract with Warner Bros.'s independent distribution arm ADA, which allowed them to retain control over their intellectual property and maintain their "artistic integrity". At the 56th Annual Grammy Awards, the duo won Best New Artist, Best Rap Album (The Heist), Best Rap Song ("Same Love") and Best Rap Performance ("Thrift Shop"). The duo's second album, This Unruly Mess I've Made (2016), followed thereafter.

In June 2017, Macklemore released the single "Glorious" (featuring Skylar Grey), which marked his return to the music industry as well as his first major single produced without Lewis since his mainstream breakthrough. Macklemore released his second solo studio album, Gemini, in September of that year, peaking at number 2 on the Billboard 200.

The Free Palestine Tour has brought together musicians and supporters to raise funds and maintain attention on the humanitarian crisis facing Palestinians.

The Seattle-born artist launched the three-show European tour after being dropped as a supporting act on Ed Sheeran's US stadium tour in September, following comments he made about Gaza.
Macklemore, 43, has spoken out in support of Palestinians during performances, calling for a "Free Palestine" and describing the situation in Gaza as a "genocide".

All proceeds from the three sold-out concerts will go to 12 organisations and charities supporting Palestinians, including those providing humanitarian aid, medical care, education and community support.
Shabby Amini, director of fundraising and marketing at Medical Aid for Palestinians, said the organisation was "incredibly grateful" for Macklemore's support.

"We are incredibly grateful to Macklemore for his generous support and for using his platform to keep the experiences of Palestinians in the spotlight, especially at a time when many are choosing to stay silent," Amini said.
"Macklemore's support is a powerful reminder that Palestinians must not be forgotten when the headlines move on."
A spokesperson for Anera, an aid organisation supporting displaced Palestinians, also praised the rapper's efforts to bring people together through music.
"Music has always had the power to bring people together, inspire action and unite us in the pursuit of something greater," the spokesperson said.
"Seeing thousands of people come together through song and love in solidarity with the people of Gaza moves us deeply."

Macklemore's Free Palestine Tour began in Dublin on October 26, followed by a show in Paris on October 29. The final concert is scheduled to take place at London's OVO Arena Wembley on Friday evening.

The organisations set to benefit from the tour include Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, Heal Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children's Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children's Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.
The rapper announced the tour 10 days after being removed from Sheeran's The Loop tour.

Macklemore has said that Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, contacted Sheeran and said the rapper would not be allowed to perform at the venue if he remained on the bill.
Sheeran later said the decision to remove Macklemore was made by his promoter, after venues indicated they would not host the shows with the rapper as a supporting act.
Several other artists subsequently withdrew from Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

Macklemore & Ryan Lewis's 2012 single "Thrift Shop" (featuring Wanz) became the first self-released song to top the Billboard Hot 100 in 11 years. Their second single, "Can't Hold Us" (featuring Ray Dalton), also peaked on chart, making Macklemore and Lewis the first duo in the chart's history to have their first two singles both reach the peak position. Their debut studio album The Heist (2012) peaked at number 2 on the U.S. Billboard 200. The duo entered into a slightly unusual three-month, one-album contract with Warner Bros.'s independent distribution arm ADA, which allowed them to retain control over their intellectual property and maintain their "artistic integrity". At the 56th Annual Grammy Awards, the duo won Best New Artist, Best Rap Album (The Heist), Best Rap Song ("Same Love") and Best Rap Performance ("Thrift Shop"). The duo's second album, This Unruly Mess I've Made (2016), followed thereafter.

In June 2017, Macklemore released the single "Glorious" (featuring Skylar Grey), which marked his return to the music industry as well as his first major single produced without Lewis since his mainstream breakthrough. headline: 'The Great Gatsby' gets crime drama adaptation
description: 'The Great Gatsby' gets crime drama adaptation
author: News Desk
article_text:
NBC is developing Gatsby, a modern-day police procedural inspired by F. Scott Fitzgerald's classic novel The Great Gatsby, with a gender-swapped twist on one of its central characters.

The series comes from writers and executive producers Jake Coburn and Jason Tracey, with Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group, attached to the project, Deadline reported on October 30.

The upcoming drama will centre on Det. Jay Gatsby, a charming investigator with a con artist's ability to read human behaviour, and New York State Police Det. Nicole "Nicky" Carraway, a decorated officer who has always wanted to become a writer.

Nicky is a gender-swapped version of Nick Carraway, the narrator of Fitzgerald's 1925 novel. In the original story, Nick moves to the fictional Long Island neighbourhood of West Egg, where he becomes acquainted with the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and his attempts to rekindle his romance with Daisy Buchanan.

The new adaptation will reimagine the literary characters in a contemporary crime-solving setting, shifting the focus towards a police procedural format.

The Great Gatsby is widely regarded as one of the great American novels and has inspired several screen adaptations. Among the best-known are the 1974 film starring Robert Redford and Mia Farrow, and Baz Luhrmann's 2013 version featuring Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire and Carey Mulligan.

Coburn previously worked on NBC's The Hunting Party, serving as co-showrunner and executive producer. His other credits include The Endgame, Quantico and Gossip Girl.

Tracey most recently served as an executive producer on ABC's RJ Decker. He also created and showran CSI: Vegas and worked on Elementary, Burn Notice and Cold Case.

No casting details or premiere date have been announced.

headline: US to deport 150 Afghan migrants via Pakistan
description: US to deport 150 Afghan migrants via Pakistan
author: AFP
article_text:
President Donald Trump's administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported Friday, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives.

Trump last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown, and sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the August 2021 takeover by Taliban authorities.

More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday.

Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies.

While the United States cannot arrange deportations directly to Afghanistan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan.

Pakistan's government earlier this year ordered law enforcement nationwide to arrest Afghan citizens without visas as part of a years-long repatriation policy that has pushed back millions of Afghans who fled their homes after the Taliban returned to power.

Taliban authorities were not immediately available for comment. The US Department of Homeland Security did not respond to questions from AFP.

"America is about to put Afghans on a plane to the Taliban, and the administration is doing it the week the country goes to vote, hoping no one is watching," AfghanEvac President Shawn VanDiver said in a statement, referring to the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

VanDiver said some of the migrants facing removal "are the brothers and sons of men who served alongside US forces, families the Taliban already has every reason to target."

"Whatever path brought them here, the danger waiting for them is the same."

After regaining power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments.

However, the United Nations has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses.

headline: PM tears into PTI's 13-year 'misrule' in K-P
description: PM tears into PTI's 13-year 'misrule' in K-P
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday called upon the provincial leadership of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa to urgently prioritise short-term, public welfare-oriented initiatives, asserting that local residents have suffered years of developmental neglect.

Addressing a gathering of the PML-N K-P chapter, the prime minister criticised the past PTI-led administration's governance record, saying that despite tall claims of revolutionary reforms in the education and health sectors, citizens continued to yearn for basic facilities.

He regretted that PTI's political focus was diverted toward protests and sit-ins rather than addressing the socio-economic needs of the province.

"How many development projects were completed? Were public funds spent judiciously, and what steps were taken against corruption?" the prime minister questioned, raising concerns over transparency and the execution of past provincial policies.

PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritize public welfare projects

Turning to national security, the prime minister paid rich tribute to the immense sacrifices rendered by the residents of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, law enforcement agencies, and the armed forces in eradicating terrorism during the 20172018 period.

He noted that the country lost approximately 80,000 precious lives, with economic losses mounting between $150 billion and $200 billion in the long fight against terrorism.

He specifically recalled the tragic attack on the Army Public School (APS) in Peshawar as an unforgettable manifestation of barbarism, while also acknowledging the sacrifices borne by political figures and security personnel.

Reflecting on past political and economic milestones, the prime minister criticized the 2014 PTI's sit-ins, noting that they coincided with and delayed the historic visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

He contrasted this with the subsequent signing of major bilateral agreements in 2015 and the eventual elimination of crippling, hours-long load-shedding under the leadership of Nawaz Sharif.

Furthermore, the prime minister expressed deep concern over security challenges witnessed in subsequent years, emphasizing the need for sustained vigilance, economic uplift, and grassroots development to deliver tangible relief to the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

About Governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), he described the measure as an unavoidable step to protect the state, economy, and the welfare of the provincial populace.

Addressing party leaders, the prime minister pointed back to the 2010 National Finance Commission (NFC) Awardconcluded under then-Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani with unanimous consensus from all chief ministerswhich allocated a 1% financial share directly to KP.

He noted that the province has accrued approximately Rs 800 billion from this arrangement over the years.

Questioning the transparency of fund utilization, the prime minister asked how much of that allocation was genuinely invested into reinforcing the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and local law enforcement.

Had those resources been properly managed, he argued, the provincial police force would have been significantly better equipped to tackle security challenges. About 8,000 police vacancies were lying in the province.

Addressing the broader macroeconomic environment, the prime minister acknowledged that ongoing crises in the Gulf region have driven global energy costs upward. However, he emphasized that the federal government has ensured uninterrupted supplies of petrol and diesel across the country.

He highlighted the launch of a targeted fuel subsidy program in February, backed by a Rs 75 billion allocation, which has successfully delivered relief vouchers to approximately 130 million citizens.

Detailing the breakdown in political negotiations he said, the federal government made concerted efforts to engage the PTI leadership in KP to address pressing national challenges cooperatively. According to the prime minister, after negotiations led by a joint PML-N and PPP delegation, the finalized draft proposals faced outright delay from Sohail Afridi, leaving them with no alternative course of action.

"We had no other option but to save the country, the economy, the society, and KP," he warned, stressing that further hesitation would have led to catastrophic outcomes.

The prime minister also outlined ongoing projects to build Daanish Schools across remote districtsincluding Chitral, Haripur, Mansehra, Bajaur, and Shanglawith plans to announce several additional campuses later in the year.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD:

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday called upon the provincial leadership of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa to urgently prioritise short-term, public welfare-oriented initiatives, asserting that local residents have suffered years of developmental neglect.

Addressing a gathering of the PML-N K-P chapter, the prime minister criticised the past PTI-led administration's governance record, saying that despite tall claims of revolutionary reforms in the education and health sectors, citizens continued to yearn for basic facilities.

He regretted that PTI's political focus was diverted toward protests and sit-ins rather than addressing the socio-economic needs of the province.

"How many development projects were completed? Were public funds spent judiciously, and what steps were taken against corruption?" the prime minister questioned, raising concerns over transparency and the execution of past provincial policies.

PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritize public welfare projects

Turning to national security, the prime minister paid rich tribute to the immense sacrifices rendered by the residents of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, law enforcement agencies, and the armed forces in eradicating terrorism during the 20172018 period.

He noted that the country lost approximately 80,000 precious lives, with economic losses mounting between $150 billion and $200 billion in the long fight against terrorism.

He specifically recalled the tragic attack on the Army Public School (APS) in Peshawar as an unforgettable manifestation of barbarism, while also acknowledging the sacrifices borne by political figures and security personnel.

Reflecting on past political and economic milestones, the prime minister criticized the 2014 PTI's sit-ins, noting that they coincided with and delayed the historic visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

He contrasted this with the subsequent signing of major bilateral agreements in 2015 and the eventual elimination of crippling, hours-long load-shedding under the leadership of Nawaz Sharif.

Furthermore, the prime minister expressed deep concern over security challenges witnessed in subsequent years, emphasizing the need for sustained vigilance, economic uplift, and grassroots development to deliver tangible relief to the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

About Governor's rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), he described the measure as an unavoidable step to protect the state, economy, and the welfare of the provincial populace.

Addressing party leaders, the prime minister pointed back to the 2010 National Finance Commission (NFC) Awardconcluded under then-Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani with unanimous consensus from all chief ministerswhich allocated a 1% financial share directly to KP.

He noted that the province has accrued approximately Rs 800 billion from this arrangement over the years.

Questioning the transparency of fund utilization, the prime minister asked how much of that allocation was genuinely invested into reinforcing the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and local law enforcement.

Had those resources been properly managed, he argued, the provincial police force would have been significantly better equipped to tackle security challenges. About 8,000 police vacancies were lying in the province.

Addressing the broader macroeconomic environment, the prime minister acknowledged that ongoing crises in the Gulf region have driven global energy costs upward. However, he emphasized that the federal government has ensured uninterrupted supplies of petrol and diesel across the country.

He highlighted the launch of a targeted fuel subsidy program in February, backed by a Rs 75 billion allocation, which has successfully delivered relief vouchers to approximately 130 million citizens.

Detailing the breakdown in political negotiations he said, the federal government made concerted efforts to engage the PTI leadership in KP to address pressing national challenges cooperatively. According to the prime minister, after negotiations led by a joint PML-N and PPP delegation, the finalized draft proposals faced outright delay from Sohail Afridi, leaving them with no alternative course of action.

"We had no other option but to save the country, the economy, the society, and KP," he warned, stressing that further hesitation would have led to catastrophic outcomes.

The prime minister also outlined ongoing projects to build Daanish Schools across remote districtsincluding Chitral, Haripur, Mansehra, Bajaur, and Shanglawith plans to announce several additional campuses later in the year.

headline: Mansehra AC wounded in K-P gun attack
description: Mansehra AC wounded in K-P gun attack
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Two separate gun attacks in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa on Saturday left a police constable martyred, two people injured and Mansehra Assistant Commissioner Adil Waseem wounded.

Waseem was targeted in Nowshera district while travelling in his official vehicle, while another attack took place outside a courtroom at the Judicial Complex in Lakki Marwat, where unidentified gunmen opened fire, killing a policeman and injuring two others.

Police launched investigations into both incidents and tightened security at the locations.

Waseem came under attack in the Panah Kot area while returning from his native village of Saleh Khana, police officials said. He sustained injuries in the firing and was immediately shifted to hospital, where doctors described his condition as stable.

Muhammad Asim, spokesperson for Peshawar's Lady Reading Hospital, said Waseem was "stable" and receiving medical treatment.

Nowshera District Police Officer Sonia Shamroz said the area had been cordoned off immediately after the attack and a search operation launched. A team had also been constituted to arrest those involved, she added.

The DPO further said a case had been registered and an investigation into the incident was under way.

In the separate incident in Lakki Marwat, a police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge at the Judicial Complex.

District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal sustained bullet wounds. Another person, identified as Inshaullah, was also injured in the firing.

Both injured men were shifted to Bannu for medical treatment. Khan confirmed that one body and two injured people had been brought to the hospital.

The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic inside the complex. Lawyers, litigants and other visitors rushed to safety as gunshots rang out.

A heavy police contingent arrived at the scene and launched an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible. Authorities subsequently sealed the complex, suspended all entry and exit movements and placed the premises under heightened security.

The attack also raised concerns over security at the judicial complex, a sensitive government facility frequented by judges, lawyers, litigants and members of the public.

Investigators are probing the motive behind the attack and working to establish the identities of the assailants.

The latest incidents come amid a series of attacks on security personnel and government officials in the province, which has witnessed growing terrorist activity and mounting security challenges in recent years.

article_text:
Fakhar Zaman struck a brilliant century to spearhead Pakistan's three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the final of the ODI tri-series at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on Saturday, as the hosts chased down a challenging 326-run target with nine balls to spare to lift the title.

Fakhar led the successful chase with a commanding 127, while Saad Baig contributed 74 and Arafat Minhas struck a quickfire 61 to help Pakistan recover from an early collapse and reach the target for the loss of seven wickets.

Fakhar, who had scored his previous century three years ago, shared a 149-run third-wicket partnership with Saad, who struck a 75-ball 74 in his maiden half-century. Saad hit 11 well-timed fours before being caught and bowled by spinner Maheesh Theekshana.

Fakhar, who scored the 12th century of his career, also completed 4,000 runs when he reached 108.

The left-hander, who brought up his century off 84 balls, then added 57 runs for the fourth wicket with Agha Salman before being bowled by pacer Dilshan Madushanka.

Fakhar struck six sixes and 11 fours in his 99-ball match-winning knock.

Dunith Wellalage then dismissed Agha Salman (17), briefly raising hopes of a Sri Lankan comeback.

However, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz thwarted that threat by sharing a 94-run sixth-wicket partnership to put the hosts in a comfortable position.

Asitha Fernando removed Arafat, who smashed a fiery 61 off 31 balls, hitting four sixes and three fours.

Fernando then dismissed Faheem Ashraf (0) with his next delivery, but Hasan and Shaheen Afridi (6 not out) completed the remaining task to seal the victory.

Hasan remained unbeaten on 37 off 45 balls, hitting two fours.

Dilshan Madushanka was the pick of the Sri Lankan bowlers, taking 3-63 in 9.3 overs.

Pakistan had made a poor start to the chase, with Madushanka removing Maaz Sadaqat (5) and Babar Azam (0) cheaply to leave the hosts in deep trouble.

Earlier, opener Kamindu Mendis struck a superb 131, while Pavan Rathnayake contributed 77 as Sri Lanka posted a competitive 325-8.

After Pakistan elected to field, Sri Lanka made a steady start through openers Avishka Fernando and Kamindu, who put on 87 runs for the first wicket.

Salman Ali Agha broke the partnership in the 18th over, trapping Fernando lbw for 38. He faced 49 balls and struck three fours and a six in his well-made knock.

Salman struck again, dismissing Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis (8) cheaply to leave his side at 109-2.

Kamindu then joined Rathnayake to rebuild the innings. The pair added 146 runs for the third wicket, putting Sri Lanka in a commanding position.

Kamindu brought up his maiden century off 107 balls, while Rathnayake reached his half-century off 47 deliveries.

The partnership ended in the 42nd over when Haris Rauf dismissed Kamindu for 131 off 128 balls. His innings included 12 fours and two sixes.

Rathnayake, who had also scored two centuries in the series, continued to score freely before falling to Rauf for 77 off 65 balls, having struck eight fours.

Sri Lanka were 255-3 when Kamindu departed. However, Pakistan fought back by taking regular wickets in the closing overs.

Dasun Shanaka struck 17 off nine balls, hitting two fours and a six, before being dismissed by Shaheen Afridi.

Janith Liyanage managed six before falling to Naseem Shah, who also removed Sahan Arachchige for 15.

Maheesh Theekshana remained unbeaten on nine, while Asitha Fernando contributed an unbeaten seven to help Sri Lanka finish with a competitive total.

Shaheen, Naseem, Agha Salman and Haris Rauf claimed two wickets each. Haris conceded 61 runs in 9.6 overs, while Naseem was the most expensive of the Pakistani bowlers, giving away 80 runs in his quota of 10 overs.

Pakistan made one change to their side, bringing in Faheem Ashraf in place of Shadab Khan.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, left out Eshan Malinga and included spinner Maheesh Theekshana to strengthen their bowling attack.

headline: Diplomacy in overdrive as Iran-US war fears mount
description: Diplomacy in overdrive as Iran-US war fears mount
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source who was briefed on the negotiations told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert new fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Trump has held off on strikes on Iran in recent weeks ahead of midterm elections that will determine whether his Republican Party will retain its thin majorities in both houses of the US Congress.

Saturday's talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that Trump could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response," Khamenei said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account. He has not appeared in public since replacing his father, who was slain at the war's outset.

Khamenei said senior commanders had reported high readiness along the Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran's northwestern and southeastern borders.

Iran's influential security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran was debating whether to lift its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons should hostilities resume, although he said no such decision had been taken. There could be no talks on Iran's nuclear programme unless Washington accepted Iran's demands, he added.

Rubio, hosting foreign ministers of the G20 major economies in Atlanta, declined to set a timeframe for the talks in Qatar, but said direct and indirect contacts with Iran were under way.

"There are multiple talks. Talks have actually never stopped," he said.

Trump would "prefer to solve it diplomatically. But I think what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," Rubio said.

DIPLOMACY CONTINUES DESPITE GAPS

Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can "finish the job".

But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to the security chief Rezaei, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it was possible to restart talks.

Trump has played the letter down, saying he approved it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: "I said if you want to do that, that's ok. Basically, it's getting supplies in to help people that are not well."

In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would take daily steps to build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.

Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade of Iranian ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which the contested strait would be reopened.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance's letter. He said the Iranian plan was the only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.

article_html:
ATLANTA/ DUBAI:

Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source who was briefed on the negotiations told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert new fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Trump has held off on strikes on Iran in recent weeks ahead of midterm elections that will determine whether his Republican Party will retain its thin majorities in both houses of the US Congress.

Saturday's talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that Trump could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response," Khamenei said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account. He has not appeared in public since replacing his father, who was slain at the war's outset.

Khamenei said senior commanders had reported high readiness along the Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran's northwestern and southeastern borders.

Iran's influential security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran was debating whether to lift its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons should hostilities resume, although he said no such decision had been taken. There could be no talks on Iran's nuclear programme unless Washington accepted Iran's demands, he added.

Rubio, hosting foreign ministers of the G20 major economies in Atlanta, declined to set a timeframe for the talks in Qatar, but said direct and indirect contacts with Iran were under way.

"There are multiple talks. Talks have actually never stopped," he said.

Trump would "prefer to solve it diplomatically. But I think what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," Rubio said.

DIPLOMACY CONTINUES DESPITE GAPS

Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can "finish the job".

But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to the security chief Rezaei, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it was possible to restart talks.

Trump has played the letter down, saying he approved it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: "I said if you want to do that, that's ok. Basically, it's getting supplies in to help people that are not well."

In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would take daily steps to build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.

Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade of Iranian ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which the contested strait would be reopened.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance's letter. He said the Iranian plan was the only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.
