headline: Syria weighs joining Makkah defence alliance
description: Syria weighs joining Makkah defence alliance
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani's remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

"Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

"How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?" he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

headline: BD death toll from dengue rises, unlikely to ease before Dec
description: The outbreak has killed 418 people and led to more than 133,000 hospital admissions this year as of Oct 30
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh recorded its highest monthly dengue death toll of the year in October, with experts warning the outbreak is unlikely to ease significantly before December.

The outbreak has killed 418 people and led to more than 133,000 hospital admissions this year as of October 30, according to health ministry data. October alone accounted for 173 deaths, surpassing September's 148 and making it the deadliest month of 2026 so far.

The surge comes as Bangladesh is also battling the world's worst measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,200 people, placing additional strain on an already stretched healthcare system.

Doctors said many dengue patients were only seeking hospital admission after developing severe complications.

At the state-run Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital in Dhaka, 279 dengue patients were being treated after 67 new admissions in a single day, hospital director Mirza Golam Sarwar said.

"We are getting many patients in shock. Their blood pressure is sometimes too low to measure, and their oxygen levels are dropping," he said. Medicine specialist ABM Abdullah said repeat infections and delays in diagnosis and treatment were driving severe cases and deaths.

"People who have had dengue before may face a greater risk of severe illness if they become infected again," he said, urging people to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek care as soon as symptoms appear. Dhaka resident Faisal Ferdous, 33, was diagnosed with dengue in 2017, 2024 and again earlier this month.

The outbreak has killed 418 people and led to more than 133,000 hospital admissions this year as of October 30, according to health ministry data. October alone accounted for 173 deaths, surpassing September's 148 and making it the deadliest month of 2026 so far.

The surge comes as Bangladesh is also battling the world's worst measles outbreak, which has killed more than 1,200 people, placing additional strain on an already stretched healthcare system.

Doctors said many dengue patients were only seeking hospital admission after developing severe complications.

At the state-run Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital in Dhaka, 279 dengue patients were being treated after 67 new admissions in a single day, hospital director Mirza Golam Sarwar said.

"We are getting many patients in shock. Their blood pressure is sometimes too low to measure, and their oxygen levels are dropping," he said. Medicine specialist ABM Abdullah said repeat infections and delays in diagnosis and treatment were driving severe cases and deaths.

"People who have had dengue before may face a greater risk of severe illness if they become infected again," he said, urging people to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek care as soon as symptoms appear. Dhaka resident Faisal Ferdous, 33, was diagnosed with dengue in 2017, 2024 and again earlier this month.

headline: Bolsonaro claims persecution in Brazil
description: He recounts how police informed him Monday that his passports were being revoked
author: AFP
article_text:
He recounts how police informed him Monday that his passports were being revoked

Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.

Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday after traveling through Argentina and Ecuador.

"The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were canceled as part of a money laundering investigation.

In the video, he recounted how police informed him Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.

"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.

"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.

Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone."

headline: Iran blinded US bases before striking military assets, AP analysis finds
description: More than 115 Iran-linked strikes damaged or destroyed structures at 26 US military bases and sites through August
author: News Desk
article_text:
Iran's strikes on more than two dozen US bases in the Middle East focused on early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage, according to an Associated Press analysis.

The AP independently verified damage to American targets using satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or have firsthand knowledge of what was hit. The AP found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-backed militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with US equipment.

The AP found that Iran initially focused its attacks on aircraft hangars and systems that detect incoming strikes, clearing the way for further strikes on warehouses, troop housing and more.

The damage has significantly reshaped the American foothold in the Middle East, with two regional officials saying the US has moved many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf. That includes aircraft, air defense systems, communications systems and other equipment crucial to base operations, one of those officials said.

The impact of the damage raises questions about American defenses in the region as President Donald Trump considers new strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections and Tehran has vowed major retaliation.

The AP's analysis found that from April 1 to June 30, Iranian strikes had damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures on US bases.

US Central Command, which oversees operations in the Middle East, has refused to comment on or specify damage to bases or equipment, usually citing the need for operational security. The command did not comment for this story.

Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell asserted that US "forces and bases are well protected and America's military is stronger than ever."

"Our service members in CENTCOM have everything they need to continue their historic success ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon," Parnell said in a statement to the AP.

Iran targeted at US bases

Most of the Iranian attacks have been in Kuwait, while US sites in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates also have been targeted, the analysis of satellite imagery shows. The deadliest known strike on US troops in the Iran war was in Kuwait, where six soldiers were killed in a drone attack at Port Shuaiba on March 1.

Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.

Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, faced even heavier losses. While Iranian attacks made most of its hangars inoperable, gathering places for troops sustained much more damage because the base had limited aircraft. Its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops to buy products on the base was hit in late July.

A strike also has severely damaged the garage and dining room there, according to the two regional officials. They and two others, who are regional military officials, spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive details about the damage to bases.

While strikes were much heavier against Iran, American matériel losses were inevitable, said Raphael Cohen, director of the National Security Program at the RAND School of Public Policy. The way wars are fought today makes all militaries "susceptible to large-scale, cheap drone attacks," he said.

"This should be a wake-up call for the United States," Cohen said.

Iran focused on targeting US systems meant to detect incoming strikes

Iran launched its response to the war with accurate attacks on systems meant to detect and thwart incoming strikes, then broadened its targets to buildings and equipment that made US bases useful and habitable.

Iran destroyed enclosures protecting US radar systems at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and Naval Support Activity Bahrain within the first two days of the war's start in late February. Additionally, Iran hit portable radars at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.

Iran prioritized striking at the backbone of the US air defense system, targeting key early-warning radars that are difficult and expensive to repair or replace, said NR Jenzen-Jones, director of the technical intelligence consulting firm Armament Research Services.

A radar was hit in Jordan and said to be destroyed. It was one of only 13 possessed by the Army globally, manufacturer Raytheon said. Budget documents show each costs about half a billion dollars.

Another radar in Qatar was damaged significantly, but it is unclear if it was destroyed. Purchased by the Gulf country in a 2013 deal valued at $1.1 billion, it appears to have been the only one in the region.

That includes aircraft, air defense systems, communications systems and other equipment crucial to base operations, one of those officials said.

The impact of the damage raises questions about American defenses in the region as President Donald Trump considers new strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections and Tehran has vowed major retaliation.
The AP's analysis found that from April 1 to June 30, Iranian strikes had damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures on US bases.

US Central Command, which oversees operations in the Middle East, has refused to comment on or specify damage to bases or equipment, usually citing the need for operational security. The command did not comment for this story.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell asserted that US "forces and bases are well protected and America's military is stronger than ever."
"Our service members in CENTCOM have everything they need to continue their historic success ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon," Parnell said in a statement to the AP.
Iran targeted at US bases

Most of the Iranian attacks have been in Kuwait, while US sites in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates also have been targeted, the analysis of satellite imagery shows. The deadliest known strike on US troops in the Iran war was in Kuwait, where six soldiers were killed in a drone attack at Port Shuaiba on March 1.
Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.

Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, faced even heavier losses. While Iranian attacks made most of its hangars inoperable, gathering places for troops sustained much more damage because the base had limited aircraft. Its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops to buy products on the base was hit in late July.

A strike also has severely damaged the garage and dining room there, according to the two regional officials. They and two others, who are regional military officials, spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive details about the damage to bases.

While strikes were much heavier against Iran, American matériel losses were inevitable, said Raphael Cohen, director of the National Security Program at the RAND School of Public Policy. The way wars are fought today makes all militaries "susceptible to large-scale, cheap drone attacks," he said.
"This should be a wake-up call for the United States," Cohen said.
Iran focused on targeting US systems meant to detect incoming strikes

Iran launched its response to the war with accurate attacks on systems meant to detect and thwart incoming strikes, then broadened its targets to buildings and equipment that made US bases useful and habitable.

Iran destroyed enclosures protecting US radar systems at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and Naval Support Activity Bahrain within the first two days of the war's start in late February. Additionally, Iran hit portable radars at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.

Iran prioritized striking at the backbone of the US air defense system, targeting key early-warning radars that are difficult and expensive to repair or replace, said NR Jenzen-Jones, director of the technical intelligence consulting firm Armament Research Services.
A radar was hit in Jordan and said to be destroyed. It was one of only 13 possessed by the Army globally, manufacturer Raytheon said. Budget documents show each costs about half a billion dollars.

Another radar in Qatar was damaged significantly, but it is unclear if it was destroyed. Purchased by the Gulf country in a 2013 deal valued at $1.1 billion, it appears to have been the only one in the region.

headline: Pindi families return to wood-fuelled cooking
description: Pindi families return to wood-fuelled cooking
author: Qaiser Shirazi
article_text:
Prolonged gas load management, with supplies available for only six hours a day, coupled with a sharp increase in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, has forced low- and middle-income households in Rawalpindi to return to firewood and coal for cooking as winter sets in.

Firewood, coal and kerosene oil are increasingly being used as fuels by middle- and low-income families, roadside eateries and small tandoors. The growing demand for firewood has also reportedly contributed to a significant increase in the theft of timber from public and private forests. Meanwhile, the prices of firewood and coal have risen sharply with the onset of winter.

In the open market, coal is selling for between Rs800 and Rs1,000 per maund. Low-smoke coal that produces a good flame costs Rs1,000 per maund, while the variety producing less heat and smoke is available for Rs800. Dry firewood, which produces less smoke and provides greater heat, is priced between Rs1,500 and Rs1,800 per maund, while ordinary firewood costs between Rs1,300 and Rs1,400. Sawdust has also reached Rs700 per maund

Sui gas supplies are being restricted to three daily intervals of two hours each, while uninterrupted outages from 9pm until Sehri have become routine. As a result, traders, large shopkeepers and affluent families have increasingly turned to gas cylinders, pushing up demand and prompting a further rise in cylinder prices.

The price of a new, empty domestic gas cylinder has increased from Rs10,000 to Rs13,500, while used cylinders are available for between Rs8,000 and Rs10,000. The cost of refilling a domestic cylinder has risen from Rs3,000 to Rs5,000.

Commercial gas cylinder refills, which cost between Rs12,500 and Rs14,000 a year ago, have now reached as much as Rs25,000, placing an additional burden on businesses.

With gas load management extending to 18-20 hours a day across the city, roadside eateries, small tandoors, hotels and bakeries have begun using firewood instead of gas. Residents and tandoor owners are also visiting furniture markets to purchase discarded wooden pieces and sawdust at lower prices.

Furniture factory owner Muhammad Faizan said that, previously, discarded wooden pieces and sawdust had been disposed of in Nullah Lai. However, the situation had changed as residents now collected the waste for use as fuel.

"We used to dispose of these wooden pieces and sawdust in Nullah Leh. Now, people come to our factory in the evening, clean the premises themselves and take the waste away," he said.

Divisional president of the All Pakistan Clerks Association, Shehzad Manzoor Kiyani, said rising inflation had brought back the era of firewood and coal. He said clerical and lower-grade government employees had reported that gas supplies were no longer reliable and monthly LPG expenses had reached Rs10,00012,000, forcing them to switch to firewood.

Teachers' leaders Basharat Iqbal Raja and Shafiq Bhalwalia said crippling inflation had compelled households to use gas cylinders for emergency cooking and making tea for guests during the day, while relying on firewood to prepare the evening meal.

headline: Sixth suspect in organ transplant case held
description: Sixth suspect in organ transplant case held
author: APP
article_text:
The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Anti-Corruption Circle Islamabad has arrested a sixth suspect in an illegal kidney transplant case and obtained his five-day physical remand from a court for further investigation.

According to an FIA official, the accused, identified as Muhammad Sohaib, owner of Ateeq Pharmacy at Haideri Chowk, Saidpur Road, Rawalpindi, was arrested during an investigation into case No. 60/2026.

The official said the suspect had allegedly been supplying medicines and surgical equipment to a gang involved in illegal kidney transplants at residential premises since 2021.

He said the accused was allegedly aware that the gang members were neither qualified doctors nor authorised medical practitioners but continued providing them with medicines and surgical supplies.

During the investigation, FIA officials obtained WhatsApp chats, voice notes and bank receipts as evidence of the suspect's alleged involvement in the illegal activities.

Meanwhile, the court also extended the physical remand of four previously arrested suspects by another two days.

headline: 'Police brutality' costs young life
description: 'Police brutality' costs young life
author: Yawar Hayat
article_text:
A young man allegedly died following police torture near Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila after a dispute over parking a vehicle on the road, prompting his family to stage a protest by placing his body on the road and blocking Museum Road to all traffic.

According to sources, allegations have emerged that police personnel beat the young man following a dispute over parking a vehicle on the road. The deceased's relatives blocked Museum Road and demanded action against the personnel allegedly involved and the provision of justice.

The family alleged that Akmal Khan died as a result of torture allegedly inflicted by police personnel. The incident has triggered widespread concern and anger in the area.

According to initial reports, the incident occurred over the parking of a vehicle on the road. An argument allegedly broke out between the police personnel and the young man, which later turned into physical violence.

The family alleged that police personnel severely tortured Akmal Khan in front of innocent children, resulting in his death. However, the actual circumstances of the incident, the nature of the alleged torture and the cause of death can only be established through an investigation by the relevant authorities and a medical report.

Following the young man's death, his relatives and local residents launched a strong protest against the police by placing his body on Taxila Museum Road.

The protest led to the closure of Museum Road to traffic, causing long queues of vehicles on both sides of the road and creating serious difficulties for commuters and passengers.

The protesters demanded a transparent investigation into the incident, legal action against the police personnel allegedly involved and that those responsible be brought to justice.

headline: Schools bring cultural heritage to classrooms
description: Schools bring cultural heritage to classrooms
author: APP
article_text:
The Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, in collaboration with the National Heritage and Culture Division, has launched the Heritage Education Initiative in Federal Directorate of Education schools to promote cultural awareness and connect students with Pakistan's heritage.

The initiative aims to integrate heritage-based learning into the educational experience of students in Classes VI to VIII through practical engagement, creative exploration, and experiential learning.

According to official sources, the pilot phase will be implemented in 10 public schools under the Federal Directorate of Education, with each school establishing a Heritage Club comprising 20 to 30 students.

Designed to complement the existing curriculum, the initiative will not introduce any additional subjects, examinations, or graded assignments. Instead, it will provide students with opportunities to explore Pakistan's cultural traditions through hands-on activities, research, observation, and creative expression.

The programme will focus on six traditional and contemporary craft areas: truck art, patchwork, jewellery making, clay pottery, rabab, and digital art.

Through these diverse forms of artistic expression, students will gain a deeper understanding of the skills, traditions, and cultural narratives that have shaped Pakistan's identity across generations.

The six-month pilot programme will follow a structured learning journey encompassing discovery, experience, creation, and showcase.

It will conclude with a student-curated exhibition, providing participants with a platform to present their work, demonstrate their learning, and share their understanding of Pakistan's cultural heritage with the wider community.

The initiative will be implemented through a phased roadmap. The first phase will focus on piloting the programme and establishing proof of concept. The second phase will concentrate on consolidation and expansion, while the third phase will aim to institutionalise the initiative and ensure its long-term sustainability within the education system.

The Heritage Education Initiative reflects the Ministry's commitment to fostering holistic education that extends beyond conventional classroom instruction.

By encouraging students to observe, question, investigate, and reinterpret cultural traditions rather than merely memorise historical facts, the programme seeks to cultivate creativity, critical thinking, cultural appreciation, and a sense of shared national identity.

Through Heritage Clubs, students will be encouraged to engage meaningfully with the tangible and intangible dimensions of Pakistan's heritage, recognise the value of traditional knowledge and craftsmanship, and explore ways to preserve and reinterpret these traditions in contemporary contexts.

headline: CCD cop, brother shot dead
description: CCD cop, brother shot dead
author: Aurangzeb Abbasi
article_text:
Two brothers were shot dead over a land dispute in Changla Gali Tajwal, an area of Galiyat adjoining Murree in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

A third brother, Shahzad, also died of a heart attack after attending the funeral of the two brothers

The deceased were identified as Tahseen Shah, a head constable with the Crime Control Department (CCD), Rawalpindi, and his brother Khizar Abbas.

Police have arrested Manzoor Shah, the suspect allegedly involved in the double murder. He is a cousin of the deceased.

The tragic incident occurred suddenly while negotiations over the land dispute were under way and several other people were also present at the site.

Police shifted the bodies to a nearby hospital for post-mortem examinations. The suspect in the double murder has been arrested.

A third brother, Shahzad, also died of a heart attack after attending the funeral of the two brothers.

According to sources, Shahzad suffered a heart attack at Mochi Dhara Hospital after seeing the funeral of his two brothers. The attack proved fatal.

Thus, what began as a minor land dispute claimed the lives of three young men from the same family.

Their funeral prayers were offered at Railway Ground in Rawalpindi. They were later buried at Dhoke Ratta graveyard.

CCD Regional Officer Hassan Wattoo, other senior officers, police personnel, relatives of the deceased and a large number of citizens attended the funeral prayers.

headline: Call to vaccinate girls against cervical cancer
description: Call to vaccinate girls against cervical cancer
author: APP
article_text:
.

Health authorities have urged parents to ensure that their daughters receive the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine under the cervical cancer prevention campaign, describing early vaccination as a vital step towards protecting girls against the disease.

The Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) has encouraged parents to make informed decisions about their daughters' health and take advantage of the preventive vaccination programme.

Health experts explain that the HPV vaccine protects against the types of human papillomavirus responsible for most cases of cervical cancer. Vaccination at the recommended age of nine to 14 years provides the best protection, ideally before exposure to the virus.

Cervical cancer develops in the cervix, the lower part of the uterus, and is largely preventable through HPV vaccination and appropriate screening later in life.

headline: Halle Berry loses bid for equal custody as judge rejects Martinez's restraining order
description: Halle Berry retains joint legal custody of son Maceo but has limited physical custody following court ruling
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Halle Berry has been temporarily denied her request for equal custody and overnight visits with her 13-year-old son, Maceo, following the latest ruling in her legal dispute with former husband Olivier Martinez.

On October 29, Los Angeles Superior Court judge Shelley Kaufman dismissed Martinez's request for a domestic violence restraining order against Berry.

However, the judge also declined Berry's requests for 50/50 custody and overnight visits, leaving the temporary custody arrangement in place while further proceedings continue.

Martinez had accused the actress of physically abusing their son during an alleged incident on September 26.

According to court documents, he claimed Berry "attacked" Maceo by "jumping on him, putting her hands around his neck, and choking him". He also alleged previous instances of abuse and sought sole legal and physical custody.

Berry has denied the allegations. Following the ruling, her attorney, Marina Beck, told USA TODAY, "We are extremely pleased that the Court has dissolved the TRO. As we move forward, Halle is determined to continue to focus on the well-being and best interests of her family."

Martinez's lawyer, Patrick Baghdaserians, described his client's continued primary physical custody as a "huge victory", according to TMZ.

The dispute follows the former couple's divorce, which was finalised in 2023 after an eight-year legal process. They had previously agreed to joint legal and physical custody, with Martinez receiving $8,000 a month in child support.

Berry's daughter, Nahla Aubry, also submitted a written declaration supporting her mother on October 3. She described Martinez's allegations as inconsistent with the parent she had known, writing that she was "shocked, very sad, and very upset" by the claims.

Nahla called Berry "a loving and devoted parent" and said she had never observed anything abusive about her mother's parenting. She also expressed concern that Maceo had become the subject of a public dispute.

headline: Rockstar reportedly planning GTA 6 Nike sneaker collaboration with Travis Scott
description: Rockstar, Nike and Travis Scott are reportedly preparing three GTA 6-themed Air Force 1 designs
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Rockstar Games is reportedly collaborating with rapper Travis Scott and Nike on a collection of Grand Theft Auto 6-themed sneakers, expected to launch alongside the highly anticipated game in November.

The reported partnership would bring together Rockstar, Nike and Scott’s streetwear brand, Cactus Jack.

The collaboration is expected to form part of the marketing surrounding GTA 6, which is scheduled for release on November 19 2026.

Rockstar has been increasing promotional activity ahead of the launch, with reported marketing events across Miami and the release of singles from the game’s soundtrack album.

Travis Scott is among the artists featured on the soundtrack, providing a potential connection to the rumoured sneaker collection.

Three Nike Air Force 1 colourways reportedly planned

Sneaker Market Romania, described as the country’s largest sneaker community, first shared details of the reported collaboration.

According to the website, the shoes are expected to appear in Nike’s Holiday 2026 seasonal catalogue, which covers the October-to-December period.

The collection is reportedly based on the Nike Air Force 1 Low and will feature three colourways: Black/Fire Pink, White/Fire Pink and Multi-Color. Each pair is expected to retail for $130, with November 19 listed as the anticipated release date.

Neither Rockstar Games nor Nike has officially confirmed the collaboration or its reported launch details.

Sneaker publication Sole Retriever has also reported on the potential partnership, adding that an accompanying clothing collection is in development.

The report also suggests that a collaboration involving the NBA’s Miami Heat franchise could be part of the wider project.

headline: The Elder Scrolls 6 reportedly titled Sentinel, with Hammerfell setting
description: The Elder Scrolls 6 may be called Sentinel and reportedly take players to Hammerfell
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Bethesda’s long-awaited role-playing game The Elder Scrolls 6 could soon receive its official subtitle, with a new report suggesting the game will be called The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel and take place in the province of Hammerfell.

According to The Verge journalist Tom Warren, who shared the information in his Notepad newsletter on October 29, sources familiar with Bethesda’s plans have identified Sentinel as the game’s official title.

Warren also reported that Xbox-owned Bethesda could announce the name as early as November, potentially coinciding with the 15th anniversary of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim on November 11.

The game was first announced in June 2018, but Bethesda has shared few details about its development since then.

Even during Xbox’s September restructuring, which saw Obsidian moved under Bethesda, The Elder Scrolls 6 remained largely out of the public eye.

Hammerfell reportedly serves as the setting

Warren’s report also provided details about the game’s setting and story. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will reportedly take players to Hammerfell, a province previously featured in The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard and The Elder Scrolls Online.

The game is also expected to explore the history of the Elder Scrolls themselves, the mysterious ancient artefacts that give the franchise its name.

The reported title had already attracted attention from fans in August, after Xbox CEO Asha Sharma shared a post referring to the game as “The Elder Scrolls VI: ********”. Fans counted the eight asterisks and suggested Sentinel, the name of a Redguard kingdom and port city in Hammerfell, as the missing subtitle.

Former Bethesda writer Michael Kirkbride added to the speculation by replying “Yep” to a Reddit post discussing the theory. However, Bethesda has not officially confirmed the title or the reported setting.

headline: 15 medicines found substandard, counterfeit
description: 15 medicines found substandard, counterfeit
author: Tufail Ahmed
article_text:
Medicines that promise relief may be offering little more than a false assurance, as laboratory tests have exposed 15 substandard, counterfeit and unregistered pharmaceutical products being sold at medical stores in the metropolitan city.

The flagged products include commonly used antibiotics, painkillers, eye and ear preparations, mouthwashes, baby-care products and other medicines. Chemical analysis revealed that ingredients declared on their packaging were not present in the products, raising concerns about the quality of medicines.

Director of the Sindh Drug Testing Laboratory Syed Adnan Rizvi told The Express Tribune on Friday that drug inspectors had collected 15 samples from medical stores in Karachi's south and central districts and sent them for chemical examination.

The laboratory found all 15 samples to be substandard and counterfeit, with some also classified as unregistered, he said.

The products identified include Baby Eye Care, Tobramycin Ophthalmic Solution, Total Care Mouthwash, Magic Lotion, Anti Plaque Mouthwash, Denziclor Mouthwash, Happy Tooth Kid Mouthwash, Babycare Ear Cream and Vital Ear Cream.

The list also includes five medicines: the antibiotics Velosef and Augmentin, the painkiller Nospa Forte, Mucaine syrup and Brexin tablets.

According to Rizvi, the chemical composition of the tested products did not match the ingredients declared on their packagings, indicating that the medicines did not contain the specified active ingredients.

In a letter dated October 28, 2026, signed by Rizvi, the laboratory declared the products substandard, counterfeit and unregistered under the Drugs Act 1976 and the DRAP Act 2012.

The letter has also been forwarded to the provincial drug inspector and the secretary of the Sindh Quality Control Board for further action.

Warning about the potential consequences, Rizvi said substandard medicines might fail to produce the desired therapeutic effect and, in some cases, could prove harmful to patients.

The findings have raised concerns about the sale of potentially ineffective medicines through retail pharmacies, particularly antibiotics, whose inadequate or absent active ingredients could leave infections untreated.

The laboratory's findings have also placed the spotlight on drug inspection and regulatory enforcement, with further action required against the sale and distribution of the identified products.

headline: Four fishermen die mysteriously after month-long fishing trip
description: All four died on separate days during treatment within a span of a week with no injury marks
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
A total of four fishermen from Rehri Goth died under mysterious circumstances days after returning from a month-long fishing trip at sea.

SHO Sukhan Irfan Ali Sehto said the fishermen - identified as Hashim, Hussain, Usman and Siddique - had gone for fishing for a month and returned to Rehri Goth. Soon after their return, their health deteriorated and they were initially taken to a private hospital and later to Jinnah Hospital.

All four died on separate days during treatment within a span of a week, the SHO said, adding that no injury marks or signs of torture were found on their bodies. Doctors termed the deaths as natural, he added.

A video statement of the niece of one of the deceased also surfaced. She said that five persons including her maternal uncle, cousin and other relatives had gone for fishing in the sea. After returning, they complained of abdominal pain. She said they were first taken to a nearby private hospital and after check-up returned home.

Later when they complained about pain again, they were taken to another private hospital and on doctors' advice shifted to Jinnah Hospital, where doctors diagnosed kidney and heart-related complications. They were admitted and died during the treatment.

SHO Sehto said further investigation into the incident is underway.

A day ago, 11 fishermen reunited with their families after their return from Indian prisons. The fishermen arrived in Karachi after being transported from the Wagah border in Lahore.

Among those returning were six fishermen from Mauripur - 28-year-old Muhammad Sharif Bengali, 35-year-old Noorul Amin Bangal, Kamal Hussain Bengali and Noor Nabi Bengali, 36-year-old Ameer Hussain Bengali, and 41-year-old Azeemuddin Bengali.

headline: AVCC official suspended for failing to recover abductee, taking bribe
description: AVCC official suspended for failing to recover abductee, taking bribe
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
An investigation officer of the Anti-Violent Crime Cell (AVCC) has been suspended following a complaint by the father of Zainul Abideen, who was kidnapped from Steel Town and brutally murdered, over allegations that the officer had taken bribes from him.

Speaking to The Express Tribune, the victim's father, Muhammad Khan, accused IO Rizwan of receiving a total of Rs22,000 from him, including Rs2,000 allegedly taken in the name of food expenses.

He said that while his son had been brutally murdered after being kidnapped, the conduct of the investigation officer had added to the family's distress. According to him, the officer had met him only three times and had shown little interest in the case. As a result, the ransom money and other belongings had not been recovered from the suspects, he alleged.

Muhammad Khan said he lodged a complaint with DIG CIA Muqaddas Haider on Thursday, accusing the investigator of negligence and dereliction of duty. Following the meeting, the DIG suspended IO Rizwan and appointed a new investigation officer. However, the newly-appointed officer had not contacted the family so far, he added.

The grieving father demanded a transparent and impartial investigation. He said the family had paid Rs500,000 in ransom in an attempt to secure his son's release, but he was not recovered. To intimidate the family, the kidnappers had also sent them a severed hand of his son, he alleged.

Muhammad Khan appealed to the Sindh home minister and the provincial police chief to ensure justice for his family.

According to the case details, Zainul Abideen, who had returned from Saudi Arabia, went missing under mysterious circumstances from Steel Town on October 14. Steel Town police registered a kidnapping-for-ransom case on October 15 and transferred the investigation to the AVCC.

His body was recovered by AVCC police on October 16 from Chhatri Ground in Bin Qasim on the identification of the arrested suspects. One of the suspects, Faisal, is a close relative of the victim. Police arrested him along with his accomplice, Ansar.

headline: Suspect involved in short-term kidnapping of jeweller held
description: Suspect involved in short-term kidnapping of jeweller held
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Ferozabad police have arrested a suspected member of a gang involved in the short-term kidnapping of a gold trader and recovered a pistol, ammunition, Rs120,000 in cash and other belongings from his possession.

According to details, Ferozabad police and Shaheen Force jointly conducted an operation near the main gate of Jheel Park in PECHS Block 2 during the night between Friday and Saturday. A suspect travelling in a vehicle bearing registration number LA-7676 was arrested.

A pistol with bullets, a wallet containing Rs120,000, a CNIC issued in the name of the suspect, Aitbar Khan, son of Zarnab Khan, several visiting cards and a mobile phone were recovered from him.

The arrested suspect, Aitbar Khan, was an important member of a gang involved in several short-term kidnapping incidents in Karachi.

He said the suspect and his accomplices had kidnapped a gold trader on October 27, 2026, and released him after snatching cash, weapons and mobile phones.

The complainant, Nauman Hussain, told police that he lived on Tipu Sultan Road in Bahadurabad and owned a jewellery shop on Tariq Road.

According to his statement, he was returning home after closing his shop on October 27 and was heading towards Kashmir Road in his car (AZB-826) to refuel it.

headline: DNA test identifies minor girl found dead
description: DNA test identifies minor girl found dead
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
.

The decomposed body of seven-year-old Ayesha Gulalai, found without clothes and stuffed in a sack near a wedding hall on Mehran Highway in Quaidabad on August 19, has been identified through DNA testing.

Ayesha had gone missing from Quaidabad on August 13. At the time, police showed her family the unidentified body recovered from a drain, but they failed to recognise it.

Then-SHO Quaidabad Gulzar Tino had said that the body was shown to the girl's family, but they could not identify her.

headline: New administrative units inevitable: Mustafa Kamal
description: New administrative units inevitable: Mustafa Kamal
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal has said Pakistan cannot be governed under the existing administrative model and that the creation of new administrative units has become inevitable.

Speaking at an event organised by the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (KATI) on Saturday, Kamal said he has reached the conclusion, after years of struggle, that raising complaints about Karachi has become futile as nobody seemed to care.

"The people of Karachi earn and contribute, yet they still have to beg the federal government for their rights," he said, adding that the federal bureaucracy in Islamabad was displeased with the presence of Karachiites.

"I honestly believe the existing government system cannot work. The longer we delay the creation of new administrative units, the greater the damage will be," he said, adding that the issue was now being taken seriously, which was why opponents had adopted a harsher tone.

The federal minister said pharmaceutical companies previously had to pay hefty bribes to register medicines with Drap. Under the new system, every document was processed automatically.

He said barcodes had been introduced for 86,000 branded products manufactured by 650 pharmaceutical companies, while the ministry's database now contained information on 86,000 medicines.

headline: Pregnant woman among three killed in road mishaps
description: Pregnant woman among three killed in road mishaps
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
As many as three persons, including a pregnant woman, were killed and three others injured in separate road accidents on Saturday.

In a first incident, a speeding trailer ran over a motorcycle carrying a married couple near Liaquatabad on Saturday, killing a pregnant woman and injuring her husband.

The accident triggered an angry reaction from residents, who pelted the trailer with stones, smashed its windows and eventually set it on fire. The driver fled the scene.

The woman was identified as Faiza, while her husband, Faheem, was given initial medical treatment before being transferred to Jinnah Hospital.

In another incident, a motorcyclist was killed after being hit by a water tanker near Jamali Bridge on the Superhighway. The deceased was indentified as 40-year-old Muhammad Asif. The tanker driver fled the scene.

Meanwhile, a car occupant was killed when a trailer rammed into his vehicle in Baldia.

The body was shifted to Civil Hospital. Chhipa officials identified the deceased as 55-year-old Muhammad Barkat, a resident of Hub Chowki.

headline: Sindh working on master plans for 31 cities: CM
description: Sindh working on master plans for 31 cities: CM
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah said on Saturday that the provincial government was working on master plans for 31 cities across the province, including major urban centres such as Karachi and Hyderabad, to ensure planned, sustainable and inclusive urban development.

Addressing the Sindh Cities Forum 2026, organised by the Sindh Master Plan Authority (SMPA) in collaboration with NED University and UN-Habitat at the Convention Centre of the Golf Club on the occasion of World Cities Day, the chief minister said master planning was essential to address growing urban challenges, including unplanned construction, traffic congestion, water shortages, inadequate drainage systems and the effects of climate change.

According to the minister for local government, housing and town planning, master plans for 17 cities had been completed, while work on the remaining 14 was in its final stages. The government has so far issued notifications for the master plans of nine cities: Sukkur, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, Umerkot, Mithi, Islamkot, Dadu, Nawabshah and Naushahro Feroze.

The CM said work on the master plans for Karachi and Hyderabad was progressing rapidly. International consultants had been engaged to prepare Karachi's master plan, which, he acknowledged, would be a particularly challenging exercise given the city's existing urban conditions.

Preparing a master plan for a new city from scratch was relatively easy, he said, adding that correcting Karachi's existing situation was a major challenge for consultants and urban planners. He urged them to propose measures not only to improve the city's condition but also to ensure effective implementation of the plan.

Recalling his personal association with Karachi, the chief minister said he had witnessed the city's rapid expansion. However, its growth had also exposed serious planning failures, making subsequent efforts to improve urban infrastructure increasingly difficult.

Referring to the 2020 monsoon floods in Yousuf Goth, District West, he said roads originally designed with adequate carriageways, central medians and storm-water drains had subsequently been encroached upon. Shops had been established on service roads, medians and drainage channels, damaging the original infrastructure.

He acknowledged that successive governments, including his own, had made mistakes that had contributed to the city's present condition. Once structural problems develop in a city, correcting them becomes extremely difficult, he said, stressing that the government could not address urban challenges without the cooperation of citizens, planners, builders, utility companies and other stakeholders.

Addressing the Sindh Cities Forum 2026, organised by the Sindh Master Plan Authority (SMPA) in collaboration with NED University and UN-Habitat at the Convention Centre of the Golf Club on the occasion of World Cities Day, the chief minister said master planning was essential to address growing urban challenges, including unplanned construction, traffic congestion, water shortages, inadequate drainage systems and the effects of climate change.

According to the minister for local government, housing and town planning, master plans for 17 cities had been completed, while work on the remaining 14 was in its final stages. The government has so far issued notifications for the master plans of nine cities: Sukkur, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, Umerkot, Mithi, Islamkot, Dadu, Nawabshah and Naushahro Feroze.

The CM said work on the master plans for Karachi and Hyderabad was progressing rapidly. International consultants had been engaged to prepare Karachi's master plan, which, he acknowledged, would be a particularly challenging exercise given the city's existing urban conditions.

Preparing a master plan for a new city from scratch was relatively easy, he said, adding that correcting Karachi's existing situation was a major challenge for consultants and urban planners. He urged them to propose measures not only to improve the city's condition but also to ensure effective implementation of the plan.

Recalling his personal association with Karachi, the chief minister said he had witnessed the city's rapid expansion. However, its growth had also exposed serious planning failures, making subsequent efforts to improve urban infrastructure increasingly difficult.

Referring to the 2020 monsoon floods in Yousuf Goth, District West, he said roads originally designed with adequate carriageways, central medians and storm-water drains had subsequently been encroached upon. Shops had been established on service roads, medians and drainage channels, damaging the original infrastructure.

He acknowledged that successive governments, including his own, had made mistakes that had contributed to the city's present condition. Once structural problems develop in a city, correcting them becomes extremely difficult, he said, stressing that the government could not address urban challenges without the cooperation of citizens, planners, builders, utility companies and other stakeholders.

headline: Demolition of illegal construction on park land ordered
description: Court seeks a compliance report from the deputy commissioner east and revenue authorities by January 20
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Sindh High Court has ordered the removal of encroachments and illegal constructions from a park in Scheme 33, where land, allegedly reserved for public recreation, was occupied and buildings erected.

Petitioner's counsel, Usman Farooq Advocate, argued that the illegal constructions posed a serious threat to human lives. He said K-Electric installations were also located at the site and the power utility had written to the relevant authorities warning of potential hazards caused by the construction work.

The counsel requested the court to order the immediate demolition of illegal structures in Sector 15-A and restrain the builder from carrying out further construction and booking units in the building.

The court observed that the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) should assist the relevant authorities in removing encroachments and restoring the park.

The court also sought a compliance report from the deputy commissioner east and revenue authorities by January 20.

Meanwhile, a Malir civil court has directed its court bailiff to get an eight-acre plot worth hundreds of millions of rupees in Scheme 33 vacated with police assistance within seven days.

Two brothers, Haris and Hamza, had approached the Model Civil Court Malir against the alleged illegal occupation of their valuable land.

In their petition, they submitted that land grabbers had occupied their eight-acre property in Scheme 33 and alleged that the police were also assisting the encroachers. The court ordered the SSP east to provide the necessary police force to facilitate the implementation of the order.

headline: SHC partially allows appeal of 'RAW agent'
description: SHC partially allows appeal of 'RAW agent'
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Sindh High Court has partially allowed an appeal filed by an alleged Indian intelligence agency RAW agent against his life imprisonment sentence, setting aside several convictions and reducing one of his sentences.

In its verdict, the high court overturned the life sentence awarded to accused Muhammad Saleem on charges of conspiring against the state and committing armed aggression. It also set aside his conviction under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

The court commuted his life sentence for possessing explosives to 10 years in prison. However, it upheld his 10-year imprisonment and fine for possession of illegal weapons.

The court observed that the prosecution had failed to produce credible evidence to establish the alleged links of the accused with RAW or his involvement in a conspiracy against Pakistan.

His travel history showing visits to India, by itself, did not establish his association with RAW or prove a conspiracy against the state, the court noted.

The prosecution also failed to present evidence of any conspiracy, communication with alleged accomplices or preparations to wage war against the state, it added.

headline: Jake Paul confirms boxing return for Christmas Eve fight in Dubai
description: Jake Paul will return to boxing on December 24, more than year after breaking his jaw against Anthony Joshua
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to professional boxing on December 24, ending an absence of more than a year following the broken jaw he suffered in his December 2025 fight against former heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer will compete in Dubai on Christmas Eve, although his opponent has not yet been announced. Paul said there were several potential names being considered but that a contract was still to be signed.

“We’ve got plenty of names on the list; let’s see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody’s getting knocked out,” he said.

Jake Paul returns after Anthony Joshua defeat

Paul last fought in December 2025, when he faced British boxer Joshua in what was considered one of the toughest challenges of his boxing career. Joshua knocked Paul down in the fifth round before securing a knockout victory in the sixth.

The defeat left Paul with a broken jaw. He subsequently suggested that he might never fight again, particularly while his injury had not fully healed. His latest announcement confirms that he intends to return to the ring.

Paul currently holds a professional boxing record of 12 wins and two defeats. Several potential opponents have previously been linked to him, including KSI, Tommy Fury and former UFC fighter Darren Till.

Fury handed Paul his first professional defeat, and the pair have continued exchanging remarks about a possible rematch.

KSI has also been linked to a potential fight with Paul following their long-running rivalry, which began through their YouTube careers. However, KSI has said he has retired from boxing.

Till remains another name associated with a possible bout, having moved into boxing after leaving the UFC. For now, Paul's opponent for the Dubai event remains unconfirmed.

headline: Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem's son makes acting debut in queer Netflix drama
description: Leo Bardem, 15, appears in small scene in his mother’s queer Spanish-language drama 'La Bola Negra'
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem’s 15-year-old son, Leo, has made his acting debut in La Bola Negra, a Spanish-language drama starring his mother that is now streaming on Netflix.

Viewers spotted Leo in a small ensemble scene towards the end of the film. Although he has no dialogue, his appearance marks his first known acting role.

The teenager's involvement also comes as his parents have continued to keep their children's lives largely private.

Cruz and Bardem, who also have a 12-year-old daughter, Luna, have previously said they want their children to decide for themselves whether they wish to pursue careers in the public eye.

During a 2024 interview with Elle, Cruz declined to confirm whether her children had inherited their parents' creative interests, saying, "It's for them to decide if they are going to have a job that is more exposed to the public or not. They can talk about that when they're ready."

Leo previously accompanied his mother to a BAFTA Q&A in 2023, where she acknowledged his presence, telling the audience, "I'm very nervous today because somebody very, very special to me is in this room, my son."

Directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, collectively known as Los Javis, La Bola Negra follows three men across three generations, with its stories set in 1932, 1937 and 2017.

The film draws inspiration from Federico García Lorca's unfinished 1936 play of the same name, as well as Alberto Conejero's 2015 play La piedra oscura. Calvo, Ambrossi and Conejero collaborated on the screenplay.

The film premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, where its directors won Best Director. It has also been submitted by Spain for consideration in the Best International Feature Film category at the 2027 Oscars.

Alongside Cruz, the cast includes Spanish musician Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González and Glenn Close. Cruz also returns to singing on screen, something she last did in the 2009 film Nine.

Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem’s 15-year-old son, Leo, has made his acting debut in La Bola Negra, a Spanish-language drama starring his mother that is now streaming on Netflix.

Viewers spotted Leo in a small ensemble scene towards the end of the film. Although he has no dialogue, his appearance marks his first known acting role.

The teenager's involvement also comes as his parents have continued to keep their children's lives largely private.

Cruz and Bardem, who also have a 12-year-old daughter, Luna, have previously said they want their children to decide for themselves whether they wish to pursue careers in the public eye.

During a 2024 interview with Elle, Cruz declined to confirm whether her children had inherited their parents' creative interests, saying, "It's for them to decide if they are going to have a job that is more exposed to the public or not. They can talk about that when they're ready."

Leo previously accompanied his mother to a BAFTA Q&A in 2023, where she acknowledged his presence, telling the audience, "I'm very nervous today because somebody very, very special to me is in this room, my son."

The film premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, where its directors won Best Director. It has also been submitted by Spain for consideration in the Best International Feature Film category at the 2027 Oscars.

Alongside Cruz, the cast includes Spanish musician Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González and Glenn Close. Cruz also returns to singing on screen, something she last did in the 2009 film Nine.

headline: Uniforms made mandatory for medics
description: Uniforms made mandatory for medics
author: Adnan Lodhi
article_text:
Hospitals in Punjab had been ordered to ensure that doctors, paramedical and other employees wear prescribed uniforms while performing their duties to improve infection prevention, patient safety and professional accountability.

The directive, issued under Section 4(2) of the Punjab Healthcare Commission (PHC) Act 2010, applies to facilities having more than 30 beds.

The commission has placed responsibility on the healthcare facilities to ensure that employees falling within the specified categories are provided appropriate professional attire and not allowed to perform duty without it.

Under the instructions, healthcare establishments must provide standard uniforms to janitorial and sanitation personnel, overalls to doctors and designated kits to employees working in operation theatres and rooms where specialised medical procedures are conducted.

Standard uniforms have also been made necessary for paramedical staff.

The commission emphasised that uniform requirements should not be treated merely as an administrative formality but as part of efforts to improve healthcare standards, infection control practices and help patients distinguish between different categories of medical personnel.

The PHC has encouraged healthcare establishments to adopt the 'bare below elbow' policy while providing patient care. The approach is intended to support better hand and forearm hygiene and reduce the risk of microorganisms spreading through contact during clinical procedures. Healthcare facilities are expected to incorporate appropriate infection prevention practices into their institutional arrangements.

The commission stressed that scrubs and white coats should not be worn outside healthcare premises. The restriction aims to prevent professional clothing used in clinical environments from being carried into public spaces where it could become exposed to contaminants.

The healthcare establishments were urged to consider a colour-coded uniform arrangement to distinguish professional roles. Such a system makes it easier for patients and attendants to identify doctors, paramedical and other hospital personnel, particularly in emergency and outpatient departments.

headline: EPA faces scrutiny as Faisalabad AQI reaches 220
description: EPA faces scrutiny as Faisalabad AQI reaches 220
author: Khawar Randhawa
article_text:
The deputy commissioner has sought an explanation from the Deputy Director of the Environment Protection Agency (EPA) over persistent delays in submitting reports, lack of coordination and failure to take action against sources of air pollution.

In a letter addressed to the EPA deputy director, the officer has been directed to submit a written explanation, supported by relevant facts and documentary evidence, within three days, explaining why administrative action should not be recommended against him for alleged non-compliance with official instructions.

According to sources, the letter states that a review meeting held on October 22, highlighted serious concerns over the EPA office's performance. Despite repeated instructions, reminders and verbal counselling through the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Enforcement), the deputy director had allegedly failed to submit required reports within the prescribed deadlines.

The letter further states that the counselling had not resulted in any noticeable improvement in the department's performance or compliance with official directions.

It also points out that despite repeated sharing of information about brick kilns and industrial units emitting black smoke and contributing to air pollution, the EPA had failed to take satisfactory enforcement action or submit timely reports on the measures taken.

The deputy commissioner observed that the agency's alleged failure to respond to official directions and maintain effective coordination was affecting administrative monitoring, accountability and the timely resolution of environmental complaints.

The letter also expresses concern over slow progress in installing cameras at industrial boilers and chimneys across Faisalabad district, despite the availability of two assistant directors, 18 inspectors and other supporting staff.

It describes the delays and lack of progress as a matter of serious administrative concern.

The deputy director has been asked to explain the alleged failure to submit reports on time, take enforcement action against identified brick kilns and industrial units, and ensure the installation of cameras at industrial boilers and chimneys.

Meanwhile, Faisalabad continued to face hazardous air pollution as colder weather set in. The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was reported at 220 on Saturday, placing it in the very unhealthy category.

Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) was identified as the primary pollutant, with a concentration of 145 micrograms per cubic metre.

Localised monitoring stations, including those near Government College University and Gulistan Colony, reportedly recorded AQI levels exceeding 300.

The EPA also issued a health advisory, urging children, older people and those with heart or lung conditions to avoid outdoor physical activity.

The general public was advised to limit prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion, wear N95 or equivalent masks and keep windows closed to reduce exposure to polluted air.

headline: CM invites French investment
description: CM invites French investment
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has invited French investors to explore opportunities in agriculture, industrial and livestock sectors through the Punjab Innovation, Value Addition and Economic Transformation (PIVOT) initiative.

The chief minister met new French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier to explore avenues for strengthening bilateral relations, enhancing trade and investment and expanding industrial cooperation between Punjab and France.

She warmly welcomed the ambassador on his arrival in Lahore, congratulated him on assuming his new diplomatic responsibilities and appreciated his diplomatic services.

During the meeting, both sides discussed opportunities to enhance economic, commercial and investment cooperation between Pakistan and France, with a focus on developing stronger provincial-level partnerships with Punjab.

Invited French investors to explore investment opportunities in Punjab's agriculture, industrial and livestock sectors through the PIVOT initiative, she emphasised that greater engagement with French companies could open new avenues for industrial development, technology transfer and economic growth.

The ambassador invited the chief minister to visit France to explore opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and economic relations.

CM Maryam Nawaz thanked him for the invitation and expressed her interest in strengthening commercial and industrial ties between the two sides.

The meeting also focused on Pakistan's GSP+ European Union (EU) preferential trade status and its significance for the country's exports and industrial economy.

The chief minister described the arrangement as a lifeline for Pakistan's exports, particularly for Punjab's textile, garments, sports goods and leather industries, which depend heavily on access to European markets.

She stressed that France's support was important for safeguarding Pakistan's trade interests within the EU and maintaining preferential access for Pakistani products.

She said alignment with the requirements of the new GSP+ framework was essential for securing the country's export prospects.

The chief minister met new French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier to explore avenues for strengthening bilateral relations, enhancing trade and investment and expanding industrial cooperation between Punjab and France.

She warmly welcomed the ambassador on his arrival in Lahore, congratulated him on assuming his new diplomatic responsibilities and appreciated his diplomatic services.

During the meeting, both sides discussed opportunities to enhance economic, commercial and investment cooperation between Pakistan and France, with a focus on developing stronger provincial-level partnerships with Punjab.

Invited French investors to explore investment opportunities in Punjab's agriculture, industrial and livestock sectors through the PIVOT initiative, she emphasised that greater engagement with French companies could open new avenues for industrial development, technology transfer and economic growth.

The ambassador invited the chief minister to visit France to explore opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and economic relations.

CM Maryam Nawaz thanked him for the invitation and expressed her interest in strengthening commercial and industrial ties between the two sides.

The meeting also focused on Pakistan's GSP+ European Union (EU) preferential trade status and its significance for the country's exports and industrial economy.

The chief minister described the arrangement as a lifeline for Pakistan's exports, particularly for Punjab's textile, garments, sports goods and leather industries, which depend heavily on access to European markets.

She stressed that France's support was important for safeguarding Pakistan's trade interests within the EU and maintaining preferential access for Pakistani products.

She said alignment with the requirements of the new GSP+ framework was essential for securing the country's export prospects.

CM Maryam Nawaz noted that the EU was Pakistan's largest trading partner, with exports to the bloc reaching $8.96 billion in 2025-26.

headline: Murder convict acquitted after 3 years
description: Murder convict acquitted after 3 years
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
The Lahore High Court has acquitted a man serving a life sentence in a murder case, granting him the benefit of doubt over serious flaws in the police investigation and contradictions in the prosecution evidence.

Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq allowed the appeal filed by Salman Ahmad and set aside his life imprisonment and other sentences, declaring that the prosecution had failed to establish his guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

In its written judgment, the court observed that the complainant's testimony had lost credibility as he had failed to establish his presence at the crime scene.

It also noted that the police had failed to record statements of key witnesses and obtain CCTV footage, despite their importance to the investigation.

According to the case record, Salman was accused of stabbing Nabeel Ahmad, causing injuries to which he succumbed while being taken to a hospital.

The court also directed the Punjab prosecutor general to take action over the poor prosecution of the case and issue guidelines across the province to prevent similar lapses in criminal investigations and prosecutions.

Misri Shah police had registered the murder case in 2023.

headline: Man accuses son of Rs380m gold theft 'for love'
description: Son was secretly taking gold from their house, handing it over to his girlfriend's family, who allegedly sold it
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Son was secretly taking gold from their house, handing it over to his girlfriend's family, who allegedly sold it

A love affair has allegedly turned into a case of Rs380 million worth of theft lodged by a businessman accusing his son and four members of his girlfriend's family of stealing 70 tola of gold from his home in Kot Lakhpat.

According to the FIR registered at Kot Lakhpat police station, the complainant, Ali Rehman, alleged that his son, Oman, had been secretly removing gold jewellery from their house and handing it over to his girlfriend's family, who allegedly sold it to goldsmiths in Lahore and Kasur.

The complainant said his wife had kept approximately 70 tolas of gold jewellery in a handbag in a cupboard at their home. The theft came to light when the couple checked the bag and found the jewellery missing.

Rehman said he became suspicious of his son and questioned him about the missing valuables.

The suspect said he had been in a relationship with the woman and wanted to marry her.

According to the FIR, he told his father that the woman's family had asked him to steal valuables from his home and hand them over for sale.

The family allegedly told him that, being a young man, he would not be able to sell the jewellery himself.

The complainant alleged that the suspect subsequently removed the jewellery in parts and handed it over to the family members who sold it through their contacts in Lahore and Kasur.

headline: PHC seeks replies from governor, speaker against governor's rule
description: PH seeks replies from governor, speaker against governor's rule
author: Yasir Ali
article_text:
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General's Office has issued notices to the governor and other relevant authorities, including the provincial assembly speaker, seeking detailed replies and comments on separate writ petitions challenging the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in parts of the province.

The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor's rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.

The petitioners argued that the situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa was not beyond the control of the provincial government to warrant such extraordinary measures. They maintained that the federal government had exceeded its constitutional authority by imposing emergency and governor's rule, effectively depriving an elected provincial government and its representatives of their powers.

The petitions further stated that governor's rule could only be imposed in exceptional circumstances when the situation in a province deteriorated beyond control, with the provincial government itself expected to recommend such action.

They also challenged the invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces, arguing that the deployment of troops in aid of civil administration fell within the provincial government's domain. The petitioners alleged that several constitutional requirements had been disregarded while taking these decisions.

Meanwhile, the Advocate General's Office has directed the governor, chief secretary, provincial assembly speaker and secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department to submit their respective reports and comments before the court through officers of Grade 17 or above by November 7.

However, questions have been raised over how the provincial assembly speaker would submit his response, as the provincial government maintains that he is currently in protective custody. The Advocate General's Office has also been informed of the situation.

The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor's rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.

The petitioners argued that the situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa was not beyond the control of the provincial government to warrant such extraordinary measures. They maintained that the federal government had exceeded its constitutional authority by imposing emergency and governor's rule, effectively depriving an elected provincial government and its representatives of their powers.

The petitions further stated that governor's rule could only be imposed in exceptional circumstances when the situation in a province deteriorated beyond control, with the provincial government itself expected to recommend such action.

They also challenged the invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces, arguing that the deployment of troops in aid of civil administration fell within the provincial government's domain. The petitioners alleged that several constitutional requirements had been disregarded while taking these decisions.

Meanwhile, the Advocate General's Office has directed the governor, chief secretary, provincial assembly speaker and secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department to submit their respective reports and comments before the court through officers of Grade 17 or above by November 7.

However, questions have been raised over how the provincial assembly speaker would submit his response, as the provincial government maintains that he is currently in protective custody. The Advocate General's Office has also been informed of the situation.

headline: Balochistan sacks 72 more doctors
description: Balochistan sacks 72 more doctors
author: Syed Ali Shah
article_text:
Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti has announced the introduction of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based attendance system in the provincial Health Department for the first time to ensure punctuality, discipline and accountability among government employees.

He said 72 more doctors had been dismissed from service for remaining absent from duty for prolonged periods, taking the total number of Health Department employees terminated over absenteeism to 200.

In a statement posted on social media platform X, the chief minister said Rs410 million had so far been deducted from government employees' salaries for violations of attendance rules and disciplinary regulations. He added that 11,000 employees had been issued notices seeking explanations for their absence from duty and negligence in performing official responsibilities.

Departmental proceedings were also under way against another 800 government employees, he said.

Bugti emphasised that government employees were public servants and must discharge their responsibilities with honesty, punctuality and a strong sense of accountability. He made it clear that no employee would be allowed to draw a salary without performing duty.

He said negligence, absenteeism and failure to provide public services would not be tolerated, adding that measures to improve attendance, discipline and institutional performance would continue across government departments.

In a separate development, the chief minister has taken personal responsibility for the welfare, education and upbringing of five orphaned siblings, including Munir Ahmed, a young boy who came into the public spotlight through a viral social media video showing him working at a roadside eatery.

Bugti met Munir and obtained details about the family's circumstances and hardships. He directed the relevant authorities to take immediate measures to ensure quality education, proper accommodation and a secure future for the children and their mother.

The chief minister ordered the admission of Munir, his younger brother and three sisters to educational institutions, directing officials to ensure that they received all necessary facilities to continue their studies without being burdened by financial difficulties or domestic hardships.

He also personally assumed responsibility for supporting all five children and their mother, instructing his staff to ensure that the family's essential needs, including education, accommodation and general welfare, were adequately addressed.
