headline: Completion of minority legislation promised
description: Completion of minority legislation promised
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has assured religious minorities that legislation concerning their rights and welfare, which has remained pending for a long time, would be completed at the earliest.

He was addressing a ceremony held at the Governor House on Saturday to mark the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. The Governor extended greetings to the Sikh community and reaffirmed the government's commitment to safeguarding the rights, dignity and welfare of people belonging to all religious communities.

Faisal Karim Kundi said Pakistan was a safe country for people of all faiths and acknowledged the significant contributions of minority communities to the country's development, prosperity and social fabric.

He said the K-P government stood shoulder to shoulder with minority communities and was making efforts to address their concerns despite limited financial resources. He stressed that ensuring equal rights, protection and opportunities for all citizens was among the government's priorities.

The Governor also regretted that previous provincial governments had not given adequate attention to the welfare and issues of religious minorities. He said the present government was determined to address their longstanding concerns and take practical steps to improve their living conditions.

Emphasising the importance of peace and stability, Kundi said lasting peace was essential for the development and prosperity of K-P. He said the sacrifices rendered by the martyrs of the Army Public School (APS), members of the public, police personnel and security forces in the struggle against terrorism would always be remembered.

He said the sacrifices of these individuals and institutions had played a significant role in the restoration of peace, adding that the nation must remain united in its efforts to maintain stability and counter violence.

headline: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro isolated
description: He sneaked out of Brazil to the US, after being ordered to surrender his passports due to investigations against him
author: AFP
article_text:
In a viral wave of mockery, Brazilian popstar Anitta declared herself free of cellulite, one influencer declared himself the “true president” of Twitter, and another social media user proclaimed himself the winner of the next lottery. The target of the taunts was Flavio Bolsonaro, who -- after fleeing to the United States following his election defeat -- proclaimed himself the leader of Brazil on Wednesday in a confusing series of revised statements.

The moves by the 45-year-old senator have been met in Brazil with a mixture of derision, disbelief, and disapproval, even from within his own camp. The eldest son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro was blindsided by his election defeat to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday, after leading a first-round vote earlier this month.

In a cloak-and-dagger operation, he sneaked out of Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador, after being ordered to surrender his passports due to several ongoing investigations against him. Hours after his arrival in Florida, he posted a statement on social media declaring himself the “true president” of Brazil, before revising the wording a few minutes later to describe himself as the “leader” of the country.

A Bolsonaro ally who published an earlier version of the statement bearing Brazil’s old coat of arms, abandoned in the sixties, said it had been a ChatGPT error. - ‘Lunatic asylum Napoleon’ - The letter was met with outrage in Brazilian media, which described its tone as “coupmongering,” while politicians from across the spectrum called for the election results to be respected.

A column in the O Globo daily likened Flavio Bolsonaro to a “lunatic asylum Napoleon,” while the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper slammed the statement as “pathetic.” On the right, the powerful governor of Sao Paulo, Tarcisio de Freitas, quickly distanced himself.

De Freitas was a former minister under Jair Bolsonaro who had been tipped as the main candidate for the right before the former president chose his son. “We are democrats. The election result is sovereign. What we have seen is the will of the majority of the population, which must be respected,” De Freitas said in an interview with the Estadao daily. As speculation switched almost immediately to who would lead the right with Flavio out of the country, the governor -- a favorite in business circles -- said a 2030 run was “a possibility.”

Rogerio Marinho, who coordinated Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign, said there was “no evidence” of electoral fraud, as claimed by the defeated candidate. Electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques, who was appointed to the Supreme Court by Jair Bolsonaro, issued a statement to highlight the “secure electoral process.”

Flavio Bolsonaro also said he would lead the opposition from abroad.

His self-proclamation as Brazil’s leader in exile “is not a misstep, it is a calculated move” intended to maintain his influence over the conservative camp in Brazil, said Geraldo Monteiro, a political scientist at the State University of Rio de Janeiro.

Hours after his arrival in Florida, he posted a statement on social media declaring himself the “true president” of Brazil, before revising the wording a few minutes later to describe himself as the “leader” of the country.

A column in the O Globo daily likened Flavio Bolsonaro to a “lunatic asylum Napoleon,” while the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper slammed the statement as “pathetic.” On the right, the powerful governor of Sao Paulo, Tarcisio de Freitas, quickly distanced himself.

De Freitas was a former minister under Jair Bolsonaro who had been tipped as the main candidate for the right before the former president chose his son. “We are democrats. The election result is sovereign. What we have seen is the will of the majority of the population, which must be respected,” De Freitas said in an interview with the Estadao daily. As speculation switched almost immediately to who would lead the right with Flavio out of the country, the governor -- a favorite in business circles -- said a 2030 run was “a possibility.”

Rogerio Marinho, who coordinated Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign, said there was “no evidence” of electoral fraud, as claimed by the defeated candidate. Electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques, who was appointed to the Supreme Court by Jair Bolsonaro, issued a statement to highlight the “secure electoral process.”

Flavio Bolsonaro also said he would lead the opposition from abroad.

His self-proclamation as Brazil’s leader in exile “is not a misstep, it is a calculated move” intended to maintain his influence over the conservative camp in Brazil, said Geraldo Monteiro, a political scientist at the State University of Rio de Janeiro.

headline: President, PM pay tribute to G-B on 79th Independence Day
description: In Nov 1947, leaders of the freedom movement liberated region from Dogra rule, unconditionally acceded to Pakistan
author: APP.
article_text:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan (G-B) on the region’s 79th Independence Day, paying tribute to those who fought against Dogra rule and highlighting the region’s strategic and economic importance.

In November 1947, leaders of the freedom movement, along with the people of G-B, liberated the region from Dogra rule and unconditionally acceded to Pakistan. To mark the occasion, a grand ceremony will be held at the Army Helipad in Gilgit, featuring various celebrations and tributes to the heroes who played a role in the region's liberation struggle.

In separate messages posted on X, both leaders recalled the events of 1947, when the people of G-B overthrew Dogra rule and the region subsequently acceded to Pakistan.

President Zardari said the people of G-B "overthrew the colonial yoke of Dogra rule, declared independence and soon after, sent the letter to Quaid-e-Azam for accession to Pakistan" 79 years ago.

"The flame for freedom has never extinguished and their loyalty with Pakistan has never been questioned all those decades and years," he added.

The president extended his "heartfelt felicitations" to the people of the region and paid tribute to those who took part in the historic struggle against Dogra rule, saying their "courage, sacrifices and decision to join Pakistan remain an important part of our shared history".

He also highlighted the political and administrative reforms introduced in the region over the years, recalling that former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto had initiated a series of landmark reforms in 1972.

Following Bhutto's visit to the region in August that year, the Frontier Crimes Regulation and Jagirdari system were abolished, the old Agency system was dismantled, and a new administrative and judicial framework was introduced, he said.

President Zardari added that the reform process continued in 1974 with the abolition of the remaining princely states, including Hunza and Nagar, bringing the region under a more unified administrative system.

He also credited former prime minister Benazir Bhutto with advancing the process through the Legal Framework Order of 1994, which established the Northern Areas Legislative Council.

The president said the process continued in 2009 under the PPP government, which introduced the Gilgit-Baltistan Empowerment and Self-Governance Order, gave the region its present name and established a legislative assembly, an elected chief minister and a governor.

Highlighting the region's strategic location, natural resources and direct border with China, President Zardari said its people had made "valuable contributions to Pakistan’s defence and development".

"Our priority must be to ensure that its people benefit from these opportunities through better roads, schools, healthcare, reliable energy and employment," he said.

He stressed that development should translate into tangible improvements in people's lives, including access to quality education and healthcare, better opportunities for young people and improved market access for farmers and small businesses.

"These practical needs must remain central to our priorities, including in remote areas," he added.

President Zardari also highlighted the region's mountains, glaciers, rivers and cultural heritage, saying tourism could provide livelihoods and support local economies, while its natural environment needed protection for future generations.

He wished the people of G-B continued progress in peace and prosperity.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the federal government remained steadfastly committed to the development and prosperity of Gilgit-Baltistan, as well as ensuring a bright future for its youth.

In a message on the 79th anniversary of G-B's National Day on November 1, 2026, the prime minister extended his "heartfelt congratulations" to the people of the region, saying the "exemplary resolve, courage and sacrifices" of its leaders and people in securing freedom deserved the highest tribute.

He said November 1, 1947, which marked the end of Dogra rule in Gilgit-Baltistan and the region's accession to Pakistan, stood as a "luminous and unforgettable day" in its history.

"This day serves as a testament to our shared national resolve, bravery and valour," he said, adding that the people's "profound and unwavering commitment to Pakistan", demonstrated across generations, was a source of national pride.

The prime minister also paid tribute to the "mujahideen, ghazis and martyrs" who had etched their names in history through their sacrifices during the struggle for freedom.

Highlighting the region's geographical significance, Shehbaz said it held a distinguished position in Pakistan's national landscape and had considerable potential for regional trade and economic development, particularly in the context of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

He said the federal government had undertaken several initiatives in Gilgit-Baltistan across various sectors, including energy, education, healthcare, employment and public safety.

The 16-megawatt Naltar Hydropower Project had been completed, which he described as a transformative initiative to address the region's energy challenges.

He added that the federal government had launched a 100MW solar energy project to provide affordable and accessible energy to the people of G-B. A transparent digital balloting process had been adopted for the free distribution of solar panels with a combined capacity of 58MW, with approximately 100,000 panels distributed so far, he said.

On education, PM Shehbaz said the foundation stones for four Daanish Schools had been laid in Sultanabad, Bunji, Ghanche and Skardu. Valued at Rs12.46 billion, the projects would provide talented children from financially disadvantaged backgrounds with access to quality, modern education and residential facilities, he added.

Under the Prime Minister's Laptop Scheme, 4,245 laptops had so far been distributed among young people in Gilgit-Baltistan, while students from the region had also been included in the Chromebook distribution programme, on a par with the rest of the country.

To boost investment and employment opportunities, approval had also been granted to designate Maqpoon Das as a special economic zone (SEZ). Spread over 250 acres, the zone was expected to host 155 industrial and commercial enterprises and generate approximately 5,000 jobs, the prime minister said.

On public safety, PM Shehbaz said the second phase of the Gilgit-Baltistan Safe City Project had been inaugurated to strengthen security and maintain law and order, while a similar project was also being initiated in Skardu.

He said the federal government was fully committed to supporting the regional government in addressing its financial challenges and implementing institutional and administrative reforms to improve public services and development initiatives.

"Let us work together towards our shared national goal of progress and prosperity," he said.

The prime minister also called for a renewed commitment to ensuring quality and equitable access to education, healthcare and employment opportunities across the country, including Gilgit-Baltistan.

"On this historic occasion, while paying tribute to the sacrifices and achievements of our forefathers, let us renew our pledge to work collectively," he said, concluding his message with the slogans: "Long live Gilgit-Baltistan! Long live Pakistan!"

In November 1947, leaders of the freedom movement, along with the people of G-B, liberated the region from Dogra rule and unconditionally acceded to Pakistan. To mark the occasion, a grand ceremony will be held at the Army Helipad in Gilgit, featuring various celebrations and tributes to the heroes who played a role in the region's liberation struggle.

In separate messages posted on X, both leaders recalled the events of 1947, when the people of G-B overthrew Dogra rule and the region subsequently acceded to Pakistan.

President Zardari said the people of G-B "overthrew the colonial yoke of Dogra rule, declared independence and soon after, sent the letter to Quaid-e-Azam for accession to Pakistan" 79 years ago.

"The flame for freedom has never extinguished and their loyalty with Pakistan has never been questioned all those decades and years," he added.

The president extended his "heartfelt felicitations" to the people of the region and paid tribute to those who took part in the historic struggle against Dogra rule, saying their "courage, sacrifices and decision to join Pakistan remain an important part of our shared history".

He also highlighted the political and administrative reforms introduced in the region over the years, recalling that former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto had initiated a series of landmark reforms in 1972.

Following Bhutto's visit to the region in August that year, the Frontier Crimes Regulation and Jagirdari system were abolished, the old Agency system was dismantled, and a new administrative and judicial framework was introduced, he said.

President Zardari added that the reform process continued in 1974 with the abolition of the remaining princely states, including Hunza and Nagar, bringing the region under a more unified administrative system.

He also credited former prime minister Benazir Bhutto with advancing the process through the Legal Framework Order of 1994, which established the Northern Areas Legislative Council.

The president said the process continued in 2009 under the PPP government, which introduced the Gilgit-Baltistan Empowerment and Self-Governance Order, gave the region its present name and established a legislative assembly, an elected chief minister and a governor.

Highlighting the region's strategic location, natural resources and direct border with China, President Zardari said its people had made "valuable contributions to Pakistan’s defence and development".

"Our priority must be to ensure that its people benefit from these opportunities through better roads, schools, healthcare, reliable energy and employment," he said.

He stressed that development should translate into tangible improvements in people's lives, including access to quality education and healthcare, better opportunities for young people and improved market access for farmers and small businesses.

"These practical needs must remain central to our priorities, including in remote areas," he added.

President Zardari also highlighted the region's mountains, glaciers, rivers and cultural heritage, saying tourism could provide livelihoods and support local economies, while its natural environment needed protection for future generations.

He wished the people of G-B continued progress in peace and prosperity.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the federal government remained steadfastly committed to the development and prosperity of Gilgit-Baltistan, as well as ensuring a bright future for its youth.

In a message on the 79th anniversary of G-B's National Day on November 1, 2026, the prime minister extended his "heartfelt congratulations" to the people of the region, saying the "exemplary resolve, courage and sacrifices" of its leaders and people in securing freedom deserved the highest tribute.

He said November 1, 1947, which marked the end of Dogra rule in Gilgit-Baltistan and the region's accession to Pakistan, stood as a "luminous and unforgettable day" in its history.

"This day serves as a testament to our shared national resolve, bravery and valour," he said, adding that the people's "profound and unwavering commitment to Pakistan", demonstrated across generations, was a source of national pride.

The prime minister also paid tribute to the "mujahideen, ghazis and martyrs" who had etched their names in history through their sacrifices during the struggle for freedom.

Highlighting the region's geographical significance, Shehbaz said it held a distinguished position in Pakistan's national landscape and had considerable potential for regional trade and economic development, particularly in the context of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

He said the federal government had undertaken several initiatives in Gilgit-Baltistan across various sectors, including energy, education, healthcare, employment and public safety.

The 16-megawatt Naltar Hydropower Project had been completed, which he described as a transformative initiative to address the region's energy challenges.

He added that the federal government had launched a 100MW solar energy project to provide affordable and accessible energy to the people of G-B. A transparent digital balloting process had been adopted for the free distribution of solar panels with a combined capacity of 58MW, with approximately 100,000 panels distributed so far, he said.

On education, PM Shehbaz said the foundation stones for four Daanish Schools had been laid in Sultanabad, Bunji, Ghanche and Skardu. Valued at Rs12.46 billion, the projects would provide talented children from financially disadvantaged backgrounds with access to quality, modern education and residential facilities, he added.

Under the Prime Minister's Laptop Scheme, 4,245 laptops had so far been distributed among young people in Gilgit-Baltistan, while students from the region had also been included in the Chromebook distribution programme, on a par with the rest of the country.

To boost investment and employment opportunities, approval had also been granted to designate Maqpoon Das as a special economic zone (SEZ). Spread over 250 acres, the zone was expected to host 155 industrial and commercial enterprises and generate approximately 5,000 jobs, the prime minister said.

On public safety, PM Shehbaz said the second phase of the Gilgit-Baltistan Safe City Project had been inaugurated to strengthen security and maintain law and order, while a similar project was also being initiated in Skardu.

He said the federal government was fully committed to supporting the regional government in addressing its financial challenges and implementing institutional and administrative reforms to improve public services and development initiatives.

"Let us work together towards our shared national goal of progress and prosperity," he said.

The prime minister also called for a renewed commitment to ensuring quality and equitable access to education, healthcare and employment opportunities across the country, including Gilgit-Baltistan.

"On this historic occasion, while paying tribute to the sacrifices and achievements of our forefathers, let us renew our pledge to work collectively," he said, concluding his message with the slogans: "Long live Gilgit-Baltistan! Long live Pakistan!"

headline: Inde Navarrette makes 'SNL' debut with Shane Gillis dig and quips about Marvel's Rogue role
description: The episode also featured Gracie Abrams making her debut as the programme's musical guest
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Inde Navarrette made her hosting debut on Saturday Night Live with a comedy-filled opening monologue, taking aim at Shane Gillis while discussing her upcoming role in Marvel's X-Men.

The actress, known for her appearance in Curry Barker's horror film Obsession, addressed the physical preparation required to play Rogue in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

She used the opportunity to reference Gillis' controversial opening monologue from his previous appearance on the NBC sketch comedy programme.

“So, every morning, I put on my little wh*re outfit and hit the gym,” Navarrette joked, prompting laughter from the audience.

She also distanced herself from her Obsession character, Nikki, insisting she was “nothing like Nikki”, before introducing her boyfriend, who was revealed to be taped to his studio audience chair.

Navarrette's debut episode featured several sketches, including a fictional Delta Airlines advert introducing a section called “Delta Disruptive”, alongside a dating show parody and a comedy segment featuring a robot named PD-44.

Other highlights included a Spanish soap opera sketch with Marcello Hernandez, in which the pair attempted to incorporate Sprite Cherry Lime Habanero into an increasingly chaotic storyline.

The episode also featured cast members Marcello Hernandez, Kam Patterson and Jeremy Culhane, who appeared in costumes as a sexy TSA agent, Elizabeth Holmes and Wolverine, respectively.

Navarrette's first appearance as host marked another milestone for the actress as she prepares for her upcoming Marvel role. The episode also featured Gracie Abrams making her debut as the programme's musical guest.

headline: Heidi Klum reveals gruesome severed hand costume at 25th annual Halloween party
description: Klum has become known for her elaborate Halloween outfits, turning into recognisable characters and unusual creatures
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Heidi Klum marked the 25th anniversary of her annual Halloween party on October 31 by arriving in a realistic severed human hand costume, continuing her tradition of elaborate transformations.

The supermodel attended the milestone celebration at Cathédrale in New York City, where her latest look once again attracted attention.

View this post on Instagram

Klum has become known for her elaborate Halloween outfits, regularly transforming herself into recognisable characters and unusual creatures.

Speaking to Variety, Klum explained her approach to creating memorable experiences through costume design. “There still needs to be people that create moments with real people … to me, it’s like a beautiful art,” she said.

She also acknowledged the temporary nature of her elaborate appearance, adding: “This is only good for the night. Tonight. Everything goes down the drain, so to speak, in the shower.”

Last year, Klum dressed as Medusa, complete with a headpiece featuring moving snakes and a trailing tail.

Her husband, Tom Kaulitz, complemented the look as an ancient Greek soldier turned to stone. A team of 15 artists worked on creating her costume.

Over the years, Klum's Halloween transformations have included E.T., Fiona from Shrek, Jessica Rabbit and the werewolf from Michael Jackson's "Thriller".

She has also appeared as a peacock, butterfly and giant worm.

Beyond her Halloween celebrations, Klum continues her television career. She returned to Project Runway as host and judge for its 22nd season, alongside Nina Garcia and Law Roach.

She previously hosted the fashion competition for 16 seasons following its 2004 debut.

Heidi Klum marked the 25th anniversary of her annual Halloween party on October 31 by arriving in a realistic severed human hand costume, continuing her tradition of elaborate transformations.

The supermodel attended the milestone celebration at Cathédrale in New York City, where her latest look once again attracted attention.

 
 
 
 
View this post on Instagram
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Klum has become known for her elaborate Halloween outfits, regularly transforming herself into recognisable characters and unusual creatures.

Speaking to Variety, Klum explained her approach to creating memorable experiences through costume design. “There still needs to be people that create moments with real people … to me, it’s like a beautiful art,” she said.

She also acknowledged the temporary nature of her elaborate appearance, adding: “This is only good for the night. Tonight. Everything goes down the drain, so to speak, in the shower.”

Last year, Klum dressed as Medusa, complete with a headpiece featuring moving snakes and a trailing tail.

Her husband, Tom Kaulitz, complemented the look as an ancient Greek soldier turned to stone. A team of 15 artists worked on creating her costume.

Over the years, Klum's Halloween transformations have included E.T., Fiona from Shrek, Jessica Rabbit and the werewolf from Michael Jackson's "Thriller".

She has also appeared as a peacock, butterfly and giant worm.

Beyond her Halloween celebrations, Klum continues her television career. She returned to Project Runway as host and judge for its 22nd season, alongside Nina Garcia and Law Roach.

She previously hosted the fashion competition for 16 seasons following its 2004 debut.

headline: Hayden Christensen recalls burglar returning his belongings after recognising 'Star Wars' actor
description: Speaking at LA Comic Con, Christensen shared the unexpected encounter
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Star Wars actor Hayden Christensen has recalled an unusual burglary at his home in which the intruder recognised him, apologised and returned his belongings during the incident.

Speaking at LA Comic Con, Christensen shared the unexpected encounter, as reported by The Nerd Wire.

The actor explained that he was upstairs when he heard someone enter his home. Upon investigating, he found a man holding his possessions.

“I’m like, is this a delivery guy?” Christensen recalled. “And I look and I’m like, this is all my stuff.”

The situation took an unexpected turn when the burglar recognised Christensen and apologised.

According to the actor, the man was struggling financially and had been attempting to raise money for a train ticket home.

Rather than simply reporting the incident, Christensen offered to help. He reportedly gave the man clothes and shoes to support his efforts to secure employment and offered to drive him to the train station and purchase his ticket the following day. However, the man never returned.

Christensen, 45, first portrayed Anakin Skywalker in 2002's Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones, reprising the role in Revenge of the Sith and later appearing in Obi-Wan Kenobi and Ahsoka.

The actor is also set to return as Anakin in the second season of Ahsoka. During an interview with IGN, Christensen discussed revisiting the character, saying he felt more connected to Anakin after having additional time to understand him.

Ahsoka Season 2 is scheduled to premiere on Disney+ on January 20, 2027, with Rosario Dawson returning as the title character.

headline: Saudi envoy visits Dino Valley, highlights Pakistan's tourism potential
description: Says exploring a country's natural beauty, engaging with people adds valuable human dimension to official relations
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Newly appointed Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy explored Islamabad's tourism potential during a visit to Dino Valley and highlighted the role of tourism and people-to-people engagement in strengthening bilateral relations, according to a post shared on X by the Press Attaché at the Embassy of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in Pakistan, Saif Nasser.

In the post, Nasser said Albugamy had enjoyed the "natural beauty and scenic landscapes" of Pakistan's capital during his visit to the tourist destination.

"Moments like these go beyond simply enjoying a destination; they reflect the true essence of public diplomacy," he said.

He stated that exploring a country's natural beauty and tourism potential, while engaging with its people and culture, helped foster people-to-people ties and added "a valuable human dimension to official relations".

"These bonds are further strengthened by the warmth, authenticity, and renowned hospitality of the Pakistani people," Nasser said.

Albugamy was appointed Saudi Arabia's ambassador to Pakistan in July, replacing Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki, who had served in the position for nearly nine years.

The new envoy arrived in Islamabad on September 26 to assume his diplomatic responsibilities. A retired major general, he later joined the Saudi Foreign Ministry with the rank of ambassador and holds a doctorate in Human Resource Management from Brunel University London.

He presented his diplomatic credentials to President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr on October 14. During their meeting, President Zardari underscored the close strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and reiterated Islamabad's commitment to the Kingdom's security and defence.

The president also stressed the need to deepen economic ties, appreciated Saudi Arabia's financial support and assistance with oil supplies, and expressed confidence that bilateral relations would reach new heights during Albugamy's tenure.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also welcomed the ambassador, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to strengthening cooperation across various sectors.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar subsequently met Albugamy and reiterated the two countries' shared commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity.

headline: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering bulk of $6 billion in stolen funds
description: Exchange says remaining 5% of stolen tokens consists of assets that are less liquid, may take longer to source
author: Reuters
article_text:
Exchange says remaining 5% of stolen tokens consists of assets that are less liquid, may take longer to source

Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals in phases after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world's largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.

Binance said phase would start between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday and include bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens.

The remaining 5% of stolen tokens consists of assets that are less liquid and may take longer to source in the required amounts, Binance posted on X late on Saturday.

The FBI said on Saturday the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.

Pyongyang has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.

Members of the unit were observed by law enforcement converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency ethereum, the FBI said in a statement, adding that it expects "further laundering" of the assets through the use of related technology.

Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals in phases after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world's largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea.

Binance said phase would start between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday and include bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens.

The remaining 5% of stolen tokens consists of assets that are less liquid and may take longer to source in the required amounts, Binance posted on X late on Saturday.

The FBI said on Saturday the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.

headline: Thousands join Indian opposition protest demanding poll chief's resignation
description: Hundreds of security personnel, some carrying batons, surround protest site accompanied by riot-control vehicles
author: Reuters
article_text:
Thousands protested in Delhi on Sunday to demand the resignation of India's election chief over a revision of voter lists, the latest in more than a month of opposition demonstrations challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Led by Congress party chief Rahul Gandhi, Sunday's protesters say the controversial revision benefits Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Analysts say the protests and growing support for the opposition form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014, though his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.

Authorities tightened security and warned of traffic diversions before protesters began a march from central Delhi to the designated rally site, where the opposition has predicted hundreds of thousands of people would participate.

'There should be accountability', protester says

Hundreds of security personnel, some of them carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot-control vehicles, surrounded the historic Ramlila Maidan ground as hundreds of people, many waving national and party flags, began moving towards it. Opposition party leaders led the march in an open-top jeep.

Among the thousands waiting for the marchers at the Ramlila Maidan was Reena Mahto, a member of the Congress' student wing, who said four people from her family had been deleted from the voter list due to the false claim that they had moved elsewhere.

She told Reuters the family has long lived in Jagdalpur in the central state of Chhattisgarh, but "now all of a sudden we have been marked as shifted from our own house," adding, "There should be accountability, and we are here to seek that."

The change to voter rolls removed over 130 million names — more than the population of Japan. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affected Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the BJP.

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Dinesh Singh said he was joining the protest for the sake of his children's future. "I am not affiliated with any political party," he said. "I am here for a cause. I want the children to remember that we fought for their future."

'Conspiracy' for 'anarchy', minister says

Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, however, called the protest a "carefully orchestrated drama".

"What is unfolding today at Ramlila Maidan is not an act of respect for democracy. It is a calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy, all in the name of democracy," he told news agency ANI.

The demonstration is the latest in a series of near-daily protests that opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have held since late September demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The protests erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.

headline: Valkyries defeat Dream to capture first WNBA crown
description: Williams' 30-point haul powers Golden State to a 68-63 win
author: AFP
article_text: Gabby Williams scored 30 points and the Golden State Valkyries captured their first Women's NBA title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a winner-take-all championship showdown. Williams scored a WNBA Finals one-half record 28 points in the second half as the second-year expansion Valkyries won the series four games to three, the longest title matchup in league history. "I wasn't going to lose on Halloween," Williams said. "It's easy when the energy is this good and positive. I wouldn't change a thing." Despite only two points in the first half, Williams seized command in the second with the game on the line and lifted Golden State ahead to stay in the dying minutes to earn the WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player award. "I just, I don't know. I love moments like this," Williams said. "Nat (coach Natalie Nakase) told me to be patient in the first half. It was hard but I listened to her and she was right as always." "All it took was good people. We have winners. "We have people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. They don't care about scoring. They just want to do defense and rebounding. Do whatever it takes and we built a beautiful culture here." The victory came before a sellout crowd of more than 18,000 at the Chase Center that cheered the home side to a crown as the Dream lost the finals for the fourth time in the team's 18-year history. "We have an incredible team. What you did was unbelievable," team owner Joe Lacob said. Williams sank a three-pointer with 2:19 remaining to give Golden State a 60-57 lead and after Atlanta's Allisha Gray missed a layup added two free throws for a five-point edge. Kiah Stokes put back a Williams miss for a 64-57 lead and free throws by Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton down the stretch sealed the victory. "This is for all the people that have been underrated, misunderstood," Nakase said. "This is proof that if you put in all your heart and all your soul you can ... win championships." Golden State seized an 8-0 lead as the Dream missed their first nine shots. Atlanta answered with a 21-6 run to seize the lead, starting the second quarter with a 9-0 streak on the way to a 30-24 halftime lead. The Valkyries, however, closed the third quarter with a 17-7 run to seize a 45-44 edge entering the fourth quarter, Williams scoring 15 points in the third period.

headline: MotoGP confident Qatar race can go ahead
description: Organisers insist all available safety measures are in place despite rider concerns over the regional conflict
author: REUTERS
article_text:
MotoGP is set to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix even as a group of riders demand more assurances for travelling to the region, with organisers arguing that a "zero-risk environment" is unrealistic. The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6 to 8 due to the US-Israeli war against Iran. "MotoGP has provided teams and riders with every assurance available from the State of Qatar, the circuit ... and our own ongoing risk assessment processes," a MotoGP spokesperson said. "We fully respect the ⁠concerns raised and highlight that safety remains the priority for everyone involved."

RIDERS SEEK MORE SAFETY ASSURANCES

However, the MotoGP spokesperson said the expectation of a zero-risk environment was not realistic anywhere in the world by any government or organiser. "Over the past months, we have maintained continuous dialogue with teams and riders, sharing the latest information available, providing direct access to documents and answering questions openly and transparently," the spokesperson said. Carlos Ezpeleta, deputy CEO ⁠of MotoGP, visited Qatar on Thursday, where the circuit's president, Abdulrahman Al-Mannai, said they were ready to welcome the riders, teams and fans for the 20th round of the season. However, Spain's embassy in Qatar has issued a notice urging its citizens not to travel to the Gulf nation unless absolutely necessary. Spaniards make up the largest share of riders on the grid, including world champion Marc Marquez. A ⁠person with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters Qatar has guaranteed teams would not ⁠be stranded in case of escalation in the conflict and they could leave the country safely in time for the final two rounds in Portugal and Spain later in November. The person said championship leader Marquez, a seven-times MotoGP champion, was one of the riders seeking more assurances. "Additional impossible asks at the last moment go beyond what can realistically be guaranteed by any event organiser, government or sporting body," the MotoGP spokesperson said. "Our position is based solely on the most up-to-date intelligence, expert advice and assurances available to us."

APRILIA WANT TO 'TURN THE PAGE'

Marquez has not publicly stated his position on ⁠travelling to Qatar, but Ducati team manager Davide Tardozzi defended the Spaniard after he came under criticism for not taking a stance. "I have read that all the ⁠blame has been placed on Marc, as if he were the one who did not want to go to Qatar. That is not the case," he told Sky Sport. "Marc simply asked, as many other riders did, for an organisational safety plan - nothing more, nothing less. He did not say, 'I don't want to go'. "There are circumstances that could make you think it would be better not to go. But if the necessary safety conditions are in place, including an evacuation plan and guarantees that there will be no problems if something happens, then we will go." Marquez did not immediately respond to ⁠a request for comment. Ducati said the Italian outfit would travel to Qatar. Aprilia are keen to race in Qatar with Spanish rider Jorge Martin, second in the standings behind Marquez after withdrawing from the Malaysian Grand Prix due to a wrist injury. "We need to turn the page and look to the next chapter, Qatar, hoping it goes better, and keep this fight going to the last," said Aprilia's technical director Fabiano Sterlacchini. "This setback has certainly made things harder for us." The MotoGP source confirmed that no decision has been taken about sporting sanctions if teams or riders do not participate in Qatar.

headline: Fichardt storms into Simmons Bank Championship lead
description: South African shoots a bogey-free 61 to open a one-shot advantage over Zach Johnson heading into the final round
author: REUTERS
article_text: South African Darren Fichardt tied the mark for lowest round of the PGA Tour Champions season with an 11-under-par 61 in the second round Saturday to take a one-stroke lead at 14-under 130 into the final round of the Simmons Bank Championship in Little Rock, Ark. Fichardt's bogey-free round left him one shot better that first-round leader Zach Johnson (67). The 50-year-old Johnson, a two-time major winner, overcame an uneven front nine to shoot 5 under on the back nine to earn a spot in Sunday's final ⁠group. New Zealand's Steven Alker also shot a 67 on Saturday, tying him for third at 11 under and gaining him the last spot in the final threesome Sunday. Sweden's Henrik Stenson (68) is tied with Alker while South Africa's Retief Goosen (66), Jerry Kelly (67), Argentine Ricardo Gonzalez (67) and Michael Block (69) tied for fifth at 9 under. Four other golfers are another shot back. Fichardt, a ⁠Tour rookie, started his day on fire at Pleasant Valley Country Club, parring the par-4 first hole before going birdie-birdie-eagle-birdie over the next four. He shot an 8-under 28 on before the turn, then birdied Nos. 10 and 11 before cooling off and parring the next six holes. He birdied the par-5 18th to end his round. His 61 ⁠tied the tournament record set in the first round last year by ⁠Alker. The top 36 players in the Charles Schwab Cup standings after Sunday will advance to the Cup Championship in Phoenix in two weeks. Fichardt's round propelled him from 46th to a projected 13th in the standings. "The first 11 holes was awesome," the 51-year-old Fichardt said after what he called his "best round ever." "I was a little irritated because (Friday) I felt like I could go low and not too much went right," he added. "But I could feel the lines were getting close to being spot on. You know, ⁠I've come off four really tough weeks where I thought I could do a lot better, but I was struggling with a ⁠few injuries. So yeah, it was good to get a good round today." "Yeah, that was a heck of a score," said Alker, whose 61 came in the first round last year. "Today was the day to do it, right? I mean, there's no wind. Fire at some flags and try to take advantage of it. ... It was a heck of a round." Alker is also one of the golfers to post a 61 this season, doing so in the second round of the Rogers Charity Classic. The season's other ⁠61, by Mark Wilson, came in the same round as Alker. Johnson, a fellow rookie and one of six players to get their first Tour win this season, credited his round-opening bogey as one of the reasons he was able to weather a front nine that included two bogeys and two birdies. "I actually made a really bad but yet very good bogey, if that makes sense, on the first hole," he said after his round. "I mean, I don't know what I made, probably a 10-footer for 5. ... And then I steadied it. I played pretty good."

headline: Antonelli admits to feeling tense of eve of potential F1 title decider
description: The Italian needs only a top-nine finish to make history despite starting fourth on the grid
author: AFP
article_text:
The Italian needs only a top-nine finish to make history despite starting fourth on the grid

Kimi Antonelli admitted he felt tense and below his best on Saturday after qualifying fifth for Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, where he can become Formula One's youngest world champion. The 20-year-old Italian, who missed Thursday's media day at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez with a virus, will start from fourth as Red Bull's four-time world champion Max Verstappen has a grid penalty. He needs to finish ninth or better to make certain of his first drivers' title and Italy's first since Alberto Ascari for Ferrari in 1953, even if one of his main rivals -- Mercedes team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton wins. Hamilton will start Sunday's race from his record 105th pole position, and first for Ferrari, with Russell second on the grid. The pair are respectively 124 and 123 points adrift of Antonelli in the title race. "I struggled (Saturday) to get a good feeling with the tyres in Q3," said Antonelli. "I just didn't have the most confidence, and I was feeling a bit tense, I'm not going to lie. "It's just been a poor lap, many mistakes here and there, but overall I'm still P4 and there is a lot to play for tomorrow. "It hasn't been the easiest weekend to be fair and I'm still not feeling 100%," Antonelli added. "The thought of what could happen now is here - and I'm definitely a bit more tense than usual."

headline: Pakistan assumes G-24 chairmanship, pledges push for global financial reforms
description: PM welcomes appointment, calls it a diplomatic milestone which will elevate country's voice in global economic affairs
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan on Sunday assumed the chairmanship of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24), with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb saying the country would focus on development-led growth, stronger representation for developing economies and reforms to the international financial architecture.

In a statement posted on X, the Ministry of Finance said Pakistan had assumed the chairmanship and reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening the “collective voice of developing economies” and advancing a “fair, responsive and development-oriented international financial system”.

Aurangzeb described the role as a “profound responsibility”, calling for greater cooperation, stronger multilateral institutions and global commitments to address climate shocks, development financing gaps and economic fragmentation.

“The future of developing economies is not peripheral to the future of the global economy. It is central to it,” he said, adding that emerging and developing nations had the potential to drive investment, innovation, entrepreneurship and global growth.

The finance minister said Pakistan's first priority would be to place development at the centre of economic policymaking. He said macroeconomic stability "must serve as a foundation for investment, productivity, employment and shared prosperity," enabling developing and low-income economies to move beyond crisis management towards sustainable growth.

His second priority was to promote more inclusive and representative multilateral frameworks and that "Pakistan will advocate for more equitable and fair governance, meaningful participation in decision-making and greater responsiveness of the Bretton Woods institutions to the evolving needs and realities of their members."

The third priority was to advance a "development-oriented financial architecture," with Aurangzeb calling for affordable and timely development financing, sustainable debt solutions and stronger global financial safety nets. He also stressed the need to strengthen climate resilience and mobilise public and private capital.

“Our task is to ensure that the immense potential of developing economies is not constrained by an international financial architecture that has yet to fully adapt to a changing world,” he said.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan's experience of economic stabilisation, reform and resilience had reinforced the importance of aligning stability with long-term development, while ensuring that economies undertaking reforms had the financing and policy space to sustain them.

He said Pakistan would approach its chairmanship through consultation, consensus and collective advocacy, working with member countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and other international partners.

The finance minister also acknowledged Nigeria's role as the outgoing chair, saying the G-24's leadership should be judged by the impact it had on developing economies.

“The true measure of our collective leadership will not simply be the strength of our voice, but the difference that voice makes,” he said.

He said the group's task was to move “from collective voice to collective influence, and from collective influence to meaningful progress”.

PM welcomes Pakistan's chairmanship

Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif welcomed Pakistan's appointment as chair of the G-24, calling it an important diplomatic milestone that recognised and elevated the country's role and voice in global economic affairs.

In a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office, PM Shehbaz praised Aurangzeb and the Ministry of Finance team for their “tireless efforts”, effective diplomacy and professional capabilities.

He commended their role during the World Bank and IMF annual meetings and their efforts to secure a prominent position for Pakistan in the economic leadership of developing nations.

The prime minister said the G-24 chairmanship would provide Pakistan with a platform to advocate reforms to the global financial system, fair climate financing and sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies.

headline: Wembanyama leads Spurs to fourth straight win
description: San Antonio overcome Minnesota despite a late fightback to secure a 121-111 victory
author: REUTERS
article_text:
Victor Wembanyama poured in a season-high 43 points to help the host San Antonio Spurs defeat the short-handed Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111 on Saturday for their fourth straight victory.

The Timberwolves, already missing star Anthony Edwards (knee) and Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles surgery), also played without defensive stopper Rudy Gobert due to low back spasms and lost for the third time in four games.

The Spurs trailed ⁠by a point at halftime before taking a five-point lead into the fourth quarter. San Antonio used a 10-0 run to expand its advantage to 101-88, but the Timberwolves refused to relent, pulling within four on Jaden McDaniels' jumper with 6:49 to play. The Spurs answered ⁠with a 6-2 spurt, and Minnesota never seriously threatened again.

Wembanyama's 3-pointer with 2:40 left put San Antonio up 118-107.

Wembanyama also had seven rebounds and six blocks. Dylan Harper added 25 points, seven rebounds and six assists for the Spurs, while De'Aaron ⁠Fox scored 22 points and added eight rebounds ⁠and seven assists. Reserve Julian Champagnie scored 12. Ayo Dosunmu led the Timberwolves with 27 points and nine rebounds.

McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga tallied 19 points each, Joan Beringer had 12, and Jaylen Clark and LaMelo Ball scored 10 apiece for Minnesota. Ball was 2-for-10 from the field before fouling out. San Antonio led for most of the first quarter, pushing its advantage ⁠to 10 on Fox's three-point play with 36 seconds left before settling for a 34-28 edge.

The ⁠Spurs extended the margin to 46-35 after Julian Champagnie made three free throws at the 8:47 mark of the second quarter. Minnesota responded with a 16-0 run, capped by Trey Lyles' two free throws with 4:12 left in the quarter that gave the Timberwolves a 51-46 lead. Minnesota built its advantage to seven before back-to-back 3-pointers by Wembanyama brought San Antonio within 61-60 ⁠at halftime. Wembanyama's 24 first-half points led all scorers, while Fox had 10. Dosunmu's 14 points paced the Timberwolves, and McDaniels added 13. The Spurs moved back in front early in the third quarter and led 73-65 when Harper hammered home a dunk at the 7:54 mark.

San Antonio stretched its advantage to 10, but a 3-pointer by Kuminga helped pull the Timberwolves within 93-88 heading into the fourth quarter.

headline: De Minaur stuns Zverev to set up Vienna final against Alcaraz
description: The Australian rallies to win 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7/4)
author: AFP
article_text: Alex de Minaur held his nerve to overcome incoming men's No. 1 Alexander Zverev in an epic three-set struggle on Saturday to reach the final of the Vienna Open where he will face Carlos Alcaraz, who beat Daniil Medvedev. Zverev had ensured he would rise to the top of the rankings earlier in the week in Vienna. He had beaten De Minaur in March in the semi-final at Indian Wells, but this time the Australian won 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7/4). Zverev wobbled on service in the fifth game to concede the first set, but the German raced to a 4-0 lead as he romped through the second set, leaving De Minaur rattled. But De Minaur kept his focus as both men held service without facing a break point in a tense third set. Zverev ran out of steam in the tiebreak, going 6-2 down. He saved two set points before De Minaur edged into the final on his third match point after 2 hours and 31 minutes. "Super proud, super proud with how I handled the situation," De Minaur said at the end. "I was very calm. "I played a very aggressive tie-break. I played on my terms. I was going to go out swinging and playing the right type of tennis, and that's what made the difference today." Seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz extended his unbeaten ATP 500 run to 15 matches as he won 6-4, 7-6 (7/2) in 1hr 36min as Medvedev dug deep in a losing battle in the second set. Both De Minuar and Alcaraz will be appearing in their first Vienna final as they meet for the seventh time on tour and the third time in a championship match, after Queen's in 2023 and Rotterdam in 2025. The head-to-head, however, is heavily lopsided, with Alcaraz holding a perfect 6-0 record. "It's a great feeling, beating someone like Daniil on an indoor court, after the (run) he was having," Alcaraz said. "I'm really happy to have the chance to play another final, and my first one here in Vienna." For Medvedev, it was nonetheless a fruitful week as a fifth consecutive run to at least the last four of a tournament secured a place in the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin next month. De Minaur's win lifted him into the qualifying places for the Finals.

headline: Kane laments Dortmund draw after 'incredible high' of Ballon d'Or
description: Fabio Silva strikes late to earn Dortmund a 2-2 draw
author: AFP
article_text:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane criticised his own performance in Saturday's 2-2 home draw with Borussia Dortmund, just days after the "incredible high" of winning the Ballon d'Or. The draw leaves Bayern and Dortmund deadlocked on 18 points atop the Bundesliga table, with Kane's side ahead on goal difference. Kane won the award in his hometown of London on Monday, the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 and the first Bayern player in 45 years. The 33-year-old said winning the award was "one of the best feelings I've had in my career without a doubt", but said he was frustrated by his own performance on Saturday. The England captain, who took to the pitch wearing boots with gold studs, missed a second-half penalty and it was his wayward pass which Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck intercepted on the way to Dortmund's equaliser. "Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," Kane told reporters. "That's just part of being a striker, a footballer. "I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net. "You have to take it on the chin sometimes. It was an incredible week, but the focus for sure now is on the games ahead," said Kane, who revealed there would be a special presentation of the Ballon d'Or award with the England team during November's international break. After 73 goals for club and country last campaign, Kane has had a slow start by his standards. With eight Bundesliga games played, he has four goals but has turned provider, laying on six assists. Kane set up a late goal for Dayot Upamecano which made it 2-1, but former Wolverhampton forward Fabio Silva scored in the 89th-minute to make it 2-2. Bayern travel to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday but look set to be short staffed, particularly up front. "When you concede late, it always feels a lot worse," Kane said. "But, it's nothing to cry about, we have many games coming up and we've got to put this one behind us and look forward to Tuesday night." The Bavarian giants lost Michael Olise, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry during Saturday's match, adding to an injury list which already includes Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany is recovering from meningeal irritation. After collapsing on the training pitch last Friday, Kompany was released from hospital on Wednesday but will need more time to recover before returning to the dugout.

Galthie brings in five fresh faces for Nations Championship

France coach Fabien Galthie on Saturday called up five more players to his 42-man squad for the Nations Championship which kicks off on November 7 against Fiji in Lyon. Clermont prop Regis Montagne replaces Bayonne's Tevita Tatafu and Toulouse scrum-half Paul Graou comes in for La Rochelle's Nolann Le Garrec, who has picked up a new hamstring injury. Montpellier lock Florian Verhaeghe, Toulouse prop Rodrigue Neti and uncapped Clermont centre Leon Darricarrere complete the quintet. After opening their campaign against Fiji, France go on to host South Africa six days later and conclude against Argentina on November 21, with both matches at the Stade de France.

headline: Rubio says US open to role on Pakistan’s Afghan terror concerns
description: Secretary of state says Washington has heard Islamabad's concerns on Afghan-sponsored terrorism
author: Web Desk
article_text:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a press briefing on Saturday said Washington had "obviously heard" Pakistan's concerns regarding terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, adding that "if there's a productive role for us to play, we'll play it."

"Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan," Rubio said, addressing a briefing in Atlanta, Georgia. He added that Islamabad felt "as though the Taliban have not done enough to constrain those attacks and they've taken action against it."

The secretary of state added, "We obviously have heard those concerns on their part, we obviously don't want them to be targeted."

He also noted that Washington didn't "necessarily have the closest relationship with the Taliban," but that "we've heard the concerns that Pakistan has raised and we've seen some of those attacks that they point to."

Rubio concluded, "We're against terrorism no matter where it emanates from and who it targets."

His remarks came amid strained relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.

Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.

Security officials estimate that up to 70% of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.

The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.

In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.

headline: North Korea tests tactical ballistic missile cluster warhead
description: North Korea's research institutes say a Type-2 standard cluster warhead can devastate an area of up to 32 acres
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
North Korea conducted a test of a cluster warhead for a tactical ballistic missile to assess its combat applicability and destructive power, state media reported Sunday.

The Missile Administration carried out the test Saturday, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

The test was overseen by Gen Kim Jong Sik, a member of the Central Military Commission of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea and first deputy director of a department of the party's Central Committee.

North Korea's Ballistic Missile Systems Research Institute and Warhead Research Institute said the test confirmed that the country's "Type-2 standard cluster warhead" could devastate a target area of about 12 to 13 hectares (29 to 32 acres) at what they described as an "ultra-high density."

The head of the Missile Administration said North Korea classifies its cluster warheads into four categories, including special-purpose and standard types.

He said Pyongyang plans to make all four types available to military units by the end of this year, allowing them to select warheads according to operational objectives and the characteristics of targets.

The Missile Administration described the test as part of regular scientific research aimed at increasing the destructive power of its weapons systems.

Pyongyang has ramped up its show of force in recent weeks with multiple missile tests and holding a drone exhibition. Analysts said the tests could be part of efforts to modernise the military. North Korea gained experience in modern warfare, sending troops to the war in Ukraine for its ally Moscow.

North Korea test-fired around 10 ballistic missiles from its east coast towards the sea on Thursday, when German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited South Korea for a summit.

headline: Shaheen eyes Test comeback
description: Pakistan ODI captain says backing players will bring better performances
author: Our Correspondent
article_text: Pakistan’s ace pacer and ODI team captain Shaheen Afridi has missed the country’s previous two major tours of the West Indies and England. He was in good form but was overlooked for those series. He has also not been drafted in the Test squad for the home series against Sri Lanka which will begin soon. He is now eyeing a return to Test cricket and expressed this desire at a news conference after guiding his side to a title-winning triumph in the ODI tri-series, which concluded at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Saturday night. “I cannot say anything about the board’s decisions. As far as Test cricket and T20 cricket are concerned, I want to make a comeback to Test cricket. For this, I am going to play a first-class game for FATA. There are still many areas for improvement, and I will work towards making a comeback,” Shaheen told reporters. Shaheen used his experience and led from the front in the ODI tri-series, finishing with ten wickets, the second highest wicket-taker of the series. Shaheen said there was a long way to go and that a couple of wins should not satisfy the team. “It’s good that Pakistan had some good moments. There is still more tough cricket ahead, with the Asia Cup and a series against England in England. One or two wins should not satisfy us. We have to win more series and matches, InshaAllah,” Shaheen said. “In the home series against Ireland, we will try to add more new players to the Shaheens team,” he said. Shaheen said that if players were backed, good performances would follow. “Players should be backed. Big decisions about players should not be taken on the basis of failures in one or two series. Fakhar Zaman is a big example. He did not score in the first four matches, but he is the kind of player who kept batting despite an injury and scored a hundred. His innings included singles and doubles also. If you back players, this type of performance will follow,” Shaheen said. He also praised Saad Baig and Arafat Minhas for their performances. “Yes, Saad and Arafat Minhas played a good series,” Shaheen said. He said Babar knew his game well. “If you talk about Babar, he knows his game and is going to play a first-class match within two days. He is clear about how to bat. Unfortunately, he faced some difficult dismissals, but that is part of cricket, and he will come back,” Shaheen said. Shaheen said the tri-series had been a good contest, adding that England and Sri Lanka were major sides. “You need such wins against teams like Sri Lanka and England. Sri Lanka have played top cricket. No one expected them to beat England, and they scored 300-plus three times. So it was a good series, and good cricket was played,” Shaheen said. “I think we played good cricket,” he added. He also defended Naseem Shah, who conceded 80 runs in the final. “Naseem was doing his best. The way things were going earlier, fast bowlers were not getting much assistance. We started bowling across the seam and thought that reverse swing could come into play towards the end. We planned to use slower balls, bouncers and yorkers to control Sri Lanka in the end. Naseem has played enough cricket. If you have to tell him what to do on every ball, then he should be playing Under-16 cricket,” Shaheen said. Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka by three wickets on Saturday night to win the tri-series. Pakistan lost just one of their five matches in the tournament.

headline: Barca hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
description: Raphinha and Yamal score twice each in a 6-1 rout
author: AFP
article_text:
Raphinha and Lamine Yamal each struck twice as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. "It was a hard week for us, there was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans (to bounce back)," Lopez told Movistar. "They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha, with them we will achieve big things." There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form after Lopez teed him up. Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead himself in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, he smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. Barcelona host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday and travel to face Atletico next Sunday in a table-topping La Liga clash. Alaves have now gone seven matches without a win, but are 10th. "We have to turn the page quickly," said midfielder Ander Guevara. "We don't need to sound the alarms, we know we're on a bad run, but we're a mature and humble team."

Seven in a row

Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. "I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. "We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game." Alex Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones. "I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures. rbs/lp

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal each struck twice as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats.

Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou.

Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more.

Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval.

Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves.

"It was a hard week for us, there was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans (to bounce back)," Lopez told Movistar.

"They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha, with them we will achieve big things."

There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week.

Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions.

Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form after Lopez teed him up.

Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead himself in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, he smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it.

Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal.

Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera.

Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time.

Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up.

Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal.

Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on.

Barcelona host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday and travel to face Atletico next Sunday in a table-topping La Liga clash.

Alaves have now gone seven matches without a win, but are 10th.

"We have to turn the page quickly," said midfielder Ander Guevara. "We don't need to sound the alarms, we know we're on a bad run, but we're a mature and humble team."
Seven in a row

Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante.

Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.

"I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar.

"We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game."

Alex Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones.

"I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011.

On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures.

headline: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment protests turn violent
description: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of $245, citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and ​healthcare
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh announced a six-member wage board on Sunday to review garment workers' pay and urged employees to return to work, but ​protests demanding higher wages continued across major industrial areas, disrupting transport ‌and factory operations.

Workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and ​healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.

The dispute has raised concerns about ​disruption to an industry that employs about 4 million workers, generates more ⁠than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western ​brands.

Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the wage board was formed after ​discussions with workers' representatives and industry leaders and urged workers to resume work.

Despite the announcement, thousands of garment workers staged fresh demonstrations on Sunday.

Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse ​workers who had blocked a busy intersection in Dhaka, police said. Some protesters hurled ​bricks at officers during the clashes.

Hundreds of workers also blocked a major highway in Gazipur, on ‌the ⁠outskirts of the capital, disrupting transport in one of the country's key industrial belts.

The demonstrations forced owners to shut 25 to 30 factories, while authorities deployed Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to maintain order, Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amjad Hossain said.

The latest ​unrest follows demonstrations in ​Ashulia, a major ⁠garment manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, where dozens of factories suspended operations on Saturday after workers staged protests demanding ​higher pay.

Chowdhury warned that prolonged disruptions could delay export shipments ​and payments ⁠from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers alike.

Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry, the world's largest after China, contributes about 10% of gross domestic product and is the ⁠backbone of ​the economy.

Manufacturers, however, said the sector is facing mounting challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions ​in the Middle East.
