headline: Pakistan beat Oman to win HK Sixes Plate final
description: Abbas smashes 11 sixes in his 16-ball 73 as Pakistan post 154 in six overs
author: Our Correspondent
article_text: Skipper Abbas Afridi smashed an unbeaten 73 off 16 balls as Pakistan defeated Oman by 18 runs in the Plate final of the Hong Kong International Sixes tournament at Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok on Sunday. Pakistan, batting first after Oman elected to field, piled up a massive 154-4 in their allotted six overs, with Abbas leading the charge through a breathtaking display of power-hitting. Abbas struck 11 sixes and one four at a remarkable strike rate of 456.25, providing the backbone of Pakistan’s explosive total. He was well supported by Abdul Samad, who hammered 32 off just seven deliveries, including four sixes and two fours. The pair added valuable runs to keep Pakistan on course for a huge total before Samad was caught and bowled by Muzahir Raza. Ahmed Daniyal provided a late flourish with an unbeaten 25 off five balls, smashing four sixes. Muhammad Shahzad also contributed 13 off four deliveries, including two sixes, before retiring out. Khawaja Nafay gave Pakistan a brisk start with seven off three balls, including a six, while Irfan Khan was dismissed for a duck. Muzahir Raza was the pick of Oman’s bowlers, claiming two wickets for 46 runs in his two overs, while Usman Ali took one wicket. In reply, Oman put up a spirited fight but finished at 136-4 in their six overs, falling 18 runs short of the target. Zohaib Amanat remained unbeaten on 61 off 18 balls, hitting eight sixes and three fours, while Usman Ali smashed an unbeaten 67 off 17 deliveries, including eight sixes and four fours. The pair launched a remarkable counterattack, adding 37 runs in the remaining part of the innings after Oman had lost their first wicket. However, the required run rate proved too steep for the chasing side. Oman captain Aamir Kaleem was run out for a duck, while Sami Hassan, Shafiq Jan and Muzahir Raza retired out without scoring. Abbas Afridi was named player of the match for his match-winning innings.

headline: Iran ready for both ‘defence and diplomacy’, says Araghchi as Tehran, Qatari mediators hold third day of talks
description: Trump says US still has to 'take care of' one or two targets in Iran, could do it in 10 minutes
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iran's Foreign ⁠Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy", adding that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks ​was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators.

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

Speaking ​to state media, Araghchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.

Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Araghchi as saying in an interview on Saturday that Iranian and Qatari ​negotiators had developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days ​of a potential agreement with Washington.

"We are doing our best in this process, and we hope that there is rationality on the other side so that they prioritise diplomacy ​over other paths," Araghchi ​said of the ⁠talks with Qatari officials.

Iran boosting military capabilities to respond ‘without geographical limits’: defence minister

Iran was rapidly strengthening its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond “without geographical limits,” Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said on Sunday.

Speaking to reporters, Akhlaghi said Iran was moving “resolutely” to enhance its armed forces’ smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

“We are rapidly increasing our armed forces’ combat capabilities to be able to respond without geographical limits,” he said.

Iran “will not be caught off guard, nor will we be stopped, and any type of attack will receive an appropriate, decisive and effective response,” he added.

Akhlaghi stressed that Iran “would not be surprised by threats, halted by pressure or dependent on the will of others in pursuing scientific and technological progress.”

His remarks come as Qatar and Pakistan continue mediation efforts to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran, amid reports of progress in indirect talks in Doha.

The efforts seek understandings on Iran’s nuclear program, sanctions relief and the security of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the US-Iran war, official says

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

The talks come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the November 3 US midterm elections. President Donald Trump has said the US will not launch new attacks on Iran before the vote and that talks with Tehran have been productive, though he has not ruled out further military action thereafter.

Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries, as the eight-month-old war continues to disrupt global oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday for discussions with Iranian officials before moving the talks to Doha on Saturday, an official had told Reuters. The talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington, the official added.

Trump says US could strike Iran's remaining nuclear sites in '10 minutes'

United States President Donald Trump on Saturday said that Washington could strike Iran's remaining suspected nuclear facilities in "10 minutes," signaling the possibility of further military action despite ongoing diplomatic negotiations.

Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that US military operations had severely weakened Iran's armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only a few sites to be targeted.

"We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes. So, we have that plan," Trump said. "You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected Iranian nuclear facility.

Trump made the remarks when asked whether there was a timeline for ongoing Qatari-mediated negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

He said the US was not in a hurry to reach an agreement, claiming that American military operations had destroyed much of Iran's navy, air force, air defences, military equipment and nuclear infrastructure.

Asked whether Washington could resume military operations against Iran as soon as this week, Trump declined to provide a direct answer. "Why would you ask such a stupid question?" he said, before adding: "I can't tell you."

Trump also reiterated Washington's opposition to Iran acquiring nuclear weapons. "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They want to make a deal; we'll find out about that," he said.

Asked about the progress of negotiations, Trump expressed skepticism about Tehran's reliability despite describing the talks as progressing. "They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. I will tell you, they make a deal and then they back out. They want to make a deal. We'll see if they make a deal," he said.

Iran designates UK's Royal Navy, Air Force as 'terrorist' organisations

Iran designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist" organisations and its foreign intelligence agency MI6 as a "hostile group" on Sunday, according to the Iranian Foreign Ministry.

In a statement carried by state-run news agency IRNA, the ministry said the move came in response to London's "malicious" actions, particularly its designation of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a "terrorist organisation."

The ministry said the decision was taken under a resolution by Iran's Supreme National Security Council and followed the United Kingdom's designation of the IRGC under the State Threats Act 2026 on July 13.

Tehran also accused London of participating in the United States-Israeli war against Iran by providing access to military and logistical bases and facilities under British jurisdiction.

IRGC commander says military 'fully prepared for any scenario enemy may devise'

IRGC's Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani said that Tehran's military was “fully prepared for any scenario the enemy may devise" and that forces were operating on the assumption that the US or Israel could strike at any moment, Al Jazeera reported.

Javani, cited by Al Jazeera, told Iran's Fars News Agency that Tehran would not be caught off guard and would respond as necessary.

The deputy also noted that Tehran's military capabilities now allowed it to confront the enemy defensively and as well as through preemptive and offensive operations.

According to Al Jazeera, Javani said Iran could inflict heavy, devastating strikes on US warships and warned that any region that enemy forces try to enter, whether by air assault or across a border, would become a “killing ground” for them.

Separately, Iran's army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia warned that any renewed US aggression would be met with an "immediate, decisive" response on a “larger” scale than before, Press TV reported.

The spokesperson added that in the event of a new war, its scope will not be confined to West Asia, Press TV said.

At least three wounded in air raids on Yemen oil facility

Al Jazeera reported that two air raids hit an oil facility in Yemen’s Hodeidah, citing Al Masirah TV.

It added that the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis had conducted two raids on an oil facility in Bajil district in the western Hodeidah governorate, with at least three civilians wounded.

Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

Despite subsequent diplomatic efforts and a memorandum signed by Washington and Tehran in June, tensions have persisted over security arrangements and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's Foreign ⁠Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy", adding that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators.

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

Speaking to state media, Araghchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.

Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Araghchi as saying in an interview on Saturday that Iranian and Qatari negotiators had developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a potential agreement with Washington.

"We are doing our best in this process, and we hope that there is rationality on the other side so that they prioritise diplomacy over other paths," Araghchi said of the ⁠talks with Qatari officials.

Iran boosting military capabilities to respond ‘without geographical limits’: defence minister

Iran was rapidly strengthening its armed forces’ combat capabilities to enable them to respond “without geographical limits,” Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi said on Sunday.

Speaking to reporters, Akhlaghi said Iran was moving “resolutely” to enhance its armed forces’ smart combat capabilities under directives from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

“We are rapidly increasing our armed forces’ combat capabilities to be able to respond without geographical limits,” he said.

Iran “will not be caught off guard, nor will we be stopped, and any type of attack will receive an appropriate, decisive and effective response,” he added.

Akhlaghi stressed that Iran “would not be surprised by threats, halted by pressure or dependent on the will of others in pursuing scientific and technological progress.”

His remarks come as Qatar and Pakistan continue mediation efforts to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran, amid reports of progress in indirect talks in Doha.

The efforts seek understandings on Iran’s nuclear program, sanctions relief and the security of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the US-Iran war, official says

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

The talks come amid concerns that the conflict could escalate again after the November 3 US midterm elections. President Donald Trump has said the US will not launch new attacks on Iran before the vote and that talks with Tehran have been productive, though he has not ruled out further military action thereafter.

Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries, as the eight-month-old war continues to disrupt global oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei issued a statement on Saturday ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday for discussions with Iranian officials before moving the talks to Doha on Saturday, an official had told Reuters. The talks were being coordinated in regular contacts with Washington, the official added.

Trump says US could strike Iran's remaining nuclear sites in '10 minutes'

United States President Donald Trump on Saturday said that Washington could strike Iran's remaining suspected nuclear facilities in "10 minutes," signaling the possibility of further military action despite ongoing diplomatic negotiations.

Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, Trump claimed that US military operations had severely weakened Iran's armed forces and nuclear infrastructure, leaving only a few sites to be targeted.

"We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes. So, we have that plan," Trump said. "You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected Iranian nuclear facility.

Trump made the remarks when asked whether there was a timeline for ongoing Qatari-mediated negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

He said the US was not in a hurry to reach an agreement, claiming that American military operations had destroyed much of Iran's navy, air force, air defences, military equipment and nuclear infrastructure.

Asked whether Washington could resume military operations against Iran as soon as this week, Trump declined to provide a direct answer. "Why would you ask such a stupid question?" he said, before adding: "I can't tell you."

Trump also reiterated Washington's opposition to Iran acquiring nuclear weapons. "Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They want to make a deal; we'll find out about that," he said.

Asked about the progress of negotiations, Trump expressed skepticism about Tehran's reliability despite describing the talks as progressing. "They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. I will tell you, they make a deal and then they back out. They want to make a deal. We'll see if they make a deal," he said.

Iran designates UK's Royal Navy, Air Force as 'terrorist' organisations

Iran designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as "terrorist" organisations and its foreign intelligence agency MI6 as a "hostile group" on Sunday, according to the Iranian Foreign Ministry.

In a statement carried by state-run news agency IRNA, the ministry said the move came in response to London's "malicious" actions, particularly its designation of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a "terrorist organisation."

The ministry said the decision was taken under a resolution by Iran's Supreme National Security Council and followed the United Kingdom's designation of the IRGC under the State Threats Act 2026 on July 13.

Tehran also accused London of participating in the United States-Israeli war against Iran by providing access to military and logistical bases and facilities under British jurisdiction.

IRGC commander says military 'fully prepared for any scenario enemy may devise'

IRGC's Deputy for Political Affairs Brigadier-General Yadollah Javani said that Tehran's military was “fully prepared for any scenario the enemy may devise" and that forces were operating on the assumption that the US or Israel could strike at any moment, Al Jazeera reported.

Javani, cited by Al Jazeera, told Iran's Fars News Agency that Tehran would not be caught off guard and would respond as necessary.

The deputy also noted that Tehran's military capabilities now allowed it to confront the enemy defensively and as well as through preemptive and offensive operations.

According to Al Jazeera, Javani said Iran could inflict heavy, devastating strikes on US warships and warned that any region that enemy forces try to enter, whether by air assault or across a border, would become a “killing ground” for them.

Separately, Iran's army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia warned that any renewed US aggression would be met with an "immediate, decisive" response on a “larger” scale than before, Press TV reported.

The spokesperson added that in the event of a new war, its scope will not be confined to West Asia, Press TV said.

At least three wounded in air raids on Yemen oil facility

Al Jazeera reported that two air raids hit an oil facility in Yemen’s Hodeidah, citing Al Masirah TV.

It added that the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis had conducted two raids on an oil facility in Bajil district in the western Hodeidah governorate, with at least three civilians wounded.

Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

Despite subsequent diplomatic efforts and a memorandum signed by Washington and Tehran in June, tensions have persisted over security arrangements and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Roma thrash Udinese ahead of Milan derby
description: Cristante, Mora, Malen and Ndicka strike before Ghilardi seals the 5-2 win
author: AFP
article_text:
AC Milan inflicted a first defeat of the season on rivals Inter Milan with a 3-1 win in a derby thriller on Saturday, as Roma cut the gap to first place to one point. Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot struck inside the opening 10 minutes to get the Rossoneri off to a dream start before Alessandro Bastoni pulled one back. An inspired Diego Moreira proved to be Milan's hero as the Belgian, having assisted the first two goals, swept home a free-kick late in the first half to restore a two-goal cushion as Ruben Amorim's side responded well to suffering their first league defeat of the season at home to Bologna in midweek. "The environment is amazing," Amorim told DAZN. "The passion is completely different from any derby I have played." "I'm really happy for the players. It was important. The fans gained a little bit more confidence in the project. We are going to have amazing nights like today and we are going to have nights like Bologna, that is part of the process." Milan's victory stretched their unbeaten record in the famous fixture to eight games as Amorim's side moved into fourth place, four points off Inter and Lazio on top. Roma's 5-2 win at Udinese moved them one point behind Inter in third. Two days after plans were revealed for both clubs to move into a new stadium in 2031, the iconic 100-year-old Stadio Giuseppe Meazza was at its atmospheric best for AC Milan's 'home' game. Milan looked fired up from the first whistle as they raced into an early lead, Pulisic heading home an inviting Moreira cross inside four minutes in the week the American signed a five-year contract extension with the Rossoneri. Moreira was the architect again when Milan doubled their lead, fizzing a corner into the path of Rabiot, who swept a clever finish through a crowded box and in off the far post. Inter hit back with a corner of their own midway through an electric first half when Bastoni nodded in from close range. The goal sparked a period of dominance from the Nerazzurri, but they could not beat an inspired Mike Maignan, who produced a sharp save on Hakan Calhanoglu before an outstanding one-handed reaction stop denied Djed Spence what had seemed a certain goal. With Inter in the ascendancy, Milan hit back against the run of play when Moreira curled a free-kick over the wall and into the top corner two minutes before the break. The frenetic nature of the game calmed in the second half as a cagier affair unfolded, Inter probing to get back in the game as Carlos Augusto headed wide from a promising position. An incorrect decision to award Inter a penalty for handball was overturned following a VAR intervention as the Nerazzurri were left frustrated in their hunt for another goal, Milan substitute Alphadjo Cisse instead coming closest late on with a curling strike that required a flying save from Josep Martinez.

Roma reduce gap

Roma blew away struggling Udinese with a rampant first-half display to claim a 5-2 away win and move one point off top. Gian Piero Gasperini's unbeaten side moved up to 24 points, one behind joint-leaders Inter and Lazio, who can pull clear on top when they host Cagliari in Rome on Sunday. Bryan Cristante, Rodrigo Mora, Donyell Malen and Evan Ndicka all struck before half-time and the woodwork twice denied the visitors in a dazzling show of attacking force. Nicolo Zaniolo scored against his former club and Matteo Palma struck with a volley as Udinese improved after the break, but Daniele Ghilardi made it five in stoppage time to leave the hosts in 19th on five points after an eight-match winless run. Earlier, Bologna claimed a third consecutive win to climb into eighth place as they came from behind to beat Monza 2-1. League top scorer Gustavo Varela bagged his ninth goal of the season from the spot to put the visitors in front, but Tommaso Pobega and Federico Bernardeschi hit back before Bologna goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski saved a late Patrick Cutrone penalty.

headline: Thierry Henry sees Pirates beat Chiefs in Soweto derby
description: Moremi's 55th-minute strike settles the contest as Pirates move within a point of leaders Sundowns
author: AFP
article_text: Tshepang Moremi scored after 55 minutes to give Orlando Pirates 2-1 victory over Kaizer Chiefs on Saturday in a South African Premiership match watched by a capacity 90,000 crowd. Victory kept Pirates second after nine rounds, one point behind Mamelodi Sundowns, who have played an additional match. French legend Thierry Henry was a special guest for the Soweto derby between the two most popular clubs in the country. Henry delivered the match ball, received sustained applause, and posed with the captains, Pirates centre-back Nkosinathi Sibisi and Chiefs goalkeeper Brandon Petersen. Chiefs, three places behind Pirates in fifth, were the superior side in the opening half and the 1-1 half-time scoreline flattered Pirates. Pirates led after 24 minutes when Thabo Moloisane deflected a Yanela Mbuthuma shot across Petersen and into the far corner of the net. Chiefs levelled six minutes later as Pirates goalkeeper Sipho Chaine spilled a cross and Pule Mmodi tapped the loose ball over the goalline. Much improved in the second half after personnel and tactical changes, Pirates regained the lead when Moremi side-footed a Thapelo Mokobodi cross into the net. South African international Moremi could have claimed a hat-trick. In the closing stages his chip rebounded off the crossbar, then he fired wide when a goal seemed inevitable. Chiefs were reduced to 10 men in added time when Angolan centre-back Inacio Miguel was sent off after being yellow-carded twice. "We were efficient, resilient and ruthless," said Pirates Moroccan coach Abdeslam Ouaddou, a former Premier League defender with Fulham. Chiefs' French coach Fernando Da Cruz lamented missed chances in the opening half: "We should have been two or three goals ahead by half-time." Later, recent signing Thabang Matuludi scored twice from headers as Sundowns overcame lowly Durban City 4-1 in Rustenburg.

headline: Kamindu says dew factor favours Pakistan
description: Top-order batsman says Sri Lanka fall 20-30 runs short, rues fielding lapses
author: Sports Desk
article_text: Sri Lanka’s top order batsman Kamindu Mendis said the dew factor played a significant role in Pakistan's three-wicket victory in the ODI tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Saturday, while admitting that his team were 20 to 30 runs short of a competitive total. Kamindu, who struck a brilliant 131 in the final, said he enjoyed his innings but was disappointed that his team ended up on the losing side. “First of all, I enjoyed my knock, but we are still on the losing side. I think we were 20 to 25 runs short, to be honest,” he said at the post-match news conference. He also praised Pakistan's Fakhar Zaman for his match-winning century but acknowledged that Sri Lanka made mistakes in the field. “I think Fakhar Zaman played really well. We made some mistakes in the field, but that can happen in the game of cricket. Still, Fakhar played a very good innings,” Kamindu said. He said Sri Lanka would now look forward to red-ball cricket, adding that the team had several positives to build on. “It's a good sign to move on to red-ball cricket. We have been doing really well in red-ball cricket as well. I think we have a good coach and a good environment. There are so many positives within our team, and going forward, we are doing much better. We are improving each and every day and in every game. I think we will be doing really well soon,” he said. Reflecting on the final, Kamindu said Sri Lanka's bowlers had made a good start but gave credit to Fakhar and Saad Baig for their outstanding batting. “It was a really good start from our bowlers, but credit goes to Saad and Fakhar. I think they played really well. The dew factor was also a huge advantage for them, but they played really good cricket,” he said. Kamindu also welcomed the concept of tri-series tournaments, saying they provided competitive cricket. “I think playing a tri-series is really good because there is always competition. Whoever performs better on the day wins the game. So I think a tri-series is a good thing to have,” he said. The Sri Lankan batter also spoke highly of his compatriots Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage. Talking about Rathnayake, Kamindu said they had played together at the same club in Sri Lanka for a long time and he had always believed his teammate had the potential to become a world-class player. “I have been playing with him since my early days. We played for the same club in Sri Lanka. I always thought he would become a great, world-class player. He is a really good player,” he said. Praising Liyanage, Kamindu said he had been performing consistently in ODI cricket since making his debut. “Talking about Janith, I think he has been doing really well in ODI cricket since his debut. He is a great player as well,” he added.

“First of all, I enjoyed my knock, but we are still on the losing side. I think we were 20 to 25 runs short, to be honest,” he said at the post-match news conference.

He also praised Pakistan's Fakhar Zaman for his match-winning century but acknowledged that Sri Lanka made mistakes in the field.

“I think Fakhar Zaman played really well. We made some mistakes in the field, but that can happen in the game of cricket. Still, Fakhar played a very good innings,” Kamindu said.

He said Sri Lanka would now look forward to red-ball cricket, adding that the team had several positives to build on.

“It's a good sign to move on to red-ball cricket. We have been doing really well in red-ball cricket as well. I think we have a good coach and a good environment. There are so many positives within our team, and going forward, we are doing much better. We are improving each and every day and in every game. I think we will be doing really well soon,” he said.

Reflecting on the final, Kamindu said Sri Lanka's bowlers had made a good start but gave credit to Fakhar and Saad Baig for their outstanding batting.

“It was a really good start from our bowlers, but credit goes to Saad and Fakhar. I think they played really well. The dew factor was also a huge advantage for them, but they played really good cricket,” he said.

Kamindu also welcomed the concept of tri-series tournaments, saying they provided competitive cricket.

“I think playing a tri-series is really good because there is always competition. Whoever performs better on the day wins the game. So I think a tri-series is a good thing to have,” he said.

The Sri Lankan batter also spoke highly of his compatriots Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage.

Talking about Rathnayake, Kamindu said they had played together at the same club in Sri Lanka for a long time and he had always believed his teammate had the potential to become a world-class player.

“I have been playing with him since my early days. We played for the same club in Sri Lanka. I always thought he would become a great, world-class player. He is a really good player,” he said.

Praising Liyanage, Kamindu said he had been performing consistently in ODI cricket since making his debut.

“Talking about Janith, I think he has been doing really well in ODI cricket since his debut. He is a great player as well,” he added.

headline: Saad, Minhas hail team's fighting spirit
description: Youngsters say belief and partnerships seal 326-run chase against Sri Lanka
author: Our Correspondent
article_text: Youngsters Saad Baig and Arafat Minhas played pivotal roles in Pakistan's three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final, producing impressive performances to help the hosts chase down a challenging target of 326 at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Saturday. Saad struck a fluent 74 off 75 balls, while Arafat smashed a blistering 61 off just 31 deliveries as Pakistan recovered from early setbacks to seal the title with nine balls to spare. Saad, who shared a crucial 149-run third-wicket partnership with Fakhar Zaman, said the team's collective effort throughout the tournament had been outstanding. “The chase was not easy, but the way we played today was tremendous. It was an outstanding performance from our team,” Saad said. The wicket-keeper batsman admitted that he felt the pressure after failing to make significant contributions in his previous three outings but said he was determined to bat deep in the final. “Definitely, there is pressure when you come into the international circuit. I got out inside 30 runs in last few games, so this time I planned to bat deep. We had lost two early wickets, but the way Fakhar Bhai played that outstanding innings made things easier for us,” he said. Meanwhile all-rounder Arafat Minhas said that he and Hasan Nawaz knew that they could chase that. Minhas said he and Hasan Nawaz backed each other when they came together at a crucial stage of the chase. “When I went out to bat, I spoke to Hasan and told him that we had already been through such situations. We tried to build a partnership and reminded each other that we had the ability to chase the target. We backed each other, waited for the bad deliveries and had confidence in one another,” he said. “I am extremely happy that we have won the series. I think such opportunities will come in the future as well, and we will keep winning,” he added. Minhas also dedicated his performance to his family, who were present at the ground to witness his contribution. “I dedicate my performance to my family, as they have been supporting me for a long time. They were also present at the ground today and must have enjoyed the game,” he said. His explosive 61, which included four sixes and three fours, came at a crucial stage after Fakhar's dismissal and helped Pakistan move closer to victory. The young all-rounder's contribution, alongside Hasan Nawaz's unbeaten 37, ensured that Sri Lanka's late fightback could not prevent Pakistan from lifting the trophy.

headline: Shnaider beats Fernandez to win Tokyo title
description: The Russian overcomes Fernandez 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to claim her first title of the season
author: AFP
article_text: Russia's Diana Shnaider won her first title of the year with a hard-fought victory over Leylah Fernandez in Tokyo on Sunday and couldn't wait to tell her mum all about it. The world number 13 beat Canada's Fernandez 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win the Pan Pacific Open and then went straight to her phone to call home. "I was calling my mum -- I wanted to hear her voice after winning a title and share a first few moments with her," the 22-year-old Shnaider said. "She said 'you've just finished and already you're calling me'." It was Shnaider's first title since Monterrey in August last year and the sixth of her career. She looked to be cruising to victory after winning the first set and taking a 4-0 lead in the second. World number 23 Fernandez came back to win the second set, but Shnaider regained control to close out the match. "It was definitely a tight, close match," Shnaider said. "It makes me even more happy that I was able to fight for the title and in the end win it." Fernandez went into the final with 16 wins in her previous 20 matches. That run included victory at the Singapore Open in September and a runner-up finish at last week's Ningbo Open in China behind world number one Elena Rybakina. Fernandez struggled with her serve, double-faulting five times throughout the match and landing only half of her first serves in the first set. She got it together when it mattered though, stunning Shnaider in the second set with some tenacious tennis to even the score at one set each. Shnaider regained her composure when she returned for the final set, breaking Fernandez's serve twice and clinching the title with her first match point. She was appearing in her first final of the year after losing in the semi-finals four times before this week. "Very happy that I was able to win the title," she said. "It definitely means a lot to me, to my team, my family to finish on a high note." Fernandez shed tears as she thanked her family in her on-court interview and said that she had received some "bad news".

headline: Marquez wins in Malaysia to close in on MotoGP world title
description: The Spaniard takes his seventh win of the season to move closer to an eighth MotoGP crown
author: AFP
article_text: Marc Marquez moved to within touching distance of an eighth world title with an imperious victory at the Malaysian MotoGP on Sunday. The Ducati star romped to a dominant win in 40min 14.236sec, finishing 4.172sec ahead of Red Bull's Pedro Acosta as his younger brother Alex Marquez came third, almost six seconds adrift. Marquez is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin after a seventh victory this season. It was also his third triumph in Malaysia in the MotoGP class, having last won in Sepang back in 2018. With Aprilia's Martin missing the Sepang weekend with a broken wrist, his fellow Spaniard Marquez can seal the championship next weekend in Qatar. "Closer, but not done," the 33-year-old Marquez said of the championship race. "So in the end, same mentality. Try to keep pushing, try to be super focused because there are not many races to go, but many moments to go." After Qatar there are just two weekends left in the campaign. Marquez wasted no time in snatching the lead from his brother as the riders came into Turn 1 from the start, and the siblings briefly traded places before the older Marquez edged ahead in scorching conditions. Marquez began to pull away from the chasing pack to develop a 1.7 sec advantage over his brother, who was valiantly defending his second spot against Acosta. Acosta was rewarded for his persistence as the Red Rull rider snatched second place from Alex Marquez on Lap 10. At the front Marquez coasted to victory unchallenged to continue his purple streak in the second half of the 2026 season. Despite closing in on another world title, Marquez refused to get carried away. "Looks like this weekend I took Alex Marquez's skills in Malaysia because I was riding exactly like how he rode last year when he won," said Marquez. Alex Marquez said he will undergo right shoulder surgery in Madrid after this, ultimately ruling him out of the Qatar race next week. "It's time to take that surgery and try to come back stronger in Valencia," he said, referring to the last race of the season.

headline: Kundi says K-P's people will have 'first right' to province’s natural resources
description: Governor urges religious scholars to play their role in promoting peace, says people listen and respect their views
author: Wisal Yousafzai
article_text:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday said the province's people would have the "first right" to its natural resources, pledging that their interests would remain his priority while he held office.

Addressing a ceremony marking the annual Urs of Darbar-e-Aalia Murshidabad Sharif in Peshawar, Kundi said the province was rich in natural resources, including gas, minerals, electricity and oil.

“My first priority is the protection of the people. As long as I hold this office, the first right over our resources will belong to the people of our province,” he said.

Kundi said residents of K-P had made immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, adding that restoring peace required collective efforts. “Although we may have differences on many issues, we must stand united to establish peace in the province,” he said.

He said the province had suffered from terrorism for a long time, with schoolchildren, security forces, police personnel and journalists among those who had made countless sacrifices for peace.

“Our mission is to make the province a cradle of peace,” he said.

The governor highlighted that his first priority was to restore peace. He added that the people of the province had distinguished themselves in various fields, adding that more than half of the national cricket team's players belonged to K-P. “We have immense talent in the field of sports,” he said.

Kundi also urged religious scholars to play their role in promoting peace, saying people listened to and respected their views.

He said children wanted to lead full and peaceful lives, while residents sought opportunities for business and employment.

“It is our shared responsibility to play our full part in the development, prosperity and peace of the province,” he said, adding that the government would welcome constructive suggestions for improving the province and its cities.

The governor also pledged to work with all stakeholders to bring peace, prosperity and development to K-P.

Mineral rights

On October 11, Governor's rule and an emergency were imposed, transferring executive authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf-led provincial government to the governor. An 11-member advisory council was formed to assist him in overseeing provincial administrative affairs.

The federal government also established a separate administrative structure for 12 districts, including an Area Representative and Development Council to facilitate local representation and development planning.

On October 17, six days after governor’s rule was imposed, Kundi said the province’s mineral resources would be extracted and sold, inviting domestic and foreign companies to invest through joint ventures with Pakistani firms and local communities.

“Our province is rich in minerals, and we will extract and sell these minerals. We will have many agreements signed so that people can prosper,” he said. He argued that such partnerships would create jobs, support local businesses and improve economic conditions, and also called for the extraction of the province’s oil and gas reserves.

The remarks fuelled concerns among opposition parties that governor’s rule could be used to gain control over the province’s mineral wealth. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry subsequently rejected any link between the imposition of the emergency and mineral extraction, saying the move had been made to address the security situation.

He also said the federal government had maintained that K-P and Balochistan would have the first right to their respective mineral resources, with the proceeds spent on provincial development.

The question of control over the province's mineral resources has been contentious for a while. In April 2025, political parties across the provincial assembly opposed the proposed Mines and Minerals Bill, arguing that it threatened provincial autonomy and the assembly's authority over natural resources.

In January this year, a separate Mineral Development and Management Company Bill triggered criticism from PTI leaders and supporters. The provincial government defended the legislation as a measure to regulate the mining sector and ensure that local communities benefited from mineral wealth. However, its implementation was subsequently put on hold amid public and political backlash.

On October 11, Governor's rule and an emergency were imposed, transferring executive authority from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf-led provincial government to the governor. An 11-member advisory council was formed to assist him in overseeing provincial administrative affairs.

The federal government also established a separate administrative structure for 12 districts, including an Area Representative and Development Council to facilitate local representation and development planning.

On October 17, six days after governor’s rule was imposed, Kundi said the province’s mineral resources would be extracted and sold, inviting domestic and foreign companies to invest through joint ventures with Pakistani firms and local communities.

“Our province is rich in minerals, and we will extract and sell these minerals. We will have many agreements signed so that people can prosper,” he said. He argued that such partnerships would create jobs, support local businesses and improve economic conditions, and also called for the extraction of the province’s oil and gas reserves.

The remarks fuelled concerns among opposition parties that governor’s rule could be used to gain control over the province’s mineral wealth. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry subsequently rejected any link between the imposition of the emergency and mineral extraction, saying the move had been made to address the security situation.
He also said the federal government had maintained that K-P and Balochistan would have the first right to their respective mineral resources, with the proceeds spent on provincial development.

The question of control over the province's mineral resources has been contentious for a while. In April 2025, political parties across the provincial assembly opposed the proposed Mines and Minerals Bill, arguing that it threatened provincial autonomy and the assembly's authority over natural resources.

In January this year, a separate Mineral Development and Management Company Bill triggered criticism from PTI leaders and supporters. The provincial government defended the legislation as a measure to regulate the mining sector and ensure that local communities benefited from mineral wealth. However, its implementation was subsequently put on hold amid public and political backlash.

headline: Robert Downey Jr and Pedro Pascal swap MCU roles for Halloween ahead of ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description: 'Avengers: Doomsday' is scheduled to open in cinemas on December 18, 2026
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal have celebrated Halloween with a playful Marvel Cinematic Universe costume swap, trading their upcoming Avengers: Doomsday characters in a surprise video shared on social media.

Downey, who is set to play Doctor Doom in the upcoming film, dressed as Pascal’s character Reed Richards, also known as Mister Fantastic. Pascal, meanwhile, donned Doctor Doom’s signature mask and costume, swapping identities with his co-star for the spooky occasion.

Downey shared the video on Instagram on October 31, captioning it: “Victor. Richard. Costume swap!”

The light-hearted moment comes as the actors prepare to face off in the highly anticipated Marvel film, which is scheduled to arrive in cinemas on December 18.

Downey’s return to the MCU marks a major change for the actor, who previously played Tony Stark, also known as Iron Man, across multiple Marvel films before his character’s death in Avengers: Endgame.

Pascal will make his MCU debut as Reed Richards, the leader of the Fantastic Four, following the team’s introduction in The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

The costume swap offers a playful nod to the rivalry between their characters in Avengers: Doomsday, where Doctor Doom is set to face heroes from three distinct universes.

The upcoming film is directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, who previously helmed Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame.

The ensemble cast includes Chris Hemsworth, Chris Evans, Anthony Mackie, Paul Rudd, Florence Pugh, Vanessa Kirby, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Wyatt Russell, Channing Tatum, Simu Liu, Ian McKellen, Tom Hiddleston, James Marsden, Patrick Stewart, Sebastian Stan, David Harbour, Letitia Wright, Lewis Pullman, Kelsey Grammer, Kathryn Newton, Danny Ramirez, Winston Duke, Alan Cumming, Hannah John-Kamen, Rebecca Romijn and Joseph Quinn.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled to open in cinemas on December 18, 2026.

headline: Israeli Democrats leader warns Netanyahu could use new attack on Iran to stay in power
description: Yair Golan says Netanyahu 'lacks moral legitimacy' to manage another conflict, calls for formation of alternative govt
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan warned Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could exploit a potential new military attack on Iran to remain in power amid political uncertainty following last week's elections.

"The likelihood of another round of fighting with Iran is growing," Golan wrote on United States social media platform X. "We have reached a point of repeated rounds of fighting with Iran, and this shows just how much Netanyahu has failed," he added.

His remarks came amid Israeli and US media reports suggesting that Israel and Washington could launch another attack on Iran after the US midterm elections scheduled for Tuesday, November 3.

Golan said Netanyahu "lacks the moral legitimacy, and even the basic capacity" to manage another conflict with Iran.

He called for the formation of an alternative government, warning that Israel's security could be endangered under Netanyahu's leadership. Golan said forming a new government as soon as possible was "of utmost importance, as Israel's security and the safety of its citizens are at stake."

The warning came after neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition parties secured enough seats to form a government in last Tuesday's parliamentary elections.

Preliminary results showed Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Jewish opposition parties and 19 for Palestinian parties. The results left all blocs short of the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

The inconclusive election results have raised several possible scenarios, including a government backed by Palestinian parties, a unity government or another election.

Netanyahu faces corruption trial, ICC warrants

Netanyahu, 76, faces an ongoing corruption trial involving charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, which could result in imprisonment if he is convicted.

He has also been wanted by the International Criminal Court since 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians during Israel's war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

headline: Tim Seifert powers New Zealand victory
description: Hosts win final T20I as India clinch series 3-2
author: AFP
article_text:
Tim Seifert narrowly missed a maiden international century but did enough to steer New Zealand to a seven-wicket win over India in the fifth and final T20 on Sunday. Opener Seifert found some form with the bat, blasting 93 off 50 balls as the home side eased to 195-3 off 18 overs, after Adam Milne had earlier taken 4-19 to restrict the target to 192. The result wasn't enough for New Zealand to salvage the series, which the tourists won 3-2 after winning the first three games. Seifert scored just 36 runs across the first four matches but the big-hitting right-hander found his touch at Seddon Park, swinging the game in New Zealand's favour by blasting 11 fours and five sixes. However, he looked devastated when he played on to Nitish Kumar Reddy in the 16th over, having posted an 18th half-century but failing once again to reach three figures. Glenn Phillips finished on 65 not out to complete an exceptional series with the bat, which included 107 when New Zealand won game four in Auckland on Friday. Phillips's 341 runs across the five games was the most scored by any batsman in a bilateral T20 series. The previous record was held by England's Phil Salt, who scored 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023. Earlier, Milne's pace proved hard to handle as India were restricted to 191-8, boosted by rapid half-centuries to Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer. The pair combined for 93 off 7.1 overs for the third wicket after both openers fell cheaply to Milne, before Kishan departed for 61 and Iyer for 50. The teams will next contest a five-match one-day international series, starting in Auckland on Wednesday, before playing two Tests.

Sports Desk added:

New Zealand’s captain Mitchell Santner said it was a very tight series. “It was a very tight series. It's a very good team. Those small moments like you said in the first couple games where, we probably could have won those games or should have. So the series could have looked a lot different. But in terms of a cricketing point of view, there's a lot of good stuff,” Santner said. “The batting was really well, and then the bowling. Guys adapted brilliantly the last couple games. There's a lot of positives. Obviously, the scoreline shows 3-2 to India, but could have been the other way around. Bowlers mixing the lengths Yeah, I thought we mixed it up really nicely. Yorker's wide, a little bit straight with length,” Santner said. India’s skipper Shreyaz Iyer said it was plausible, honestly. “We could have been better, considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I recreated the momentum. And then from there on, we lost back-to-back wickets, and then suddenly pressure on the new batsmen,” he said. “It wasn't an easy wicket to play on, especially when the ball was seeming and holding a bit, and also skidding through at times. You must have seen a couple of time, myself and Tilak we got out in a similar fashion. It was challenging, especially of that hard length, but to get to 194, it was reasonable, I feel. I think we still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. We were a bit sloppy, but great learning,” he said.

headline: PIA welcomes its first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner in Islamabad
description: The aircraft arrived on flight PK-786 from London Heathrow Airport
author: Aftab Khan
article_text:
Pakistan International Airlines’ (PIA) first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner arrived in Islamabad from London on Sunday, marking a new development in the national carrier’s efforts to modernise its fleet and expand international operations.

The aircraft arrived on flight PK-786 from London Heathrow Airport. It was leased from Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic Airways under an Aircraft, Crew, Maintenance and Insurance (ACMI) agreement, commonly known as a wet lease. Under the arrangement, Norse Atlantic will provide the aircraft and its crew, while also remaining responsible for maintenance and insurance.

The aircraft was welcomed at Islamabad International Airport by PIA Chief Executive Officer Air Vice Marshal Amir Hayat and his team.

Reacting to its arrival, Aircraft Owners and Operators Association (AOOA) Pakistan said the induction of the Dreamliner was an important milestone for PIA and a significant step towards the airline’s revival.

In a statement, the organisation said the aircraft would strengthen PIA’s international operations and play an important role in improving air connectivity between Pakistan and the United Kingdom. It added that the new aircraft would provide overseas Pakistanis with better travel facilities.

AOOA also stressed that acquiring modern aircraft alone would not be enough to restore the airline’s standing, saying improvements in service standards were essential to its revival.

It said punctual flights and quality facilities should be among PIA’s priorities, adding that the airline needed to regain passengers’ confidence through a modern booking system and better customer service. Improvements in services, it said, should accompany the airline’s rebranding.

The organisation congratulated the new chief executive officer on the Dreamliner’s arrival and praised the efforts of the outgoing CEO and his team.

It expressed hope that the new leadership would take forward the airline’s revival, saying modern aircraft and staff training were essential for its growth.

Financial discipline and profitable routes were also key to PIA’s success, it added.

“The arrival of the Dreamliner marks a new beginning; the real goal is to restore PIA to its former glory,” AOOA Pakistan said.

In June, the Arif Habib Consortium formally took over the airline’s management through PIA Equity Ltd, following the completion of the privatisation process. The transaction involved a total investment commitment of Rs180 billion, including Rs125 billion in fresh capital for the airline and Rs55 billion payable to the government.

The new management had identified fleet renewal, route expansion and improvements in services as key areas for investment.

Earlier in October, PIA signed an agreement with Norway-based Norse Atlantic Airways for two Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners under an ACMI arrangement. The arrangement was intended to increase PIA’s long-haul capacity and support its expansion on UK routes.

PIA had also resumed direct flights to London in March after a gap of six years, initially operating three weekly flights from Islamabad and one from Lahore. The resumption increased the airline’s weekly flights to the United Kingdom to seven.

headline: 'Nobody Wants This' star Tovah Feldshuh addresses cast tensions over Adam Brody’s Palestine comments
description: The discussion comes as 'Nobody Wants This', created by Erin Foster, continues with its third season on Netflix
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Nobody Wants This actress Tovah Feldshuh has addressed reports of disagreements among the Netflix series' cast following Adam Brody's public comments on the Israeli genocide in Palestine.

Feldshuh, 77, took to Threads on Friday, 30 October, to reject suggestions that tensions were escalating between cast members.

“Tensions are NOT RISING. Profound differences of opinion are,” she wrote. “Please do not conflate the two — And none of it will be brought to the set.”

She added, “I deeply enjoy filming NWT and hope we are chosen to go on for a fourth season.”

Her comments followed an interview in which Brody, who portrays Rabbi Noah Roklov, shared his views on the violence in Gaza.

Speaking to GQ, the actor said: “I have spoken a lot about it privately. I haven’t spoken much about it publicly.”

He continued: “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”

Feldshuh, who plays Brody's on-screen mother, Bina, expressed a different perspective during an interview with the New York Post.

“To accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild,” she said. “It’s right out of Hitler’s playbook. You take the victim and you make the victim the perpetrator.”

Despite their differing views, Feldshuh emphasised her commitment to maintaining a professional working environment, stating,“My job, as Bina but also as Tovah, is to love the people on set at my place of work, to be kind.”

The discussion comes as Nobody Wants This, created by Erin Foster, continues with its third season on Netflix.

The romantic comedy follows Rabbi Noah and Joanne, played by Kristen Bell, as they navigate a relationship across religious and cultural differences.

headline: Guy Ritchie’s $500m Sherlock Holmes hit breaks into Apple TV’s global top 10, 17 years after release
description: The show stars Robert Downey Jr. as Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s iconic crime-solver, with Jude Law playing Dr John Watson
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Guy Ritchie’s Sherlock Holmes is enjoying a fresh wave of popularity, securing a place among the ten most-watched films on Apple TV worldwide.

Released in 2009, the detective adventure stars Robert Downey Jr. as Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s legendary crime-solver, with Jude Law playing his trusted companion, Dr John Watson.

The film reimagines the classic literary character through Ritchie’s distinctive action-driven style, combining mystery, elaborate investigations and fast-paced sequences.

The film’s continued streaming success is particularly notable given its age.

It earned approximately $524 million worldwide against a reported production budget of $90 million, making it one of the biggest box-office performers of 2009.

Its commercial success also led to a sequel, Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows, which maintained the franchise’s popularity.

Ritchie has recently enjoyed renewed attention across streaming platforms. The second season of The Gentlemen has helped keep the filmmaker in the spotlight, while MobLand has also attracted viewers with its latest episodes.

Both series have strengthened his presence in television, but the performance of Sherlock Holmes demonstrates that his earlier film work continues to find new audiences.

The director is also preparing another collaboration with Jason Statham. The pair are reuniting for Viva La Madness, an upcoming action thriller based on JJ Connolly’s 2011 novel and connected to the world of Layer Cake.

Its cast includes Vinnie Jones, Jason Isaacs and Ben Foster.

With Sherlock Holmes now ranking among Apple TV’s global top ten most-watched films, Ritchie’s influence on streaming remains strong across both new productions and established favourites.

headline: Harry Styles receives banner from Jalen Brunson at the end of 30-night Madison Square Garden residency
description: The New York Knicks point guard presented the singer with the commemorative banner during the final show
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Harry Styles has received a special 30-night banner at Madison Square Garden after bringing his record-breaking Together, Together residency to a close on October 31.

New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson presented the singer with the commemorative banner during the final show, celebrating his consecutive run of 30 performances at the iconic New York venue.

The pair shared a hug as the audience cheered, with Brunson wearing a “Techno Is My Boyfriend” hat previously associated with Styles.

The presentation took place during the second night of Styles’ Halloween performances, known as Harryween.

The singer marked the occasion by dressing as a New York City rat and performing “Psycho Killer” by Talking Heads.

The previous evening, Styles had worn an Elvis costume before changing into the outfit from his X Factor audition.

He also performed Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely”, the same song he sang during his original audition.

This is not the first time Styles has been honoured at Madison Square Garden. In 2022, he completed a 15-night residency at the venue and received a commemorative banner during his final performance.

Reflecting on that recognition, he told the audience: “Any time that you come to Madison Square Garden and you see that, remember it’s because of you. That is ours.”

The Together, Together tour also included performances in Amsterdam, London, Brazil and Mexico City before its New York finale.

Throughout the run, its central theme celebrated music’s ability to bring people together and create lasting human connections.

headline: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in India's Manipur state
description: Killings come amid mass protests demanding abrogation of ceasefire arrangement between Kuki armed groups, Indian state
author: Reuters
article_text:
Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India's northeastern state of Manipur, police said on Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in the conflict-hit region.

Three men from the Kuki tribal group were killed in an exchange of gunfire between "unidentified armed miscreants" in the state's Noney district on Saturday, according to a police statement.

The bodies of two other men from the same community, who had gone missing earlier this week, were recovered in Kangpokpi district on Sunday morning after security personnel launched a search operation, a second police statement said.

A top Kuki tribal body blamed Naga separatist outfits for the killings, describing them as a "direct unprovoked assault . . . in their homeland."

The killings came amid mass protests attended by hundreds of thousands of people in the state capital Imphal and other areas, demanding the abrogation of a ceasefire arrangement between Kuki armed groups and the Indian state.

The predominantly Christian Kuki and Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state.

The latest fighting erupted after a Naga man was allegedly assaulted by men from the Kuki community in February this year.

The killing of three Kuki pastors in May, allegedly by Naga armed groups, triggered a series of retaliatory abductions and killings by both sides.

The latest Kuki-Naga clashes have added to tensions in Manipur, where the Kuki community is also embroiled in a bloody ethnic conflict with the mainly Hindu Meitei community that began in May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas.

More than 60,000 people displaced by the conflict, which has claimed more than 300 lives, continue to live in temporary shelters.

headline: Xiaomi's October EV deliveries top 50,000, hit 2026 monthly high
description: Chinese EV sales surged in October, with BYD up 11% and Leapmotor setting a delivery record.
author: Reuters
article_text:
Chinese EV sales surged in October, with BYD up 11% and Leapmotor setting a delivery record.

Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi ​said on Sunday it ‌delivered more than 50,000 electric vehicles ​in October, the ​highest monthly total this ⁠year, as it ​ramps up production ​to meet its 2026 target.

Deliveries reached about 336,000 vehicles ​for the ​first 10 months after topping ‌30,000 ⁠units in August and 40,000 in September.

The company aims ​to deliver ​550,000 ⁠vehicles in 2026. Its January-October ​deliveries represent ​about ⁠61% of that goal.

According to cnevpost website, other Chinese websites show significant increase in EV sales. Xpeng also sold vehicles in Octo 2-26.ber 2026 which is 19 percent high as compared to previous year sales. surpassing 42,013 vehicles in October last year.

Leapmotor delivered more than 100,000 vehicles for the fourth consecutive month, setting a new record. BYD sold 490,168 NEVs which is up 10.97% year-on-year and 5.74% from September

headline: Chad Lowe lists $3.25 million Los Angeles home after 13-year-old daughter Fiona's death
description: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter have reportedly accepted an offer for their LA home following their daughter’s death
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Actor Chad Lowe and his wife, Kim Painter, have reportedly agreed to sell their Los Angeles home for $3.249 million, weeks after the death of their 13-year-old daughter, Fiona.

The couple’s 3,239-square-foot property in the Mar Vista neighbourhood was listed on October 16, according to TMZ, which cited real estate records.

The four-bedroom, three-bathroom home features vaulted ceilings and Spanish-style architecture. Lowe and Painter purchased it in March 2025 for $3.15 million.

TMZ reported that the couple accepted an offer of $3.249 million, although the deal remains “contingent on certain conditions being met”.

Fiona died on 29 September 29. The medical examiner’s office confirmed her death by suicide, as reported by People. She was the second of Lowe and Painter’s three daughters, alongside Mabel, 17, and Nixie, 10.

The family announced the loss in a statement shared with People, describing Fiona as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance”.

“She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents,” they added. “In fact, she was the light of our lives.”

The family also requested privacy as they grieved and encouraged anyone experiencing mental health difficulties to contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

The reported property sale follows another major loss for the family. Their previous home was destroyed in the Pacific Palisades Fire in early 2025.

In February that year, Lowe shared photographs of his daughters returning to see the remains of their home, praising their “spirit and resilience” as they faced the aftermath.

headline: Taika Waititi criticises film reviewers after 'Klara and the Sun' receives a 26% Rotten Tomatoes score
description: The filmmaker addressed the criticism online, describing some critics as 'out of touch', 'obsolete' and 'irrelevant'
author: Pop Culture, Art
article_text:
Taika Waititi has criticised film reviewers following the poor reception of his latest film, Klara and the Sun, which has received a 26% score on Rotten Tomatoes from 90 reviews.

The 51-year-old filmmaker addressed the criticism in an Instagram post on Friday, October 30, describing some critics as “out of touch”, “obsolete” and “irrelevant”.

“I haven’t read a review of anything aimed at me or my peers in almost 15 years,” he wrote. “But I do listen to the people. So this Halloween, let’s spare a thought for those sad lost souls who couldn’t achieve their dreams of becoming artists, and thus became critics.”

Waititi continued his criticism by referring to his 2019 film Jojo Rabbit, which also received negative reviews from some critics.

“The same people who also hated Jojo Rabbit. Irrelevant. Out of touch Obsolete. In the bin,” he added.

The comments come as Klara and the Sun faces challenges at the box office.

According to TheWrap, Sony Pictures is reportedly scaling back the film’s international release plans after it earned just $1.067 million domestically.

Based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2021 novel, the dystopian science-fiction drama follows Klara, an artificial robot companion played by Jenna Ortega.

Purchased to keep young Josie, portrayed by Mia Tharia, company, Klara develops a close bond with the girl as she tries to understand human emotions and the world around her.

Amy Adams plays Josie’s mother, while the supporting cast includes Aran Murphy, Steve Buscemi and Natasha Lyonne.

Despite the disappointing critical response and box-office performance, Waititi has publicly defended the film and challenged the relevance of its reviewers.

headline: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as drones damage Russian facility
description: Russia says 235 Ukrainian drones downed overnight, Kyiv says 371 of 433 Russian long-range drones shot down
author: Reuters
article_text:
Russian strikes left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, while Russian authorities reported major damage to an industrial site following Ukrainian drone attacks on Nizhny Novgorod region.

Even as a six-day local ceasefire held on its final day around the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, there was no letup in fighting elsewhere along the front line and both sides kept up long-range air attacks.

Zelenskiy said Russia had hit power infrastructure in four Ukrainian regions overnight, cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of households. "The intensity of the strikes is very high, and the Russians are seeking to maximally exploit the deficit of ballistic missile interceptors," he said on Telegram.

He said Ukraine, meanwhile, had hit the Kamensky plant in Russia's Rostov region, which he said was involved in the manufacture of Russian missiles. Moscow did not comment on the reported attack in Rostov.

In Nizhny Novgorod region, however, Governor Gleb Nikitin said a large-scale overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused "significant damage" to an industrial facility. He did not identify the site that was hit. The region is home to the NORSI oil refinery, one of Russia's largest.

Overall, Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had downed 235 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. Ukraine's air force said it had shot down 371 of 433 long-range drones launched by Russia since Saturday evening.

In its morning update, the air force said dozens of Russian drones were still in the air as of Sunday morning. Six separate drone alerts had been issued in Kyiv since midnight.

Fuel supplies

Nizhny Novgorod's regional government also did not identify the facility that was struck, but it said it was taking steps to ensure gas stations were supplied with fuel, urging motorists to "buy fuel only as needed and avoid panic buying," Interfax reported.

The warning suggests the damaged facility was linked to the region's oil-refining or fuel-supply infrastructure. Kyiv did not immediately claim responsibility for the Nizhny Novgorod attack.

On Friday, Russia said Ukraine had resumed strikes on its oil refineries and accused Kyiv of ignoring a request from US President Donald Trump to stop such attacks, which Trump has blamed for raising the cost of diesel before US midterm elections next week.

Ukraine says it supports a full ceasefire on energy targets, including its own battered power grid, but that Moscow is unwilling to agree to this.

In an interview with state TV channel Vesti on Sunday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, who oversees the energy sector, did not mention the Nizhny Novgorod strike, but said Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries were adding to global fuel market imbalances and affecting prices.

headline: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza - medics say
description: Hamas denies it is trying to carry out attacks and rebuild arsenal, accuses Israel of undermining Gaza peace deal
author: Reuters
article_text:
Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on ​Sunday, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.

Medics said ‌three people were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City. The interior ministry said the five police officers were killed in another strike in western ​Khan Younis, in the south of the enclave.

The Israeli military ​said it struck several militants in Khan Younis, without giving ⁠further information. It did not immediately comment on the Gaza ​City strike.

Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and ​launching attacks in violation of a year-old ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.

Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild ​its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.

Last ​year's US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress ‌has ⁠been made as negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel to withdraw its troops, who control about two-thirds of the territory where they have ordered residents out.

Nearly all of the ​more than 2 ​million residents live ⁠in the remaining third of the enclave among war ruins, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, ​still under effective control of Hamas.

At least 1,500 Palestinians ​have ⁠been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four soldiers have been killed.

Palestinian ⁠authorities ​say more than 74,000 people have been ​killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in ​southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

headline: Lawson relegates to Mexico GP back row
description: Technical breach wipes out qualifying effort after ninth-place finish
author: AFP
article_text:
Liam Lawson will start Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix from the back of the grid after his strong performance in Saturday's qualifying was erased for technical reasons. The Racing Bulls driver had qualified a promising ninth ahead of team-mate Arvid Lindblad in a thrilling session topped by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton in a Ferrari. It was a record-extending 105th pole position for the Briton and his first for the Italian team. The luckless Lawson, who is fighting to keep his seat for 2027, had his laps deleted after an inspection revealed his power unit's output fell outside the regulations. The infringement was noted as the 24-year-old crossed the line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2 when he had exhausted his battery energy. The regulations require electrical power to decline at a controlled and progressive rate, not abruptly. In a statement, the race stewards said Lawson "did not lift off the power immediately" as expected. His demotion on the grid comes on the back of a tangle with four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull during Friday's practice, resulting in both drivers receiving a one-place grid penalty. Lawson apologised to Verstappen, who will start from fifth, on Saturday morning after another incident-filled session in which he claimed his bid for pole was thwarted by outgoing world champion Lando Norris's McLaren. He said Norris was running slowly on the racing line and ruined his lap as he locked up and lost time. "When I saw his car on the right, I couldn't believe my eyes," said Verstappen.

"I was fighting for pole."

Verstappen also spoke out to support his team-mate Isack Hadjar after the Frenchman had been officially reprimanded for pushing aside an aggressive fan demanding a selfie with him in the chaotic paddock on Friday. "I understand his reaction," said the Dutchman. "It's incredibly irritating when people just touch you without asking... I've never pushed anyone away, but there have been times when I came close. "I've compared the paddock to a zoo before -- and this is the situation you get when you let so many people in." Hadjar was relieved to receive a warning and not a more severe punishment. "It makes sense and I'm glad they made the right decision," he said. "Fair play. I'm going to work. It's not a reality show and I am going into the garage."

headline: Alibaba partners with Apple to integrate Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence for Chinese market
description: Alibaba's feature enters iOS developer beta on Nov. 4, ahead of its December iOS 27.3 launch
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Alibaba's feature enters iOS developer beta on Nov. 4, ahead of its December iOS 27.3 launch

Chinese tech company Alibaba Group has partnered with Apple to integrate its Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence for the Chinese market, state-run Xinhua news agency reported Saturday.

The feature will be available for testing in the latest iOS developer beta starting Nov. 4 and will launch with the official iOS 27.3 release in December, Alibaba said.

Qwen’s AI capabilities will be integrated into several Apple features, including Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence.

Users can choose whether to enable the integration and what information to share. Alibaba said user requests and generated responses would not be used to train its AI models.

The feature will be available on compatible iPhones whose device location and Apple Account region are both set to China.

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the partnership would bring new AI-powered services to Chinese users.

Wang Xiaojie, an AI expert at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said this marked the first time a major global consumer hardware maker had adopted a Chinese large language model as its primary system-level AI backbone in the Chinese market.
